The only machine-readable interface it exposes is the WordPress core REST content API behind hydrostor.ca, which is anonymously readable, read-only without credentials, and carries the project portfolio, the newsroom archive and the media library. That surface is profiled here for discovery purposes and is described from the site's own self-describing route index.

providers.name: Matthews International
providers.description: Matthews International Corporation (NASDAQ: MATW) is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania diversified manufacturer founded in 1850 and reporting in three segments. Memorialization covers bronze and granite memorials, caskets, cremation-related products and cremation and incineration equipment for the cemetery and funeral home industries, sold through Matthews Aurora Funeral Solutions and Matthews Environmental Solutions. Industrial Technologies covers product identification — the Matthews Marking Systems marking and coding business and its MPERIA controller platform — plus the design, manufacture and service of custom energy storage solutions including dry-battery-electrode coating and converting lines. Brand Solutions is now a 40% ownership interest in Propelis Group, the entity formed on 1 May 2025 when Matthews contributed the majority of its SGK brand business; the company sold its warehouse automation business (Matthews Automation Solutions — Pyramid, Compass and Lightning Pick) to Duravant on 31 December 2025. Matthews is a manufacturer rather than a software vendor: it operates no public developer program and publishes no API documentation, SDK, package, CLI, MCP server, agent card or machine-readable specification. The MPERIA controller sold with its marking and coding equipment markets a "common API" for ERP, WMS, MES and PLC integration, but that is an on-premises XML or command-line protocol carried over Ethernet or RS-232 and documented only in sales collateral — not a public web API.

providers.name: Peaxy
providers.description: Peaxy, Inc. is a San Jose, California industrial AI and digital-twin software company founded in 2012, with offices in Stockholm, Sweden and Cagliari, Italy. Its Peaxy Lifecycle Intelligence (PLI) platform threads design, test, manufacturing, field and service data for mission-critical physical assets into a single cloud-based source of truth, then applies machine learning to predict failures, extend asset life and support warranty, quality and readiness decisions. Product lines cover battery and energy-storage analytics (R&D through manufacturing, deployment and second life), defense readiness and predictive maintenance for the U.S. Department of Defense and Department of Energy, critical infrastructure and airport/circuit-level AI, a battery LIMS, and EcoGrid for renewable energy communities. Peaxy markets "a range of open APIs" for platform integration, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract — access runs through a demo request and a customer engagement. The platform is SOC 2 Type II certified and aligned to NIST 800-171.

providers.name: HAMAMA
providers.description: Hamama is a West Sacramento, California consumer-products company that makes it easy to grow fresh microgreens at home. Founded by two MIT-trained mechanical engineers, Hamama sells self-watering microgreen grow kits and its signature pre-seeded "Seed Quilts" (non-GMO, mostly Certified Organic) that sprout edible greens in 7-10 days with nothing more than a single addition of water, no soil, pesticides, or fertilizer required. The company sells grow kits, ceramic trays, Seed Quilt refills, green-onion and mushroom kits, and accessories directly to consumers through its Shopify storefront, offers flexible subscribe-and-save refill plans, and supports growers with Growing Guides, recipes, a rewards program, and a Grow Coach customer-support team.

providers.name: Reservoir
providers.description: Reservoir makes home electrification easy, affordable, and awesome, starting with hot water—the fastest way to make the biggest impact. It offers solutions to save power and savor showers, aiming to accelerate the transition to clean energy in households.

providers.name: Bobw
providers.description: Bob W is a hospitality brand offering short‑stay, fully equipped apartments across Europe. It combines hotel‑level service with local design, sustainable practices and tech‑enabled check‑in. The company offsets all guest emissions, sources local furniture, and aims for net‑zero hospitality by 2050. With over 60 properties in 21+ cities, Bob W delivers flexible stays for business and leisure travelers, emphasizing sustainability and community integration.

providers.name: Tetra Tech
providers.description: Tetra Tech is an American consulting and engineering services firm headquartered in Pasadena, California. Founded in 1966, it provides consulting, engineering, program management, and construction management services across water, environment, infrastructure, resource management, energy, and international development. With 30,000 employees across 550 offices worldwide, Tetra Tech delivers data-driven digital solutions under the Tetra Tech Delta brand, encompassing advanced data analytics, artificial intelligence, process automation, and cloud integration. Key digital offerings include the Cosmos mobile data collection platform, WaterNet SaaS for water network management, and environmental data management tools. The company's GitHub organization (tetratech) hosts open-source environmental and water quality analysis tools.

providers.name: University of Maryland Dept. of Geographical Sciences
providers.description: The University of Maryland Department of Geographical Sciences focuses on research, education, and outreach in geography, GIS, remote sensing, and spatial analysis. It offers undergraduate and graduate programs, conducts interdisciplinary research on environmental change, land use, and geospatial technologies, and provides resources and collaborations for students, scholars, and partners.

providers.name: Build
providers.description: Build is an AI-native operating partner for the built world, pairing autonomous AI agents (its "Dougie" platform) with deep domain expertise to accelerate commercial real estate and infrastructure development. The platform automates mission-critical development workflows including site selection, due diligence, underwriting, investment-committee memos, test-fit analysis, market and zoning research, environmental diligence, and ESG reporting. Build serves institutional clients across data centers, industrials, energy, power, office, telecommunications, mixed-use, hotels, and multifamily. Backed by Index Ventures; profiled in the API Evangelist network. Build is a services company and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Impossible Metals
providers.description: Impossible Metals is a deep-ocean robotics and critical-minerals company founded in 2020 by CEO Oliver Gunasekara, headquartered in San Jose, California with a robotics lab in Canada, and a member of Y Combinator's W22 cohort. It builds the Eureka autonomous underwater vehicle, a hovering AUV that uses computer vision and robotic arms to pick polymetallic nodules from the seabed one at a time — leaving visible fauna and the sediment layer in place — as an alternative to the dredge-and-riser designs used elsewhere in deep-sea mining. Eureka I and Eureka II have been sea-tested, Eureka III is slated for a 2026 test in the BGR contract area of the Clarion-Clipperton Zone, and the company has applied for a deep-sea mining lease in U.S. federal waters and for observer status with the International Seabed Authority. It is a certified B Corp and publishes environmental data, policy positions and testimony alongside its technical work. Impossible Metals is a robotics and mining company rather than a software vendor: it operates no developer program, publishes no product API, SDKs or developer portal, and hosts no api. or developer. subdomain. The only machine-readable interfaces it serves are the WordPress REST content API behind impossiblemetals.com and the two OpenAPI documents its events plugin publishes on that same host, which are captured here for discovery purposes and are anonymously readable and read-only.

providers.name: Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC)
providers.description: The Open Geospatial Consortium is the standards body for geospatial interoperability — a member-funded consortium founded in 1994 and headquartered in the United States, with 362 member organizations plus 159 individual members across government, commercial, academic and non-profit sectors. OGC wrote the web-mapping layer the public sector has run on for two decades — WMS, WFS, WCS, WMTS and CSW, the OWS suite — and is now replacing it with the OGC API family: a set of resource-oriented, OpenAPI-described standards sharing a common core, of which eleven are approved (Features, Common, EDR, Tiles, Processes, Maps, Moving Features, Records, Connected Systems, DGGS and SensorThings) and seven more are in draft. Its API posture is genuinely open where it counts and closed where most standards bodies are: every adopted standard is a free download, the schemas and OpenAPI documents are served anonymously from schemas.opengis.net, and drafting happens in public on GitHub across 361 repositories — while portal.ogc.org, where Technical Committee documents, votes and delegate rosters live, returns HTTP 401 to the public. OGC runs a compliance and certification programme (CITE) and publishes its active member roster as a CSV, which is unusual and makes the coalition measurable. The distinction this repo keeps is that OGC publishes SPECIFICATIONS, not services: the contracts here have templated servers and describe what a conformant implementation must offer, so they must never be read as a callable API.

providers.name: Saildrone
providers.description: Saildrone is an Alameda, California maritime autonomy company that designs, manufactures, and operates a global fleet of wind/solar-powered autonomous surface vehicles (USVs) for ocean science, maritime domain awareness, and defense applications. Founded in 2012 by Richard Jenkins, the company runs four USV classes — Explorer (23ft, environmental sensing), Voyager (33ft, MDA and counter-narcotics), Surveyor (65ft, deep-ocean bathymetric mapping), and the newer Spectre (ISR / anti-submarine warfare / kinetic payloads). Saildrone has logged over 2.5M nautical miles and 65,000 days at sea across customers including NOAA PMEL, NOAA SWFSC, the US Navy (Task Force 59), NASA, EUMETSAT, BOEM, and Lockheed Martin (which invested $50M in October 2025). Saildrone delivers data through two product surfaces — the Saildrone Mission Portal (secure web app for tasking and live multi-INT visualization) and the Saildrone Public Mission API (BETA) at developer-mission.saildrone.com, which exposes key/secret authenticated endpoints for health, drone access discovery, and time-series retrieval across vehicle, atmospheric, oceanographic, and biogeochemical datasets. Open ocean data from past missions is published via NOAA PMEL ERDDAP and NCEI under open-data terms.

providers.name: Complir
providers.description: Complir is the AI infrastructure for product compliance, described by the company as "Vanta for physical products." Its AI agents map product data, analyse compliance risks, generate audit-ready documentation, and track regulatory changes across every market a brand sells in - covering GPSR, ESPR, EPR, REACH, RoHS, PPWR, EUDR, CE/UKCA marking, Digital Product Passports and 100+ other frameworks across 40+ markets. The platform maps each SKU to its regulatory requirements, produces translations, labels, warnings, declarations of conformity and technical files, verifies marketing claims, and offers native Adobe Illustrator/InDesign plugins plus a natural language interface for querying compliance data. Founded in 2024 (Gustav Bang, Marc Kaa Brejner, Tine Kuhnel) and part of Y Combinator's Spring 2026 batch, Complir monitors 100,000+ products for international retailers including Flying Tiger Copenhagen, Konges Sloejd, Matas and COOP.

providers.name: Ecorobotix
providers.description: Ecorobotix SA is a Swiss agricultural technology company founded in 2011 and headquartered in Yverdon-les-Bains, Switzerland, building AI-driven ultra-high-precision (UHP) crop-care equipment. Its flagship ARA smart sprayer combines Plant-by-Plant AI detection with UHP-Spray-Technology to scan a field, classify crops versus weeds in under 250 milliseconds, and place treatment on a roughly six-by-six centimetre target, cutting herbicide and plant-protection input volumes by up to 95 percent compared with broadcast spraying. The product family spans the ARA620 and ARA595 UHP sprayers for row and vegetable crops, the ALBA UHP sprayer for turf, and a library of crop-specific algorithms for broccoli, carrots, onions and chicory. More than 1,000 ARA units have been deployed across Europe, the United Kingdom, North America, South America and Australia/New Zealand. Machine telemetry, treatment maps and fleet data are delivered to customers through the Ecorobotix cloud portal, which is backed by an authenticated REST API; that API is not offered as a public developer program.

providers.name: First Solar
providers.description: First Solar, Inc. (NASDAQ: FSLR) is the largest American manufacturer of solar modules and the leading producer of thin-film cadmium telluride (CdTe) photovoltaic technology, an alternative to conventional crystalline silicon. It designs and manufactures Series 6 and Series 7 modules at vertically integrated factories in Ohio, Alabama, Louisiana, India, Malaysia and Vietnam, and supports utility-scale PV projects with energy prediction, plant design and post-sales technical services. First Solar publishes no public API, developer program or machine-readable contract. Its "Developer Portal" is a Salesforce Experience Cloud site for solar project developers and EPC partners, not software developers, and requires a login. PlantPredict, the energy-modelling API and Python SDK First Solar built, was acquired by Terabase Energy in October 2021 and is catalogued against Terabase.

providers.name: 3Bar Biologics
providers.description: 3Bar Biologics (3BarBio) is an agricultural biotechnology company in Columbus, Ohio, spun out of research at The Ohio State University and operating as the first contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) dedicated to agricultural biologicals. Its business is getting living microbes to the field alive: the patented LiveMicrobe platform, including the Iso-Pak and Re-Pak delivery systems, keeps beneficial bacteria viable through storage and distribution, the problem that has historically limited adoption of microbial crop inputs. The company sells design, development, biomanufacturing and fulfillment services to discovery companies, distributors and bulk suppliers, and previously marketed its own Bio-YIELD inoculant to corn, soybean and wheat growers in the eastern Corn Belt. 3Bar Biologics is a manufacturer and services business, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDKs and no pricing for any programmatic product. The only machine-readable interface it exposes is the WordPress REST content API behind its corporate website at www.3barbiologics.com, which is captured here for discovery purposes. That surface is anonymously readable, read-only, entirely undocumented by the company, and carries two reproducible defects on its media collection that are recorded in this profile.

providers.name: Bloomberg ESG Products
providers.description: Bloomberg ESG Products provide environmental, social, and governance data, analytics, and scores to help investors assess sustainability risks and opportunities. Bloomberg collects ESG data from thousands of companies globally, offering ESG scores, climate data, green bond data, and sustainable finance analytics through the Bloomberg Terminal and API.

providers.name: Bloomberg Sustainable Finance Products
providers.description: Bloomberg Sustainable Finance Products provide comprehensive data, analytics, and tools for sustainable investing, green bond markets, ESG integration, and climate risk assessment. Bloomberg serves as a key data provider for sustainable finance markets, offering green bond data, ESG scores, climate analytics, and impact measurement tools aligned with major regulatory frameworks including SFDR, EU Taxonomy, and TCFD.

providers.name: Cato Digital
providers.description: Cato Digital is a sustainable bare metal cloud provider that repurposes large-scale, second-life servers from hyperscalers like Meta and NVIDIA to deliver AI & GPU servers (up to 512GB VRAM), ephemeral application servers, and build-your-own storage arrays at 60-75% below major cloud providers. Led by CEO Dean Nelson, the company operates on a "use what we have before we build more" circular-economy principle, tapping underutilized data center capacity and clean energy, and is a founding member of the Infrastructure Masons Climate Accord. Customers provision and manage infrastructure through the Cato console rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: EcoSoul Home
providers.description: EcoSoul Home is a direct-to-consumer sustainable home-essentials brand selling compostable and eco-friendly tableware — plates, bowls, hot cups, cutlery, napkins, bagasse and areca-leaf products — plus everyday household goods made from renewable materials. The brand sells online through its Shopify storefront (and via major retail marketplaces) with the mission of replacing single-use plastic in the home. Backed by Accel, EcoSoul was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched from its public agent-native commerce surface: a published /llms.txt (agents.md) instruction file, Shopify Customer Accounts OpenID Connect for authentication, and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint that lets buyer-approved AI shopping agents search the catalog, build carts, and complete checkout via Shop Pay, Google Pay, or card.

providers.name: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF)
providers.description: The European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) is an intergovernmental organization that provides comprehensive numerical weather prediction services and climate data to its member states and the broader scientific community. Operating one of the world’s most powerful supercomputing facilities, ECMWF conducts cutting‑edge research in atmospheric science, data assimilation, and climate modelling, delivering high‑resolution forecasts, reanalysis datasets, and specialized products for sectors such as aviation, marine, and emergency management. Its open data initiatives and collaborative platforms support global efforts to understand and mitigate weather‑related risks.

providers.name: XGS Energy
providers.description: XGS Energy is a next-generation geothermal power developer founded in 2008 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, formerly Geothermic Solution. Its patented Thermal Reach Enhancement technology packs a thermally conductive material around a closed-loop wellbore so heat is drawn from the surrounding rock without relying on natural permeability or produced water, siting geothermal in geology conventional hydrothermal and EGS cannot use. It is developing a 150 MW round-the-clock project in New Mexico with Meta and utility PNM, and in 2025 acquired drilling firm Capuano Engineering. XGS Energy is an energy infrastructure developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, product API, SDKs or API documentation. The only machine-readable interface it exposes is the WordPress REST content API behind www.xgsenergy.com, captured here for discovery — anonymously readable, read-only, and undocumented by the company.

providers.name: Archive
providers.description: Archive is a brand-owned resale and recommerce technology platform, founded in 2021, that lets forward-thinking global brands launch and scale profitable, sustainable resale businesses. Its circularity platform spans branded recommerce storefronts, peer-to-peer marketplaces, trade-in (online and in-store), take-back, warranty and repair, a resale warehouse management system (WMS), a unified product catalog, a dynamic pricing engine, and analytics — reclaiming supply through returns, past-season inventory, consumer listings, and in-store trade-ins. Archive serves 50+ brands across 10+ countries, including The North Face, lululemon, Peloton, New Balance, Dr. Martens, Fjällräven, Oscar de la Renta, Hanna Andersson, and Faherty. The company is backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners (with Energize Capital leading its $30M Series B), and has raised $54M to date.

providers.name: SeekOps
providers.description: SeekOps Inc. is an Austin, Texas emissions-measurement company that detects and quantifies methane and carbon dioxide from industrial facilities using drone-mounted laser spectroscopy. Its SeekIR sensor suite applies tunable diode laser absorption spectroscopy (TDLAS) originally developed at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory to search for methane on Mars, hardened for terrestrial energy operations. SeekOps sells measurement as a service — Leak Detection and Quantification (LDAQ) surveys flown over upstream and midstream oil and gas sites, offshore platforms, landfills, biogas digesters and renewable natural gas facilities — and delivers the results through two software surfaces: Celsius, a cloud analytics and reconciliation-reporting dashboard, and FASTR, a real-time telemetry view. Founded in 2017, the company has surveyed facilities across six continents and is backed by Equinor Ventures and OGCI Climate Investments. Its software is customer-only: both Celsius and FASTR sit behind authentication and SeekOps publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Tem
providers.description: Tem (Tem-Energy Limited) is a UK-based energy technology company building AI-native transaction infrastructure for a modern energy market. Its RED platform is a modern utility that removes wholesale market markups to cut business electricity costs by up to 30%, provides transparent line-by-line billing from half-hourly meter data, and gives generators fairer earnings with renewable-energy traceability across 6,000+ sites. Backed by a February 2026 GBP 55M Series B led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. The customer-facing platform runs at app.tem.energy behind an OIDC login; the platform API at api.tem.energy is a private AWS API Gateway with no publicly documented developer surface at the time of profiling.

providers.name: Geolynx
providers.description: Geolynx is an Estonian geospatial technology company offering professional GIS solutions, custom ESG data services, web hosting for spatial data, and training. Leveraging long‑term experience in open‑source GIS, satellite data analysis, and advanced computational methods, Geolynx provides accurate environmental risk assessments, tailored ESG reporting, and robust spatial data infrastructure for public and authenticated access. The company serves clients such as Emajõe Waterworks and aims to support both beginners and advanced users through courses on QGIS, PostGIS, and GeoServer.

providers.name: helios
providers.description: helios is a French sustainable-banking company (HELIOS SAS, Paris) offering current, Premium, joint, youth, Liberté and independent/professional accounts, a green savings passbook, sustainable life insurance and wooden or recycled-plastic Visa cards through iOS, Android and web. It is a société à mission and a certified B Corp whose promise is that no customer euro finances fossil fuels or polluting industry, and it publishes the list of transition projects it funds. helios is registered in REGAFI under 731225 as a payment services agent of OKALI, the ACPR-approved electronic money institution that services the accounts. It publishes no public API, SDK, webhook or developer portal; the one machine-readable document it serves is an llms.txt AI-usage policy.

providers.name: Standard Industries
providers.description: Standard Industries is a privately-held global industrial company headquartered in New York City and tracing its origins to 1886. The company operates a portfolio of building solutions, performance materials, logistics, real estate, and investment businesses, with more than 20,000 employees and approximately $11 billion in annual revenues. Standard Building Solutions includes GAF (North America's largest roofing manufacturer), GAF Energy (Timberline Solar nailable solar shingles), BMI Group (Europe's largest pitched and flat roofing manufacturer, with brands including Braas, Monier, Icopal, Wolfin, and Redland), Siplast (specialty roofing and waterproofing for iconic structures), SGI (mining and mineral processing), Schiedel (flue, stove, and ventilation systems), and Standard Logistics. Performance Materials is anchored by W. R. Grace & Co., which produces catalysts, engineered materials, process technologies, and fine chemicals. Standard Investments deploys capital across public equities and early-to-growth venture investments. Winter Properties is a vertically integrated real estate firm with more than 100 years of history in New York City. Standard Industries does not publish a public developer API or developer portal at the corporate level; technology integration with customers and partners is handled inside the individual operating companies (most notably GAF and Grace).

providers.name: Vaisala
providers.description: Vaisala is a global leader in measurement instruments and intelligence, providing weather, climate and industrial solutions. With over 1 million sensors manufactured annually and a presence in 150+ countries, Vaisala delivers reliable data for climate action, aviation, energy and many other sectors, supporting customers worldwide with innovative technologies and services.

providers.name: Hula Earth
providers.description: Hula Earth is a Munich-based environmental technology company providing real-time biodiversity monitoring. It combines solar-powered, maintenance-free Hula BioT IoT sensors with AI-powered species detection, satellite-based Earth Observation, and the Hula Platform dashboard so organizations can monitor, manage, and report on biodiversity at landscape scale. Hula Earth serves renewables (solar and wind), agriculture, nature conservation, and urban development, turning environmental uncertainty into operational confidence and compliance-ready reporting.

providers.name: Indigo Agriculture
providers.description: Indigo Agriculture is a Boston-based agriculture-technology company combining microbial seed and foliar treatments (biotrinsic) and on-farm seed treatment hardware (CLIPS) with two large supply-chain programs: Carbon by Indigo, a soil-carbon program that pays growers for verified carbon credits using Indigo's proprietary measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) stack; and Source by Indigo, a Scope-3 program that connects consumer-goods buyers to sustainably grown crops with greenhouse-gas, water, and low-carbon-biofuel outcome reporting. Indigo does not publish a public developer portal; partner and supply-chain integrations are negotiated directly through their team.

providers.name: Noda
providers.description: Noda (formerly Infogrid) is an agentic AI platform for commercial real estate building operations. It functions as an always-on AI virtual building engineer that connects to a portfolio's building management systems (BMS), IoT, weather, and utility data, continuously detects faults and energy waste, identifies root causes, generates quantified savings recommendations, and executes authorized setpoint and load adjustments — tying every action to measured, audit-ready ROI. The platform processes 100M+ data points daily and reports 15-25% annual energy reduction across deployed assets. Trusted by owners and operators of 400M+ square feet including Hilton, JLL, CBRE, Macerich, Cousins, DivcoWest and Salesforce. ISO 27001 certified and hosted on AWS in the United States. Backed by Northzone. Noda exposes no public developer API; onboarding is enterprise/demo-based.

providers.name: CO2 AI
providers.description: CO2 AI is an enterprise sustainability platform that helps organizations measure, reduce, and report carbon emissions across their entire value chain. It combines trustworthy emissions data, AI-powered workflows, and supply-chain collaboration to baseline and track Scope 1, 2, and 3 corporate footprints, compute audit-ready product carbon footprints (PCF) at scale across thousands of SKUs (PACT, TfS, PEF, ISO aligned), engage suppliers for primary data, and build decarbonization plans ranked by Marginal Abatement Cost. Backed by Partech and surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a climate-sector company profile. No public developer API is published as of this enrichment pass; the profile captures the company's security, trust, and legal surface.

providers.name: Diligent
providers.description: Diligent Corporation is a governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) software company best known for its board management portal (Diligent Boards / Boardbooks) and the broader Diligent One Platform, which unifies board management, enterprise risk, audit, compliance, entity management, and ESG. The board portal itself is a security-hardened product with no public developer API - it is integrated through SSO (SAML 2.0), SCIM provisioning, and packaged connectors (Okta, Microsoft 365/Teams, Zoom, DocuSign). Diligent does, however, publish a real developer portal at developer.diligent.com covering the GRC side of the platform - the HighBond (Diligent One) REST API for audit/risk/compliance data, a GraphQL Entities API for legal-entity and subsidiary management, an ESG API for activity/usage data, and a Workflow API for jobs, tasks, and campaigns. API access is customer/partner-gated (a HighBond API key or SSO-scoped token is required) and pricing is quote-based via Diligent sales.

providers.name: Meshcrafts
providers.description: Meshcrafts, operating publicly as CURRENT (Current Eco AS, formerly Meshcrafts AS, of Oslo, Norway), is a charge point management system (CPMS) provider for electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure. Its cloud platform lets location owners and charge point operators manage EV charging points, handle payment and invoicing, apply smart energy management and load balancing, and offer white-label charging experiences to drivers. The platform is hardware-agnostic and OCPP (Open Charge Point Protocol) certified for OCPP 1.6 and OCPP 2.0.1, including Advanced Security, and advertises 99% uptime. Current was the first in the Nordics to reach OCPP 2.0.1 CORE and Advanced Security. The company is backed by 500 Global and surfaced in the API Evangelist network through that portfolio.

providers.name: Arka
providers.description: Arka is a custom packaging company that lets ecommerce brands design, order, and ship eco-friendly custom boxes, mailers, and sustainable packaging online. Arka offers low minimums, fast turnaround, and plug-in integrations with commerce platforms including Shopify, BigCommerce, and Square so merchants can reorder packaging alongside their fulfillment workflow. Arka's storefront runs on Shopify and exposes a modern agent-commerce surface — a published /llms.txt, an agentic-discovery sitemap, OIDC/OAuth 2.0 discovery for the Shopify Customer Account API, and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint that lets AI shopping agents search the catalog, build carts, and complete buyer-approved checkouts. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled here as part of the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: CPower
providers.description: CPower Energy is a commercial and industrial (C&I) virtual power plant (VPP) operator that helps organizations monetize the flexibility of their energy assets through demand response and distributed energy resource (DER) programs. Its CPower CONNECT platform lets customers view, manage, and unlock revenue from energy assets while supporting grid reliability and sustainability goals. CPower serves data centers, crypto mining, healthcare, education, retail, commercial real estate, industrial operations, and the public sector, and has operated distributed energy programs across the U.S. since 2015. CPower was acquired by NRG Energy and operates a combined C&I VPP platform. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-adjacent deep-tech lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; CPower publishes a customer portal and a security and compliance posture but no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Crux
providers.description: Crux is a capital platform for the clean economy, connecting clean energy and manufacturing developers with buyers, lenders, and investors. Its marketplace facilitates the sale of transferable clean energy tax credits created under the Inflation Reduction Act, alongside debt capital markets, tax equity, and preferred equity solutions and advisory services. Crux pairs a transaction platform and secure data room with market intelligence drawn from tens of billions of dollars in deal data, serving project developers, manufacturers, tax credit buyers, banks, tax advisors, and legal teams. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. Crux operates a customer application but does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Nuvolo
providers.description: Nuvolo is a modern Integrated Workplace Management System (IWMS) and Enterprise Asset Management provider that delivers its Connected Workplace suite natively on the ServiceNow platform. It unifies facilities and space management, real estate and lease administration, capital planning and projects, maintenance and work management, healthcare technology management (HTM), GxP and life-sciences asset management, refrigeration management, sustainability and energy, and OT security into a single cloud platform. Nuvolo serves healthcare, life sciences, public sector, retail, and education organizations, helping them manage the full lifecycle of their assets, spaces, and facilities with mobile access and real-time reporting. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Puro.earth
providers.description: Puro.earth provides a certification infrastructure for carbon removal, turning durable carbon removal into a global, investment‑grade market. It offers a registry, standards, and tools for issuing, trading, and verifying carbon removal credits, supporting transparency and trust in the emerging CDR sector.

providers.name: TenneT
providers.description: TenneT is a leading European transmission system operator (TSO) responsible for high‑voltage electricity grids in the Netherlands and Germany. It ensures reliable, secure power supply, drives the energy transition, and provides market platforms for electricity trading. The company focuses on sustainability, grid expansion, and digital innovation to support a low‑carbon future.

providers.name: Posteo
providers.description: Posteo is a German email service provider focused on privacy, security, and sustainability. It offers ad‑free, encrypted email with strong data protection, green hosting powered by renewable energy, and features such as DANE, OpenPGP, and two‑factor authentication. The service emphasizes user anonymity, no tracking, and transparent policies, positioning itself as a secure alternative to mainstream email providers.

providers.name: KITRO
providers.description: KITRO is a Swiss company founded in 2017 in Zurich that helps professional kitchens measure and reduce food waste through AI-powered automation. Its KITRO TARE device pairs an IoT scale with a camera and computer vision to automatically identify, weigh and categorize discarded food with no change to kitchen workflow, feeding a cloud analytics dashboard that surfaces waste trends by time, item and station, compares performance across properties, and exports reports for sustainability and EU food-waste compliance reporting. KITRO serves hotel groups and resorts, hospitals and care homes, corporate canteens, universities and schools, and river and ocean cruise operators in 20+ countries, with customers including Marriott, Hyatt, TUI BLUE, Pestana, 25hours Hotels and Sydney Opera Bar. KITRO publishes no public developer API, SDKs or developer portal — the only customer-facing software surface is the authenticated dashboard at my.kitro.ch — but it does publish an llms.txt agent-readable company description at www.kitro.ch/llms.txt.

providers.name: Spiber
providers.description: Spiber Inc. is a Japanese biotechnology and advanced-materials company founded in 2007 and headquartered in Tsuruoka, Yamagata Prefecture, Japan. Spiber develops Brewed Protein materials — structural proteins produced by precision fermentation of plant-derived sugars using engineered microbes, then spun into fibers, resins, and films as animal-free, petroleum-free alternatives to silk, wool, cashmere, leather, and synthetic polymers. The company operates fermentation plants in Japan, Thailand, and the United States and supplies apparel, outdoor, automotive, and consumer brands, alongside a research program in synthetic biology, polymer science, and life-cycle assessment. Spiber is a materials manufacturer rather than a software vendor and publishes no developer program, developer portal, SDKs, or product API; the only machine-readable HTTP surface it serves is the read-only WordPress REST content API behind its corporate website.

providers.name: Aquaria
providers.description: Aquaria makes water from thin air—delivering abundant, safe water for your entire home with no pipes, no wells, no PFAS. The company provides atmospheric water generators for residential, commercial, and community use, aiming to solve water scarcity with sustainable technology.

providers.name: Huawei FusionSolar
providers.description: Huawei FusionSolar provides intelligent solar energy solutions, including photovoltaic inverters, energy storage systems, and management platforms for residential, commercial, and utility-scale solar projects. The platform offers monitoring, design tools, and a developer portal for integrating solar data and services.

providers.name: JOLT
providers.description: JOLT is a Sydney-headquartered electric vehicle charging network operator that builds and runs free-to-start kerbside DC fast chargers across Australia, and has since extended the same model into New Zealand, Canada, the United Kingdom and the United States. Its charge points deliver the first 7kWh of each day's charging at no cost — around 45km of range in roughly 15 minutes over CCS2 or CHAdeMO — funded not by the driver but by the digital out-of-home advertising screens mounted on the charger itself, which makes JOLT simultaneously a charge point operator and a media network selling audience reach to advertisers. It sits in the energy value chain as a downstream infrastructure and demand-side player: it buys electricity (claiming 100% GreenPower green-certified wind and solar), owns and operates the charging assets on public and retail land in partnership with governments and hosts such as Transport for NSW, Ausgrid and major grocery retailers, and monetises the dwell time rather than the kilowatt-hour. Its API posture is honestly closed. JOLT publishes no developer programme, no API documentation, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no open data feed; the only public HTTP surfaces on its domains are a marketing WordPress install (whose custom jolt/v1 REST namespace exposes a single VAT form endpoint) and an api.joltcharge.com host that serves a static redirect to the mobile app rather than any API. It is not a designated data holder under the Australian Consumer Data Right for energy — it does not appear in the CDR Register's energy data holder brands — so the CDR energy mandate that compels Australian electricity retailers to expose standardised usage and tariff data does not reach it, and no OCPP, OCPI, ISO 15118 or Green Button/ESPI conformance is published. All customer charging data, session history and audience analytics are reachable only through the JOLT consumer app or a sales conversation.

providers.name: Deloitte
providers.description: Deloitte is one of the Big Four professional services organizations, operating through a network of member firms coordinated by Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Limited (DTTL). The organization spans approximately 150 countries and territories, has more than 180 years of history (founded 1845), and serves roughly 90% of the Fortune Global 500. Deloitte organizes delivery across four primary service lines — Audit & Assurance, Consulting, Tax, and Legal — plus specialized cross-functional practices including Business Process Solutions and Global Employer Services. Consulting offerings cover Customer, Cyber, Engineering / AI & Data, Enterprise Technology & Performance, Finance Transformation, Human Capital, Strategy & Transactions, and Risk / Regulatory & Forensic. Deloitte Digital is the technology-and-experience practice with alliances spanning Salesforce, Adobe, SAP, Google Cloud, AWS, ServiceNow, Oracle, Shopify, Sitecore, and Genesys, and accelerators such as FrontOffice Advantage, Revenue Advantage, Agentic Marketing Cloud, CreativEdge, Blueprint, Content Studios, and TrustID. The organization serves six industries divided into twenty sectors: Consumer; Energy, Resources & Industrials; Financial Services; Government & Public Services; Life Sciences & Health Care; and Technology, Media & Telecommunications. Deloitte Insights is the organization's research-publishing surface, organized into eight research centers — Cross-Industry, Economics, Consumer, Energy & Industrials, Financial Services, Government & Public Services, Life Sciences & Health Care, and Tech, Media & Telecom — producing flagship series including Tech Trends, Global Human Capital Trends, Digital Media Trends, TMT Predictions, FSI Predictions, the Weekly Global Economic Outlook, and the annual Industry Outlooks. The Deloitte AI Institute drives applied-AI research and points of view. Deloitte does not publish a public developer API or open developer portal at the corporate level. The Deloitte US Consulting GitHub organization is small (5 visible repositories, mostly archived upstream forks; the original artifact is `beacon`, a first-party web-analytics packaging library in TypeScript). Reader-facing distribution flows through MyDeloitte (personalized content + newsletter subscriptions), Dbriefs (live webcasts with CPE credit), the Deloitte Insights Magazine, and the YouTube channel; no public RSS index page was discoverable on www.deloitte.com at the path published in legacy archives.

providers.name: EnergyX
providers.description: EnergyX (Energy Exploration Technologies, Inc.) is a critical-materials technology company founded in 2018 by Teague Egan and headquartered in Austin, Texas, with operations in Texarkana, Antofagasta in Chile, and San Juan, Puerto Rico. It develops direct lithium extraction (DLE) technology — a modular, brine-agnostic flow sheet combining adsorbents, solvent extraction and its own selective membranes under the GET-Lit platform — together with SoLiS lithium-metal battery technology and NUKE-it membranes for lithium-6/7 isotope separation and nuclear fuel-cycle applications. The company produces lithium hydroxide, lithium carbonate and lithium dihydrogen phosphate, holds a large patent portfolio, and controls lithium resources in Chile and the United States including the Black Giant project. EnergyX is a materials and process-technology company rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no API documentation, no SDKs and no developer portal. The only machine-readable interface it exposes is the WordPress REST content API behind its corporate website at energyx.com, which is captured here for discovery purposes and is anonymously readable but read-only.

providers.name: Enervee
providers.description: Enervee operates an AI-powered white-label marketplace platform that helps utilities and government energy programs scale energy efficiency across 39 million-plus households in North America. Its stack spans a utility-branded online store for efficient appliances and equipment across 40-plus product categories (HVAC, water heaters, heat pumps, smart thermostats, EV chargers), the Enervee Score - a proprietary 0-100 energy-efficiency rating updated daily - Eco Financing embedded lending at checkout through national bank partners, and Instant Rebates that automatically stack utility, government, and manufacturer incentives at checkout. Enervee is a portfolio company of Obvious Ventures. No public developer API or documentation surface is currently published; this profile captures the company's public security, trust, and identity posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Plan A
providers.description: Plan A is a Berlin-based sustainability technology company providing certified carbon accounting and ESG management software that helps businesses measure, report, and reduce their greenhouse gas emissions. The platform is built on GHG Protocol standards, is SOC 2 Type II certified, and offers AI-enhanced emissions intelligence, supplier engagement, decarbonisation planning, and regulatory reporting (CSRD/ESRS). Plan A operates enterprise data integrations via custom APIs but does not publish a public developer platform, OpenAPI specification, or API reference. Backed by HV Capital and Lightspeed Venture Partners; surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched with verified public identity and web properties.

providers.name: Valyuu
providers.description: Valyuu is an Amsterdam-founded embedded recommerce service provider offering a plug-and-play trade-in platform that businesses integrate to buy back, resell, and recycle used consumer electronics such as smartphones, tablets, and smartwatches across Dutch, German, and English-language markets. Its partner-facing Trade-In API powers embedded trade-in flows covering device catalogs, condition questions, offers, payments, and shipping. Valyuu is a Techstars portfolio company; as of mid-2026 valyuu.com redirects to prioont.com, whose storefront is currently unreachable.

providers.name: Tracera
providers.description: Tracera (formerly ESG Flo) is an AI-powered corporate sustainability and ESG data platform that automates the collection, verification, auditing, and reporting of sustainability data with finance-grade accuracy and traceability. The platform extracts audit-ready metrics from raw data across PDFs, spreadsheets, and ERP systems for 900+ metrics, supports reporting frameworks including CSRD, SEC, GRI, and CDP, and serves Fortune 2000 enterprises across manufacturing, real estate, construction, retail, technology, and healthcare (customers include EnerSys, La-Z-Boy, Sauder Woodworking, and Putzmeister). Founded in 2022 and based in New York, Tracera raised a $12M Series A in April 2025 led by Foundry with Rho Ignition, Tola Capital, and Contour Venture Partners ($17.25M total). Enrichment probing found no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or event surface; the website is bot-gated by a SiteGround captcha.

providers.name: Makersite
providers.description: Makersite is an AI-powered Product Lifecycle Intelligence platform that helps manufacturers manage product sustainability, cost, and compliance by connecting products to deep-tier supply chain, material, and chemical data. The platform automates lifecycle assessments (LCA) and product carbon footprint (PCF) calculations, supports eco-design and cost optimization, and produces regulatory reporting such as EU Taxonomy and CBAM. It integrates with enterprise CAD, ERP, and PLM systems (PTC Windchill, Siemens Teamcenter, Autodesk, ANSYS). Makersite is a portfolio company of Partech. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Searoutes
providers.description: Searoutes is a maritime routing and carbon-emissions API platform for logistics, freight forwarding, and supply-chain teams. Its REST APIs compute point-to-point, port-to-point, and port-to-port sea routes with distances and durations (including SECA, HRA, and ice-area avoidance), geocode ports, airports, and places, calculate multimodal CO2e emissions (sea, road, rail, air, inland waterway) using a GLEC-accredited methodology, track vessels via AIS (positions, ETAs, traces, arrivals), look up carriers and services, and return historical, real-time, and forecasted weather along routes. All APIs are served from https://api.searoutes.com and authenticated with an x-api-key header.

providers.name: UP42
providers.description: UP42 is a geospatial marketplace and developer platform for Earth observation (EO) data and analytics, operated by Airbus Defence and Space. It lets you search a global archive of satellite and aerial imagery (Catalog), task new satellite acquisitions on demand (Tasking), place and track Orders, store and download results as cloud-native Assets, and browse everything through a STAC-compliant data management API. Delivery, ordering, and storage are exposed over a documented REST API at https://api.up42.com, authenticated with OAuth2 access tokens (obtained from an API key or account credentials), and are also wrapped by an official Python SDK. Storage is powered by STAC and the cloud-native asset model, and job/order status changes can be pushed to consumer endpoints via webhooks.

providers.name: WeaveGrid
providers.description: WeaveGrid builds grid-orchestration software that lets electric utilities absorb rapid EV and distributed-energy load growth without overbuilding the distribution system. Its DISCO (Distribution-Integrated System Capacity Orchestration) platform ingests vehicle telematics and cloud-connected device data, then sends hyper-local, individualized charging and dispatch signals to EVs, home batteries, smart thermostats and other flexible loads so they respond to real constraints at the transformer, feeder and substation level. The company runs managed-charging and time-of-use programs for utilities including Pacific Gas and Electric, Dominion Energy, DTE, Xcel Energy, Baltimore Gas and Electric, Alabama Power, Ameren Illinois and Portland General Electric, and integrates directly with OEM and device partners such as Toyota, Lexus, Rivian, Hyundai, Kia, ChargePoint, Wallbox, Emporia, SolarEdge, FranklinWH and ecobee. WeaveGrid markets a partner API for aggregators, but publishes no public developer portal, reference or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Ecovadis
providers.description: Ecovadis is a global leader in providing sustainability ratings and performance improvement tools for companies looking to assess and improve their environmental and social practices. Their platform helps organizations evaluate the sustainability performance of their suppliers, partners, and vendors, enabling them to make more informed decisions when it comes to selecting business partners.

providers.name: terralayr
providers.description: terralayr is a German energy-flexibility company that develops, owns and operates utility-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) and runs LAYR, a cloud platform that aggregates heterogeneous storage assets and makes their flexibility available as bookable capacity to utilities, grid operators, power traders, aggregators and asset owners. The platform lets customers buy and sell dispatchable capacity to balance renewable generation against fluctuating grid demand, with storage bookable via API and no complex hardware onboarding. terralayr is backed by Creandum and Earlybird. Its LAYR product API is B2B/private and publishes no public OpenAPI, SDKs or developer documentation; this profile captures the public well-known discovery, security and operational surface.

providers.name: Metrobloks
providers.description: Metrobloks, LLC develops and operates multi-tenant colocation data centers in underserved metropolitan markets, positioning capacity at the metro edge so that AI inference, IoT, gaming, streaming, telecom and financial workloads run closer to the users and devices that generate them. Founded by Ernest Popescu (CEO), Scott Couzens (COO), Ryan Shea (SVP Real Estate) and Alejandro Maldonado (CMO), the company came out of stealth in June 2024 with an oversubscribed $5.2M seed round led by Current Equity Partners with participation from Serena Capital, and has since announced a Eurazeo commitment of up to EUR 100 million for European expansion, a financing round led by the Canopy Generations Fund, a Kansas City joint venture with Lincoln Property Company, and a partnership with Soluna. Sites are announced or under development in Miami FL, Phoenix AZ, Detroit MI, Kansas City MO, Indianapolis IN and McAllen TX in North America, plus Paris in Europe. The product is physical: modular standardized halls, scalable power, air and hybrid liquid cooling with near-zero water consumption, and carrier-neutral interconnection including a self-perform cross-connect option. Metrobloks sells infrastructure, not software. It publishes no API, no developer portal, no customer self-service platform and no machine-readable specification of any kind; its only published compliance claim is a SOC 2 and SOC 3 assertion on its ESG page.

providers.name: Nexamp
providers.description: Nexamp is a Boston-based clean energy company, founded in 2007 by two U.S. Army veterans, that develops, builds, owns and operates distributed solar generation and battery storage across the United States and is one of the country's largest fully integrated community solar providers. The company runs end-to-end: project development and acquisition, engineering and design, construction, asset operations, and subscriber management for residential and commercial community solar customers, alongside power purchase agreements, land leasing for solar farm hosts, energy storage, and standalone development and asset-management services. Customer-facing software is delivered through the community.nexamp.com subscriber portal and the portal.nexamp.com Decarbonization Platform. As of the 2026-08-01 enrichment pass Nexamp publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contract; the api.nexamp.com host that exists is gated behind Microsoft Entra ID and is not publicly documented.

providers.name: Olyns
providers.description: Olyns is a Silicon Valley company, founded in 2019, that operates an AI-powered reverse vending and retail media network built around the Olyns Cube — a self-serve kiosk that accepts beverage containers and rigid plastic packaging, uses computer vision to identify and sort each item at the point of deposit, pays the consumer their deposit (CRV) refund electronically, and carries a 55-inch screen that Olyns sells as digital-out-of-home advertising inventory. Cubes are placed with supermarkets, big-box retailers, pharmacies and gas stations, and the advertising side is sold both directly and programmatically through Screenverse. Olyns ships consumer and operations software — a mobile/web wallet app at app.olyns.com and a self-service ad portal at ads.olyns.com — but publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: XDI
providers.description: XDI (Cross Dependency Initiative) provides physical climate risk expertise, offering solutions such as asset risk screening, deep‑dive analyses, reporting, stress‑testing, and resilience planning. Their platform delivers data and insights to help financial, corporate, government, and civil‑society clients understand, report, and mitigate climate‑related risks across portfolios.

providers.name: Skanska
providers.description: Skanska is a global construction and development company delivering complex building and infrastructure projects across diverse market sectors. With a focus on sustainability, innovation, and community impact, Skanska builds for a better society, offering services in commercial development, transportation infrastructure, and building construction worldwide.

providers.name: Biome Makers
providers.description: Biome Makers is a global agricultural technology company founded in 2015 and headquartered in El Macero, California, that uses soil microbiome DNA sequencing and machine learning to measure and restore soil health. Its BeCrop platform decodes the functionality of soil microbial communities across 200+ crops in 56+ countries, delivering agronomic recommendations, agricultural-input validation, and supply-chain sustainability benchmarking to farmers, ag retailers, CPG companies, and research labs. Products include BeCrop Farm, BeCrop Test, BeCrop Trials, and BeCrop Rate. BeCrop is accessible via API for large-scale partner integrations, though the developer API is partner-gated and no public OpenAPI specification is currently published.

providers.name: Brother's Bond Bourbon
providers.description: Brother's Bond Bourbon is a craft bourbon brand founded by actors Ian Somerhalder and Paul Wesley. The company produces award‑winning straight bourbon, blended rye, and limited‑edition releases, emphasizing sustainability and innovative grain blends. Their website showcases the story, method, product lineup, and press coverage, positioning the brand within the premium spirits market.

providers.name: Certa
providers.description: Certa (operated by Opinr, Inc. d/b/a Certa) is an AI-native third-party risk management (TPRM) and compliance platform that unifies the full third-party lifecycle — onboarding, due diligence, contract management, continuous compliance monitoring, and offboarding — in a single no-code system. Founded by Jag Lamba and headquartered in Saratoga, CA, Certa serves Fortune 500 companies (Honeywell, Uber, Mars, Box, Quantcast) across 120+ countries and 17 languages. The platform covers all risk domains — operational and resilience, infosec and cyber, compliance and legal, financial and credit, reputational, geopolitical, and ESG and ethical risk — via its Studio no-code process designer, Certa Connect (130+ native integrations), and embedded AI agents. Certa was named a Leader in the inaugural 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Third-Party Risk Management Tools. External integration is available through an enterprise external API surfaced from the platform; no public OpenAPI or developer portal is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Clarity AI
providers.description: Clarity AI is a sustainability technology and fintech company that provides AI-powered extra-financial intelligence for financial decision-making. Its platform delivers ESG risk ratings, climate and physical-risk analytics, regulatory-compliance reporting (EU Taxonomy, SFDR, MiFID II, ESMA fund naming, Pillar 3), impact and UN SDG alignment, and retail-banking climate engagement tools. Clarity AI reports coverage of 300K+ listed and private companies, 450K+ funds, and 400+ sovereigns, and serves asset managers, asset owners, banks, wealth managers, and corporates. The company exposes its data through a web application, data feeds, APIs, and emerging AI agent / MCP integrations, though its developer surface is gated behind an enterprise platform login rather than a public developer portal. Clarity AI is a portfolio company of the SoftBank Vision Fund. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Koloma
providers.description: Koloma is a Denver, Colorado based natural (geologic) hydrogen exploration and production company founded in 2021 by Pete Johnson and Tom Darrah, PhD, with a research laboratory in Columbus, Ohio. The company applies subsurface geoscience, proprietary data and data-driven exploration methods — airborne geophysics, passive acoustic and magnetotelluric surveys, and lab characterization of rock, liquid and gas samples — to locate and produce naturally occurring hydrogen generated by serpentinization deep within the Earth. Koloma operates in the United States and internationally, including Koloma Australia and exploration operations in the Philippines, and is backed by Amazon Climate Pledge Fund, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and United Airlines. Koloma publishes no public developer platform, API documentation or SDKs; its only machine-readable agent surface found in this pass is a Wix-platform Model Context Protocol endpoint plus an llms.txt served from the Koloma California regional site.

providers.name: greenerahead-com
providers.description: Greener Ahead provides ESG software solutions for voluntary sustainability reporting, CSRD compliance, carbon accounting, and climate strategy. Their platform helps businesses collect, analyze, and report environmental data, offering tools for emissions tracking, regulatory reporting, and strategic planning to turn sustainability into a competitive advantage.

providers.name: Turion Space
providers.description: Turion Space is an Irvine, California aerospace company founded in 2021 (Y Combinator S21) that designs, builds and operates DROID maneuverable spacecraft for space domain awareness, non-earth imaging and in-orbit servicing, alongside the STARFIRE software platform for mission planning, autonomous tasking and command-and-control across Turion and third-party constellations. Its customer-facing surface is the STARFIRE dashboard at starfire.turionspace.com, backed by a first-party REST API gateway at api.app.turionspace.com that issues per-user API keys and meters imagery tasking and Starfire NEXUS jobs against a Stripe-billed credit balance. The company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification; the entire contract sits behind the STARFIRE customer login.

providers.name: Aunt Flow
providers.description: Aunt Flow is a woman-owned company on a mission to end period poverty by making menstrual products freely accessible in public restrooms the same way toilet paper is. It manufactures and sells free-vend period product dispensers (models P, E, R, and O), organic cotton tampons and pads, touch-free disposal systems, and retail display boxes, serving schools, universities, offices, airports, stadiums, ski resorts, restaurants, health systems, amusement parks, and coworking spaces. Since 2021 the company has donated over 6 million period products to people in need. Aunt Flow is a physical-products and e-commerce business (Techstars-backed) with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity, commercial links, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Open Climate Fix
providers.description: Open Climate Fix delivers AI-driven forecasting solutions for solar, wind, and demand energy systems. By leveraging satellite data and advanced models, they provide accurate, minutes‑to‑hours ahead predictions to help grids run cleaner and more efficiently. Their work spans solar forecasting, wind forecasting, cloud‑casting, and data unlocking, supporting the global energy transition.

providers.name: Remoov
providers.description: Remoov is a San Francisco-based full-service removal, resale, donation, and recycling company that helps households and businesses declutter by picking up unwanted furniture and goods, then reselling them on consignment (via reperch.com), donating them to charities, or recycling them responsibly. Customers schedule a pickup, receive a quote, and earn a share of resale proceeds. Remoov also serves realtors, stagers, property managers, and living communities as partners. Backed by 500 Global. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; Remoov publishes a consumer web app and help desk but no public developer API.

providers.name: Resourcify
providers.description: Resourcify (Resourcify GmbH) is a Hamburg, Germany based digital platform for waste management and circular-economy operations, describing itself as "the operating system for a circular future." Its cloud software helps enterprises digitize and optimize their waste streams end to end - automating waste and recycling operations, optimizing cost, CO2 and recycling rates, tracking compliance, and running take-back systems - across manufacturing, construction, retail, healthcare, and airports. The platform connects waste producers with a network of recyclers and haulers, captures waste data and documentation, and reports on sustainability and material recovery. Resourcify is backed by Speedinvest. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal; integrations are delivered as managed connections rather than a self-serve API.

providers.name: AENTS
providers.description: AENTS (엔츠) is a Seoul, South Korea climate-technology company founded in 2021 by CEO Gwangbeen Park and CTO Chongsoo Jung. Its product is AENTSCOPE (엔스코프), an enterprise carbon-management and carbon-accounting SaaS platform — described by the company as the first of its kind in Korea, launched in early 2022 — that lets a corporation build a greenhouse-gas inventory, automate Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions calculation, run third-party verification, and produce disclosure reports aligned to KSSB, IFRS S2, CSRD, GRI, ISSB and CDP, alongside product carbon footprint (PCF/LCA), CBAM, climate physical-risk analysis and a supplier portal for Scope 3 value-chain data. AENTS pairs the platform with a climate-expert ESG consulting practice, and publishes a Korean-language blog, newsletter and a free corporate emissions calculator. Named customers include JYP, Nongshim, Woosung and Hansalim. The company raised a Series A led by Envisioning Partners in February 2023 and is also a Mashup Ventures portfolio company. AENTSCOPE is an API CONSUMER rather than an API producer: the company markets automated data collection through connections to external systems — the Korea Electric Power Corporation (한국전력/KEPCO) API, the Allbaro (올바로) national waste-management API, and customer ERP systems including SAP and Douzone — but publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK or webhook surface of its own.

providers.name: Amperecloud
providers.description: Amperecloud (Amperecloud GmbH) is a German renewable-energy management software company whose cloud platform provides an operating system for monitoring, operating, and commercially managing solar, wind, and other renewable-energy assets at scale. The platform brings asset performance monitoring, maintenance and ticket management, commercial and technical asset management, and virtual power plant (VPP) capabilities into a single system, supported by migration, consulting, and custom-integration services. It is used by more than 300 customers worldwide managing over 8,000 installations and 10+ GWp of capacity. Added to the API Evangelist network as a point-nine portfolio company; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is currently published, so this profile captures verified company identity and a domain-security probe pending any future public API surface.

providers.name: Ascend Elements
providers.description: Ascend Elements is a Westborough, Massachusetts battery materials company that manufactures engineered lithium-ion battery materials from valuable elements reclaimed from spent lithium-ion batteries and gigafactory manufacturing scrap. Founded in 2015 as Battery Resourcers out of MIT-affiliated research by Eric Gratz and Professor Yan Wang, it recovers up to 98% of the critical battery metals in end-of-life cells and uses its patented Hydro-to-Cathode direct cathode precursor (pCAM) synthesis process to produce cathode precursor and battery-grade lithium carbonate, reducing the carbon footprint of new EV battery cathode material by up to 90%. Its Base 1 facility in Covington, Georgia is North America's largest electric-vehicle battery recycling plant, and Apex 1 in Hopkinsville, Kentucky is its commercial pCAM plant. Ascend Elements publishes no public developer API for its materials, recycling or logistics business; the only machine-readable surface observed on its own hosts is the WordPress REST API at ascendelements.com/wp-json, which serves the corporate website's content, media-coverage, jobs and supplier sourcing-event collections.

providers.name: Base Power
providers.description: Base Power (Base Texas REP, LLC, PUCT License #10338) is an Austin, Texas home energy company that pairs an installed home battery (40–80 kWh) with retail electricity service across Texas and Illinois. The battery powers a home automatically during outages with no manual switch and helps lower the energy bill: batteries charge when grid demand is low and send power back to the grid when demand is high (grid-balancing), and that grid revenue helps keep member energy rates low. Base can be the retail electricity provider with or without a battery, works with existing solar, and serves the Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, TNMP, CoServ, GVEC, Farmers Electric, and El Paso Electric areas in Texas plus ComEd in Illinois. Led by CEO Zach Dell and co-founder Justin Lopas; named to the TIME100 Most Influential Companies (2026); backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Addition, Bond Capital, Ribbit Capital, and Spark Capital. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Base publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: FlexGen Power Systems
providers.description: FlexGen Power Systems is a Durham, North Carolina energy storage technology company founded in 2009 that designs, integrates and operates grid-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) and the software that runs them. Its flagship product is HybridOS, a hardware-agnostic energy management system (EMS) for multi-source, multi-site battery and solar portfolios, alongside HybridOS Control BMS (a US-built battery management system), a solar power plant controller (PPC), EMS retrofit, activation and lifecycle services, and data-center power solutions. FlexGen has been named a BloombergNEF Tier 1 energy storage company, acquired Clean Energy Services (CES) and the assets of Powin, and states that HybridOS exposes automated APIs and historian data API access to customers. No public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification is published; the HybridOS API surface is reached only through customer deployments and the login-gated FlexGen customer portal.

providers.name: Growatt
providers.description: Growatt New Energy is a global manufacturer of solar PV inverters, energy storage systems, and smart energy management products for residential, commercial, and utility-scale installations. Growatt operates the ShineServer / ShinePhone cloud monitoring platform and publishes a token-authenticated Open API (V1) that lets third-party systems read plant and device telemetry, retrieve historical energy data, and read or write inverter parameters for MIN (TLX) string inverters and SPH (MIX) hybrid inverters across regional endpoints. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital; enriched from Growatt's public developer surface.

providers.name: RatedPower
providers.description: RatedPower, part of Enverus (ENVERUS RATEDPOWER S.L.U., Madrid, Spain), is a cloud software platform for the design and engineering of utility-scale renewable energy projects. Its pvDesign product automates solar photovoltaic (PV) plant layout, energy-yield simulation, battery energy storage system (BESS) and hybrid plant design, substation and grid-connection engineering, earthwork estimating, and bankable proposal documentation. The platform is delivered as a browser-based SaaS application (login at ratedpower.enverus.com) and reports 64,000+ projects designed and 5.1 TW of simulated capacity. No public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer portal is published; enterprise automation access exists only behind the authenticated application. This profile was seeded as a Techstars portfolio lead and has been run through the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Twaice
providers.description: TWAICE (TWAICE Technologies GmbH) is a Munich-based battery analytics software company. Its predictive analytics platform turns BMS data from battery energy storage systems (BESS) and electric-vehicle fleets into actionable insights for performance management, warranty management, safety monitoring, digital commissioning, and BESS reporting, alongside a battery simulation model library for engineers. Customers include BESS asset owners and operators, IPPs, utilities, automotive and bus/truck OEMs, and battery manufacturers. TWAICE is ISO 27001 certified, holds the automotive TISAX label, and is backed by investors including Creandum and Speedinvest. It publishes no public API or developer program; the platform is a closed SaaS.

providers.name: Agreena
providers.description: Agreena is a Copenhagen-based agtech and climate finance company, founded in 2021, that helps farmers transition to regenerative agriculture and monetize the resulting soil-carbon outcomes. Its AgreenaCarbon platform combines farmer enrollment, a satellite-, AI-, and soil-sampling-based digital measurement, reporting and verification (dMRV) engine, and Verra-certified carbon credit issuance. Agreena also offers standalone remote-sensing products such as a field-boundary-detection API for agrifood supply-chain monitoring. The platform spans roughly 5 million hectares and 2,500+ farmers across ~20 European countries. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis and HV Capital and is being enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Agreena publishes no public developer portal or OpenAPI surface at this time.

providers.name: BreezoMeter
providers.description: Environmental intelligence REST API providing real-time and forecast air quality, pollen counts, wildfire data, and weather information with street-level accuracy. BreezoMeter was acquired by Google in September 2022 and its technology is now integrated into Google Maps Platform.

providers.name: Goodr
providers.description: Goodr is an Atlanta-based sustainable surplus food management and hunger-relief logistics company founded in 2016 by Jasmine Crowe-Houston. Goodr helps businesses divert edible and inedible food waste from landfills by scheduling pickups, donating surplus edible food to local nonprofits, and providing donors with the tax deductions and impact reporting tied to those donations. Alongside its food-waste solutions, Goodr runs hunger-relief programs including pop-up grocery markets, meal delivery, student snackpacks, and community grocery stores. The company reports more than 30 million meals served and 4 million pounds of food diverted from landfills for enterprise partners such as Amazon, Google, NASA, and Fulton County. Goodr operates through a partner portal rather than a public developer API; this profile tracks its public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: International Energy Agency (IEA)
providers.description: The International Energy Agency (IEA) provides a REST API for accessing global energy statistics, renewables data, CO2 emissions factors, monthly electricity generation data, oil market reports, and energy policy information. The IEA API enables programmatic access to authoritative energy data covering 150+ countries and offering up-to-hourly real-time emissions factors alongside comprehensive historical datasets.

providers.name: Kayrros
providers.description: Kayrros is an environmental-intelligence and geospatial-AI company that independently tracks human activity and its physical footprint worldwide by combining satellite imagery, alternative data, and machine learning. Its products span energy markets — crude oil and jet fuel intelligence, LNG, renewables, solar and battery-storage construction monitoring, industrial and on-road energy demand, and stockpiles — and environmental risk — methane emissions via Methane Watch, wildfire risk, forest-carbon and deforestation monitoring, and carbon accounting. Kayrros delivers asset-level data feeds, APIs, and dashboards to traders, operators, financial institutions, regulators, insurers, and the public sector. The company was acquired by Energy Aspects in May 2026.

providers.name: KNMI Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute
providers.description: The Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute (KNMI) is the Dutch national weather service, providing weather forecasts, climate data, and seismology information. It operates as a public research institute, delivering data and expertise to government, businesses, and the public. The KNMI offers APIs for weather observations, forecasts, climate statistics, and earthquake data, supporting applications in agriculture, aviation, emergency management, and scientific research.

providers.name: Air France-KLM
providers.description: Air France-KLM is a leading European airline group operating worldwide, offering passenger and cargo services through its Air France, KLM, and Transavia brands. The group serves over 320 destinations, emphasizing sustainability, innovation, and customer experience. It provides extensive travel solutions, loyalty programs, and digital services, reflecting its commitment to responsible aviation and global connectivity.

providers.name: Chargesini
providers.description: ChargeSini is a Malaysian electric vehicle (EV) charging network operator that installs, operates, and bills public and private chargers across Malaysia. It offers a mobile app for locating, reserving, and paying for charging sessions, supports fast DC charging up to 120 kW, and provides solutions for condos, businesses, and malls. The company emphasizes sustainability, offers subscription plans, and partners with local businesses to expand EV infrastructure.

providers.name: Waste Connections
providers.description: Waste Connections is the third-largest integrated provider of solid waste services in North America, serving approximately nine million residential, commercial, and industrial customers across 46 U.S. states and six Canadian provinces. The company provides non-hazardous waste collection, transfer, disposal, and recycling services, primarily in exclusive and secondary markets. Waste Connections is investing in AI-powered dynamic routing and expanding customer connectivity features through its online customer portal.

providers.name: Bluestonelane
providers.description: Bluestone Lane is an Australian‑origin coffee brand operating cafés across the United States. It offers ethically‑sourced, meticulously‑roasted coffee beans, a subscription service, wholesale programs, and a loyalty app that rewards frequent customers. The company emphasizes sustainable packaging, community‑centric café experiences, and corporate coffee solutions for businesses. While it runs a robust retail e‑commerce site and provides corporate coffee services, it does not currently expose a public API for external developers. The brand focuses on quality, sustainability, and a distinctive Australian café culture brought to American neighborhoods.

providers.name: LevelTen Energy
