providers.description: LevelTen Energy operates a two-sided digital marketplace and transaction platform for carbon-free energy, describing itself as the transaction infrastructure for the energy transition. Clean energy buyers, advisors, project developers, utilities and financiers use the LevelTen Energy Marketplace to compare thousands of power purchase agreement (PPA) offers, run NPV and settlement cashflow analysis, evaluate risk scenarios and track a Development Maturity Score across projects in North America and Europe. The platform also covers granular certificates, hybrid and storage PPAs, and performance monitoring, alongside market intelligence products including MarketPulse, the LevelTen PPA Price Index and Market Transparency Reports. The marketplace is served by an authenticated API at api.levelten.energy, which is gated behind marketplace login and publishes no public developer documentation, SDKs or machine-readable specification at this time.

providers.name: Cladwell
providers.description: Cladwell is a smart-closet and outfit-planning consumer application that helps people build capsule wardrobes and get more wear out of the clothes they already own. The service digitizes a user's closet, then uses AI styling ("Ask Cladwell") together with weather and personal preferences to recommend daily outfits, reduce over-buying, and encourage sustainable, intentional dressing. With more than one million app downloads, Cladwell is delivered primarily as iOS/Android and web apps (app.cladwell.com) with a subscription model; it currently exposes no public developer API. Founded and led by CEO Erin Flynn, it was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment tracking.

providers.name: Biomejapan
providers.description: Biomejapan, operating under the brand Biome Inc., provides comprehensive nature data platforms and ecological analytics solutions for corporations and governments in Japan. Leveraging the country’s largest real‑time biological distribution dataset, the company offers APIs and services that enable monitoring, protection, and enrichment of natural environments, supporting sustainability initiatives and regulatory compliance.

providers.name: Altarock Energy
providers.description: AltaRock Energy is a technology leader in Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) development, raising EGS to massive scale. It provides clean, affordable, renewable geothermal energy worldwide, advancing innovative drilling, reservoir engineering, and power generation to make geothermal power available anywhere and everywhere.

providers.name: Brandback
providers.description: Brandback is a Berlin-based embedded resale infrastructure company (legal entity Arbor Technologies GmbH) that lets online retailers and fashion brands integrate resale directly into their baskets, product listings, and checkouts. Shoppers see an item's future resale value before they buy, resell it later in a single click, and receive store credit, while Brandback's AI handles pricing recommendations, condition checks, customer service, shipping, disputes, and payouts. Retailers can launch a white-label resale marketplace with no upfront cost and integrate with any e-commerce platform. Founded in 2023 and backed by $7.4M in pre-seed and seed funding led by Earlybird VC, Brandback reports a 9.5% average conversion-rate lift with customers including Replay Jeans and Sandqvist.

providers.name: Sunairio
providers.description: Sunairio is a grid forecasting company that provides integrated weather, climate, and energy insights for power markets. Its flagship platform, Sunairio ONE, generates 1,000-member ensemble forecasts across horizons from hourly to decadal, capturing extreme-weather and grid-stress scenarios that traditional forecasts miss. The company also publishes SHED (Sunairio High-resolution Earth Data), a proprietary historical weather dataset for the Continental US from 1950 to present at roughly 100x the resolution of ERA5, with asset-level wind and solar variability. Customers such as energy traders, grid operators, utility-scale asset developers, and demand-response aggregators access forecasts and data through a web UI, an API, and (on higher tiers) direct Snowflake data delivery. Founded in 2020 by Rob Cirincione, the company has been recognized by the National Science Foundation, American Clean Power, and EPRI.

providers.name: Greenplaces
providers.description: Greenplaces is a sustainability and ESG reporting platform that pairs software with expert consulting to help companies — especially suppliers responding to enterprise requirements — measure their carbon footprint under the GHG Protocol and complete sustainability framework submissions including CDP, EcoVadis, SBTi, GRI, SASB/ISSB and GRESB. The managed-service platform also supports B Corp certification, CSRD readiness, SOC 2 and AI-governance compliance, and tracking of regulations such as California SB 253 and SB 261. Greenplaces is venture-backed by Felicis and Redpoint Ventures. Added to the API Evangelist network from VC portfolio data; the company publishes a managed product (app.greenplaces.com) but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Spoiler Alert
providers.description: Spoiler Alert is a Boston-based software company (a Techstars portfolio company) that helps consumer packaged goods (CPG) manufacturers, wholesalers, and retailers manage and sell excess, short-dated, and obsolete inventory. Its purpose-built platform digitizes discounting and liquidation processes, matching surplus inventory with the right buyers at the right price through a secondary marketplace, with automated listing generation, dynamic pricing optimization, freight cost management, and performance analytics to recover margin and reduce food and product waste. The platform is delivered as a closed SaaS application (app.spoileralert.com); no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published.

providers.name: Cargobeamer
providers.description: CargoBeamer provides a smart, reliable and environmentally friendly system for intermodal transport of semi‑trailers by rail across Europe. It connects logistics companies, freight forwarders and shippers with a growing network of routes and terminals, aiming to reduce road congestion and emissions while offering flexible, fast rail‑based freight solutions.

providers.name: Mainspring Energy
providers.description: Mainspring Energy is a Menlo Park, California power-infrastructure company that designs, manufactures, and deploys the Linear Generator, a modular, fuel-flexible onsite power generation system. Its technology delivers firm, dispatchable, and low-emission electricity for data centers, utilities, and industrial and enterprise facilities, running today on natural gas and biogas with a seamless transition to zero-carbon fuels such as hydrogen and ammonia. Backed by Khosla Ventures and other investors, Mainspring has more than one gigawatt of Linear Generator capacity in late-stage development and operation. Mainspring is a hardware and power-systems company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its corporate, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: Oath
providers.description: Oath Soil Life is a US‑based company that offers products designed to replenish the soil microbiome, helping trees, lawns, and gardens thrive. Operating an e‑commerce storefront on Shopify, the brand markets soil‑health solutions and educational content to support sustainable gardening practices. The website provides a blog with gardening tips, a contact page for support, and clear terms of service and privacy policy. Oath aims to improve plant health through microbiome enrichment.

providers.name: Sighten
providers.description: Sighten was a San Francisco software company, backed by Obvious Ventures, that built a cloud platform for the residential and commercial solar industry — covering system design, proposal generation, sales, and financing workflows used by solar installers, dealers, and finance providers. The Sighten business was acquired (by GoodLeap) and folded into EverBright; the original sighten.io domain now redirects to goeverbright.com. EverBright operates as a residential solar and home-battery financing platform, connecting homeowners with local installers through lease and Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) products and the MyEverBright monitoring portal. No public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation is published for the Sighten or EverBright brand; a partner-facing platform (engine.goeverbright.com) and a protected API host (api.goeverbright.com, HTTP 401) exist but are not publicly documented. This profile records the company's current, honest public surface after enrichment.

providers.name: Husqvarna Group
providers.description: Husqvarna Group is a global leader in outdoor power products, including chainsaws, lawn mowers, and garden tools, as well as professional forestry equipment. The company operates through several divisions such as Husqvarna Forest & Garden, Gardena, and Husqvarna Construction, serving both consumer and professional markets worldwide. It focuses on innovation, sustainability, and digital services, offering connected devices and platforms for efficient outdoor work.

providers.name: Sound Agriculture
providers.description: Sound Agriculture is an Emeryville, California agriculture company founded in 2013 by Eric Davidson and Travis Bayer that sells nature-based crop nutrition products to row-crop growers through an independent dealer network: SOURCE, a foliar-applied soil activator that stimulates soil microbes to supply nitrogen and phosphorus; BLUEPRINT, an arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi inoculant; and INFLECT. It also runs an on-demand breeding program that tunes plant gene expression epigenetically without editing DNA. Sound Agriculture is not a software company and publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract; its only authenticated surface is a Salesforce Experience Cloud dealer portal at dealerportal.sound.ag.

providers.name: Capture6
providers.description: Capture6 is a water-positive carbon removal company based in California and New Zealand. It turns saltwater into fresh water while capturing atmospheric CO₂, creating fresh water and valuable by‑products. The integrated system reduces brine disposal costs, generates commercial value, and supports climate resilience for industrial partners. Capture6 partners with governments and corporations to deliver scalable water security and carbon removal solutions.

providers.name: GreenFi
providers.description: GreenFi is a climate-focused consumer financial technology company — the rebranded continuation of Aspiration's consumer banking arm. It offers a combined checking and savings account, high-yield savings with goal-based "Savings Pods", a debit card, a GreenFi Plus subscription tier, investing through its Redwood fund, and a cash-back Marketplace of sustainable brands, alongside impact programs such as Plant Your Change, tree planting and carbon offsetting. GreenFi is a financial technology company, not a bank; banking services and the debit card are provided by Coastal Community Bank, Member FDIC. Aspiration spun its consumer unit out in 2024 to Mission Financial Partners, LLC, which rebranded it GreenFi in April 2025; Coastal Financial Corporation acquired the GreenFi brand in January 2026. It is a separate company from Aspiration Partners, Inc., the enterprise carbon business that entered Chapter 11. GreenFi ships iOS, Android and web applications to end users and publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Grove Collaborative
providers.description: Grove Collaborative is a digital-first consumer products company and online marketplace for sustainable everyday household essentials — eco-friendly cleaning supplies, bamboo and recycled paper products, personal care, beauty, pet, and vitamins & supplements from hundreds of vetted brands. Orders meet strict ingredient standards and are carbon neutral, and the company operates as a plastic-neutral, sustainability-focused retailer sold through grove.co (a Shopify-hosted storefront) and retail partners. Grove is a public benefit company (NYSE: GROV) that was an early portfolio company of 500 Global and Bullpen Capital. It publishes no first-party developer API or public developer program; this profile captures its public web, security, and Shopify-platform discovery surface.

providers.name: Natural Resources Canada
providers.description: Natural Resources Canada (NRCan) is the federal department responsible for the sustainable development, management and use of Canada’s natural resources, including energy, minerals, forests, and water. It provides data, research, tools, and services to support industry, government, and the public in making informed decisions about resource stewardship, environmental protection, and economic growth. NRCan’s digital platforms offer APIs for accessing geospatial data, energy statistics, forest resources, and more, enabling developers to integrate authoritative Canadian resource information into applications and analyses.

providers.name: Bruvi
providers.description: Bruvi is a Los Angeles‑based company offering a next‑generation single‑serve coffee system. It sells brewers, reusable B‑Pods and a mobile app that automates brewing, pod ordering and personalization. The brand emphasizes sustainability, premium craft coffee, and a subscription model for fresh pods delivered to customers.

providers.name: Aclima
providers.description: Aclima is a San Francisco-based environmental intelligence company that maps and analyzes air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions at hyperlocal, block-by-block resolution. Using a network of roving (vehicle-mounted) and stationary sensors, Aclima measures multiple pollutants and climate gases simultaneously at up to 100,000x greater resolution than traditional monitoring, then translates billions of scientific measurements into environmental intelligence for governments, companies, and communities. Its professional analytics software, Aclima Pro, delivers visualization and automated analytics for emissions reduction and public-health programs, while its free air.health app maps address-level air and climate insights for the communities Aclima serves. Co-founded by CEO Davida Herzl, Aclima is backed by DCVC and is added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: PortF
providers.description: PortF is an AI-powered portfolio monitoring platform for private equity, venture capital, and institutional investors. It automates investment data collection and reporting by extracting qualitative and quantitative data from emails, documents, and 25+ connected systems (Excel, OneDrive, SharePoint, SSO, Salesforce, FIS Global, Xero, QuickBooks, Sage, and NetSuite), then consolidates financial, ESG, and impact data into a single source of truth with real-time analytics, IRR benchmarking, and agentic reporting workflows. Founded by Alex Lu and headquartered in London, PortF is backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Replenysh
providers.description: Replenysh is an enterprise circularity platform that runs circular supply chains for brands and recovery facilities. It routes, recovers, verifies, and optimizes material recovery flows across a network of 5,000+ partners, giving enterprises a single control layer for reverse logistics with audit-ready chain-of-custody, pricing, settlement, and compliance documentation. Customers include PepsiCo, Disney, Marriott, and Live Nation. Backed by Kindred Ventures and M13. Surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched via the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Revivn
providers.description: Revivn provides an integrated hardware lifecycle platform for managing end-of-life IT equipment. The company handles secure device pickup, certified data sanitization and destruction, and redistribution of usable hardware to underserved communities through nonprofit partnerships. Its software surface (the Revivn App at app.revivn.com) lets IT and asset-management teams schedule retrievals, track chain-of-custody, generate compliance and sustainability reporting, and — per Revivn's marketing — integrate Revivn's API with their IT software stack for customized workflows. No public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or SDK is published; the integration API appears to be a private, enterprise-only surface. Revivn is a 500 Global portfolio company.

providers.name: Booster Fuels
providers.description: Booster (Booster Fuels, Inc.) is a mobile energy delivery company that brings gasoline, diesel, diesel exhaust fluid (DEF), and renewable fuel alternatives directly to vehicles, fleets, and on-site fuel tanks using a fleet of Smart Tankers, removing the need for drivers to visit gas stations. The company serves enterprise fleets and local businesses across the United States, pairing on-demand fueling with a proprietary technology platform (BoosterOS / the Fleet dashboard at fleet.trybooster.com) for real-time fleet management, fuel-usage reporting, invoicing automation, fraud prevention, and emissions reduction. Booster offers custom enterprise integrations (ERP, CRM, and telematics such as Geotab and Samsara) but does not publish a public developer API portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. This profile is a company/lead entry in the API Evangelist network; no public API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Ceres Imaging
providers.description: Ceres Imaging is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: vc-portfolio; backed by lemnos-labs) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Chrysalabs
providers.description: Chrysalabs provides reliable soil carbon measurement, verification, and reporting (MRV) solutions for bankable carbon assets. Their platform uses proximal sensing technology to deliver high‑integrity data, helping project developers and financiers turn complex soil carbon projects into market‑ready assets with transparency and scientific rigor.

providers.name: Go To-U
providers.description: GO TO-U is an operating system for electric-vehicle charging management, built for Charge Point Operators (CPOs) and businesses that run charging infrastructure. The platform is hardware-agnostic, integrating with 50+ charger manufacturers (ABB, Wallbox, Siemens, EVBox and others), and bundles charge-point management, AI-powered analytics and load optimization, a driver-facing mobile app (iOS and Android), roaming, white-label options, and integrated payment processing. Its Advanced Reservation Technology (ART) lets drivers book charging slots in advance to reduce wait times. GO TO-U is a Techstars portfolio company. This profile was enriched from the company's public website; no public developer/API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications were discoverable at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Plans
providers.description: Plans (plans.app, formerly lun.energy) is a climate-technology company focused on decarbonising the built world. It removes the friction that stands in the way of transitioning homes to low-carbon energy faster, letting professionals capture building data on a mobile device, analyze it, and produce retrofit / energy plans — "capture, analyze, plan, all in your pocket." A web platform (platform.plans.app) and a Chrome extension support the workflow, and the product is offered across English, Danish, and French markets. Plans is backed by Partech. No public developer API has been identified during enrichment; the platform is a login-gated single-page application and the site exposes no OpenAPI, SDKs, docs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Renew Financial
providers.description: Renew Financial (Renew Financial Group LLC) is a specialty consumer finance company founded in 2008 and headquartered in Oakland, California that pioneered and administers Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) financing for residential energy efficiency, renewable energy, water efficiency and resiliency home improvements. It administers the CaliforniaFIRST program in California and RenewPACE in Florida, funding solar, HVAC, roofing, windows, landscaping, hurricane and seismic projects through a voluntary property tax assessment repaid over terms up to 30 years. The company is licensed by the California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation as a PACE Program Administrator (#60DBO-90653) and carries NMLS ID 1788120. Renew Financial runs a contractor technology platform and an online homeowner application, but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: SMHI
providers.description: SMHI (Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute) is Sweden’s national authority for weather, water and climate information. It provides public services, research, and professional solutions, offering open data, forecasts, climate scenarios, and expert advice to support societal planning, safety, and sustainability. The institute gathers extensive observational data and develops models to inform the public, businesses, and policymakers about weather events, climate change, and water resources.

providers.name: Inspire
providers.description: Inspire (Inspire Clean Energy) is a consumer clean-energy company on a mission to transform the way people access clean energy and accelerate a net-zero carbon future. It gives residential customers access to renewable energy for their home electricity supply through flat-rate subscription plans designed to deliver predictability and reduce exposure to electricity rate volatility. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Obvious Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, documentation, or OpenAPI surface — this is a non-API consumer brand.

providers.name: Orsted
providers.description: Ørsted is a global leader in offshore renewable energy, developing, constructing and operating offshore wind farms, as well as providing onshore wind, solar, bioenergy and energy trading solutions. The company focuses on sustainable energy transition, delivering clean power to customers worldwide while driving innovation in digital trading and analytics. Ørsted’s portfolio includes large-scale offshore wind projects across Europe, the United States and Asia, and it actively invests in new technologies to reduce carbon emissions and support a greener future.

providers.name: Archer
providers.description: Archer provides a comprehensive regulatory change management platform, offering solutions for risk, compliance, ESG, and AI governance. Their suite includes Archer Evolv, Evolv Foundation, and RMIS AI, serving enterprises across financial services, healthcare, utilities, and more. The platform unifies policy management, audit, third‑party risk, and operational resilience, delivering real‑time insights and automated compliance workflows to help organizations mitigate risk and meet regulatory requirements.

providers.name: Haven Energy
providers.description: Haven Energy is an Austin, Texas based residential clean-energy company that sells, finances, installs and operates home battery storage and solar systems, and then aggregates those systems into one of the largest virtual power plant (VPP) networks in the United States. Homeowners get an instant online quote, a fixed monthly payment over a ten-year term, end-to-end permitting and certified installation through Haven's Channel Partner network of local electricians, and ongoing remote monitoring. Haven then enrolls the installed batteries into utility and grid programs - California SGIP, PG&E, and Massachusetts ConnectedSolutions among them - so customers can monetize grid participation while utilities and community choice aggregators gain flexible local capacity. Founded in 2022 by Jeff Chapin, Philip Krim and Vinnie Campos, the company raised a $40M Series B in December 2025 led by Giant Ventures. Haven operates as a direct-to-consumer and utility-partner business; it publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Aldiusa
providers.description: Aldi USA operates a network of grocery stores across the United States, offering a limited‑assortment model focused on high‑quality private‑label products at everyday low prices. The company emphasizes simplicity, efficiency, and value, providing both in‑store shopping and online ordering for pickup and delivery through its website. Aldi USA is part of the global Aldi group, known for its cost‑effective retail approach and commitment to sustainability.

providers.name: Conservation Labs
providers.description: Conservation Labs is a Pittsburgh-based smart water technology company, backed by Techstars, Amazon, RET Ventures and SustainVC. Its flagship product, H2know, is a clamp-on acoustic smart water monitor that measures a building's inbound pipe every second and uses patented sound-detection technology and machine learning to translate those signals into accurate water-flow estimates, leak alerts and water-usage insights delivered through a companion mobile and web app. The company also offers Sustainable Machines, an edge-to-cloud platform for machine condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. Conservation Labs serves residential homes, commercial real estate, restaurants and hotels, and industrial operators. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes a consumer-facing app but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook documentation.

providers.name: LiveWire
providers.description: LiveWire designs and manufactures high-performance electric motorcycles, offering models such as the LiveWire ONE, S4 Honcho, and S2 series. The company focuses on innovative electric vehicle technology, sustainability, and a premium riding experience, with a US presence and a growing global market. It provides product information, financing options, and a dealer network through its website.

providers.name: Clearbluemarkets
providers.description: Clearbluemarkets provides carbon market intelligence and services, helping companies navigate compliance and voluntary carbon markets worldwide. Their platform offers market data, analytics, advisory, and tools for offset insight, position optimization, and EV credits aggregation, aiming to simplify decarbonization efforts and maximize financial benefits for clients.

providers.name: Phononic
providers.description: Phononic is a Durham, North Carolina solid-state cooling company founded by CEO Tony Atti that replaces compressor-based refrigeration with semiconductor thermoelectric devices. Its products cool optical and fiber transceivers, co-packaged optics, GPU high-bandwidth memory, LiDAR sensors, medical and vaccine cold chain, grocery retail merchandising and HVAC. The current focus is AI data centers, where the Thermal Kit and Thermal Fabric combine thermoelectric cooling chips with embedded control firmware that the company markets as API-accessible and Redfish-compatible, delivering millisecond thermal response plus real-time telemetry and analytics. Phononic publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification; technical access runs through sales and customer support.

providers.name: Rondo Energy
providers.description: Rondo Energy is an Alameda, California industrial decarbonization company led by CEO John O'Donnell that builds the Rondo Heat Battery (RHB), a thermal energy storage system that converts intermittent wind and solar electricity into heat stored in thousands of tons of refractory brick at temperatures up to 1,500C and returns it as continuous steam, thermal oil, superheated air, or combined heat and power at rated outputs from 2MWth to over 100MWth. The RHB is sold as a drop-in replacement for a fossil-fuel boiler, via capital purchase, lease, or heat purchase agreement, into cement, food and beverage, chemicals, fuels and ethanol, textiles, pulp and paper, mining, pharmaceuticals, and direct air capture. Rondo operates the world's largest industrial heat battery and has announced a 90GWh factory plan with Siam Cement Group, backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and Catalyst, Energy Impact Partners, Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund, Rio Tinto, SABIC, Aramco Ventures, and the European Investment Bank. Rondo sells hardware and delivered heat, not software: it publishes no developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Vantage Data Centers
providers.description: Vantage Data Centers provides innovative, scalable wholesale data center campuses to hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises across North America and Europe. They offer secure, high‑performance facilities with robust power, cooling and connectivity, supporting critical digital infrastructure and enabling rapid growth for technology‑driven businesses.

providers.name: Algenesis Labs
providers.description: Algenesis Labs develops Soleic, the world’s first fully biodegradable, high‑performance polyurethane made from plant‑based polymers. Founded in 2016, the materials‑science company creates bio‑based solutions to eliminate microplastics and reduce carbon footprints across industries. Their technology is validated by peer‑reviewed studies and recognized for green chemistry innovation.

providers.name: Arkema
providers.description: Arkema S.A. is a French specialty materials company headquartered in La Defense, Paris and listed on Euronext Paris under ticker AKE. The group is organized around three Specialty Materials segments — Adhesive Solutions (anchored by the Bostik brand), Advanced Materials (high-performance polymers including Kynar PVDF, Rilsan polyamides, Pebax elastomers, Sartomer photocurable resins) and Coating Solutions (acrylic monomers, waterborne and solvent-borne resins, additives) — plus a smaller Intermediates business. Arkema employs roughly 21,000 people across 55 countries with about 154 production plants and 17 R&D centers, generating around EUR 9.1 billion in 2025 revenue. Strategy is anchored in materials science, decarbonization and a validated 1.5 degree SBTi pathway toward Net-Zero by 2050. Arkema does not publish a public developer portal or REST API; customer integrations and product data are exchanged through commercial sales channels, the Product Finder web UI and Safety Data Sheet downloads.

providers.name: Barakah
providers.description: Barakah is a Saudi foodtech company operating a consumer mobile marketplace that fights food waste by connecting restaurants, cafes, hotels, bakeries, and grocery retailers with consumers who buy their surplus, still-fresh meals and food products at discounts of up to 70 percent for pickup or delivery. Founded in Jeddah and backed by 500 Global, FoodLabs, and Salica Investments, Barakah has grown into one of the most downloaded food and drink apps in Saudi Arabia with partnerships across more than 800 merchants, including global brands. Barakah is a business-to-consumer mobile application and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, or SDK; this profile captures its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: CLUBZERO
providers.description: CLUBZERO (CLUBZERØ) is a London-based reuse system administrator helping the food and beverage industry transition from single-use to reusable packaging. Its AI-powered platform serializes every reusable item with a GS1-standard QR, RFID, or barcode identifier, then coordinates the drop points, collection, washing, and redistribution logistics that keep packaging in circulation across on-trade, online delivery, and retail channels. CLUBZERO reports 95-98% return rates and 3.3M+ packaging rotations, running reuse programs for brands including McDonald's, Nestlé, Aramark, Compass Group, Just Eat, and the Wimbledon Championships. Backed by Seedcamp and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public API surface is currently documented.

providers.name: Dimension
providers.description: Dimension is a nationwide, on-demand waste management and junk removal platform (formerly Trash Warrior) backed by 500 Global. It offers digital booking with instant AI-generated pricing (their "Mirror Mirror AI" quoter), same-day and next-day pickup for cardboard, appliances, mattresses, hazardous and medical waste, plus dumpster rentals, for both businesses and individuals. Every job includes tracking with detailed diversion data, receipts, and photos, and can be booked as a one-off or recurring service. Dimension has been awarded a State of California RFP contract for PPE waste removal. The company operates a customer-facing booking application and help center but does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Imperfect Foods
providers.description: Imperfect Foods is a consumer grocery delivery service focused on reducing food waste. It sources surplus, cosmetically imperfect, and excess-inventory food — produce that is too large or small, packaging overstock, near best-by-date items, and manufacturing byproducts — and delivers them to members at a discount through a weekly, customizable grocery order of produce, meat, seafood, dairy, pantry staples, and snacks. Imperfect Foods was acquired by Misfits Market in 2022 and now operates as part of that company; its consumer web and mobile apps remain live. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface was found during enrichment — this profile is maintained as a company identity record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Misfits Market
providers.description: Misfits Market is a subscription-based online grocery delivery service founded in 2018 by Abhi Ramesh and headquartered in Philadelphia. It rescues surplus, cosmetically imperfect, and near-best-by organic produce, pantry staples, dairy, and meat, then delivers them to customers at a discount to reduce food waste. Members shop a personalized storefront during a weekly delivery window with no subscription fees or order minimums, and can skip or cancel anytime. The company acquired rival Imperfect Foods in 2022 and The Rounds in 2025. Backed by Accel and SoftBank Vision Fund. Misfits Market operates as a consumer e-commerce business and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: N-Drip
providers.description: N-Drip is an Israeli agritech manufacturer of gravity-powered micro-irrigation systems, led by Prof. Uri Shani, Israel's former Water Commissioner. Its patented drip system operates on gravity alone at under 0.87 PSI / 0.06 BAR, requiring no pumping station and no pressure-based filtration, and is positioned as a direct replacement for flood irrigation — which still accounts for roughly 85 percent of the world's irrigated agriculture and wastes an estimated 70 percent of the water it uses. Alongside the hardware the company ships N-Drip Connect, a sensor-and-app decision-support platform that measures root-zone water potential and available nitrogen, layers NDVI satellite imagery over the field, and issues irrigation and fertilization recommendations to growers. N-Drip technology is deployed in ten countries and five US states across 25 crop types including rice, corn, soybeans, potatoes, sugar cane, alfalfa and cotton, with a US production hub in Yuma, Arizona. N-Drip publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDK or machine-readable API contract: N-Drip Connect is delivered strictly as a closed web and mobile application.

providers.name: Planet FWD
providers.description: Planet FWD is a decarbonization software platform that helps consumer brands measure, reduce, and report their carbon emissions. It provides AI-powered product life cycle assessments (LCAs), corporate greenhouse-gas inventories across Scope 1, 2, and 3, and supply-chain decarbonization scenario planning for food & beverage, retail, and apparel companies. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Cowboy Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API surface was found at enrichment time.

providers.name: Smartex
providers.description: Smartex is an AI and computer-vision company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Porto, Portugal that builds hardware-enabled software for the textile manufacturing industry. Its systems inspect fabric in real time on the knitting machine to detect defects at the source, cutting textile waste, CO2 emissions, water, energy and rework. The product suite spans CORE (a machine-vision inspection add-on for circular knitting machines), FACT (an all-in-one digital factory-management platform for production visibility and quality control) and LOOP (supply-chain communication and traceability). Smartex is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, DCVC, Tony Fadell's Build Collective, H&M Group, SOSV/HAX, Spider Capital, Momenta Ventures and Fashion for Good. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; customer access is through the FACT platform login. This profile was surfaced from the VC-portfolio pipeline and enriched from Smartex's public web surface.

providers.name: SustainCERT
providers.description: SustainCERT is an independent, digitally-enabled climate impact verification company. It provides third-party validation and verification for carbon-market projects, corporate greenhouse-gas inventories and climate reporting, value-chain (Scope 3) decarbonization claims, and digital monitoring, reporting and verification (DMRV) for renewable energy and product carbon footprints. Customers work through the SustainCERT web platform; the company exposes no public developer API surface at this time. Added to the API Evangelist network from the Partech portfolio and enriched with domain-security probes and identity metadata.

providers.name: Timberhub
providers.description: Timberhub is a European B2B timber trading platform that connects buyers with more than 70 sawmills across 28 countries. It offers timber sourcing with 24-hour quotes, built-in EUDR (EU Deforestation Regulation) compliance automation, and AI-powered workflow automation spanning product matching, logistics, and compliance documentation. The company operates a login-gated web application at app.timberhub.com and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or machine-readable API documentation. Backed by Creandum, HV Capital, and Speedinvest.

providers.name: WiredScore
providers.description: WiredScore is the global standard-setting organization for digital connectivity and smart technology in the built environment. It assesses, benchmarks, and certifies buildings through two programs — WiredScore (digital connectivity) and SmartScore (smart building technology) — across office, residential, industrial, and hotel asset types. Landlords, developers, and occupiers in more than 40 countries use its certifications and its network of Accredited Professionals to demonstrate that a building meets modern technology and connectivity expectations; over 4,000 buildings covering roughly one billion square feet have been certified. WiredScore is a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Fifth Wall. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Arbor
providers.description: Arbor is a consumer energy savings service operating in deregulated electricity markets across 13 states in the U.S. Northeast, Midwest, and Texas. The Arbor app analyzes a household's current electricity supply rate, matches the customer with vetted alternative suppliers, and automatically switches them to a lower-cost plan when one becomes available, all without changing the utility provider, interrupting service, or charging the customer. Arbor earns revenue through referral fees from energy suppliers rather than from consumers. Founded in 2022 by Andrew Meyer (previously co-founder of Swell Energy), Arbor is backed by First Round Capital, Obvious Ventures, Spring Tide Capital, and Blisce. Arbor is a consumer-facing application and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Cloover
providers.description: Cloover is a climate-fintech company building an all-in-one, "Shopify of energy" platform for the residential renewable-energy transition. It connects the stakeholders of home energy - installers, homeowners (prosumers), manufacturers, energy providers and investors - so small and mid-sized installation firms can sell, quote, finance and manage solar panels, home batteries, heat pumps and EV charging in a single package. The platform pairs installer sales and operations software with embedded financing and energy management, and offers homeowners flexible subscription and financing options. Founded in 2023 and operating primarily in Germany, Austria and wider Europe, Cloover has raised sizeable seed and Series A equity plus a large debt facility and is backed by QED Investors, MMC Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital and others.

providers.name: Enurgen
providers.description: Enurgen is a solar energy software company whose DUET platform uses 3D physics-based modeling to optimize photovoltaic assets across their entire lifecycle. The platform spans three products - Design, Construction, and Operations - helping large-scale solar developers, independent power producers, EPC engineers, and asset managers improve energy yield estimates, validate construction against expected performance, and monitor plants in production to close the gap between forecasted (P50) and actual field output. Enurgen is a Techstars-backed company; customers include Scatec, Potentia, Lightsource, Eni, and Kiewit. The company operates a customer web application at app.enurgen.com but does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs. This API Evangelist profile is an enrichment pass that captures the company's public web properties and domain security posture.

providers.name: Fuse
providers.description: Fuse Energy is a UK retail energy supplier providing gas and electricity to homes and businesses, alongside EV charging, solar and battery storage tracking with grid export, and smart home energy management. The company emphasises savings against the UK price cap, a fast (~3 minute) online sign-up, automated supplier switching, and 24/7 customer support including an AI assistant called "Plugs". Fuse was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and Speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network. It operates a consumer/business energy web and mobile experience and does not publish a public developer API program at this time.

providers.name: Gireve
providers.description: Gireve is a B2B digital platform for electric-vehicle charging and new-mobility services, connecting charge point operators (CPOs), e-mobility service providers (eMSPs), and EV drivers across Europe. Its interoperability hub powers EV charging roaming, clearing and transaction settlement, Plug & Charge, smart charging, and mobility data services, spanning 680,000+ connected charging points and roughly one million monthly roaming transactions across 13,000+ signed agreements. Technical integration is delivered to connected operators over an OCPI-based hub through the Connect Place B2B platform; Gireve does not publish a public self-serve developer portal or OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: Green Chef
providers.description: Green Chef provides organic meal‑kit delivery services, offering chef‑crafted recipes with responsibly sourced produce and premium proteins. Customers receive weekly boxes containing fresh ingredients, detailed cooking instructions, and nutrition information, supporting healthy lifestyles while minimizing food waste. The company emphasizes sustainability, seasonal menus, and convenient home cooking solutions for busy individuals and families.

providers.name: Invesdor
providers.description: Invesdor is a pan-European crowdinvesting and digital investment platform that connects private and professional investors with companies raising capital through equity, subordinated loans, and bonds, with minimum tickets starting around EUR 250. Founded in Finland in 2012 and expanded through mergers with Finnest, Kapilendo, and Oneplanetcrowd, Invesdor now serves more than 180,000 investors across Europe and has channeled over EUR 600 million into more than 1,000 renewable-energy, scale-up, and SME financing rounds. It operates as a regulated investment firm under the EU Crowdfunding Service Provider (ECSP) regime. Invesdor does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; this profile tracks its public web, investor, and legal surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Runwise
providers.description: Runwise provides wireless smart-control systems that automate heating, cooling, water, and gas infrastructure in multifamily and commercial buildings. Its retrofit hardware and cloud platform replace legacy boiler, steam, and HVAC controls, cutting heating, cooling, and water bills by roughly 23% with same-day installation. Runwise reports more than 10,300 buildings under management and over $175 million in cumulative utility savings for customers. The company is backed by Fifth Wall, Initialized Capital, and Menlo Ventures. This API Evangelist profile tracks Runwise's public web presence; as of this pass no public API, developer portal, or programmatic integration surface has been identified.

providers.name: Sydney Water
providers.description: Sydney Water is the statutory state-owned water utility serving Greater Sydney, New South Wales, Australia. Its own site describes its role as supplying water, wastewater, recycled water and stormwater services, protecting public health, managing the environment and the health of Greater Sydney's waterways. The site offers a My Account customer portal for billing and meter reading, plumbing, building and developing services, and supplier and tender information. No public developer API portal was found on its site.

providers.name: The House Of LR&C
providers.description: The House of LR&C (Love, Respect & Care) is a Seattle-based, mission-driven direct-to-consumer fashion company founded in 2020 by Russell Wilson, Ciara, and retail veteran Christine Day. A Certified B Corporation, it operates a portfolio of apparel brands including Good Man Brand, LITA by Ciara, and Human Nation, donating 3% of net revenue to the Why Not You Foundation. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Its public commerce runs on Shopify; the company publishes no first-party developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. The only machine-readable surface on the storefront host is Shopify's platform-level Customer Account API OIDC discovery document.

providers.name: Active Membranes
providers.description: Active Membranes is a California water-technology company, founded in 2022 out of research at the UCLA Samueli School of Engineering, that builds electrically conductive "electro-active" reverse-osmosis membranes for desalination and water reuse. Where a conventional RO membrane filters passively and is cleaned after it fouls, Active Membranes embeds conductive material in the membrane's polymer matrix and uses a control unit it calls the Active Box to apply a tunable low electrical potential at the membrane surface, electrostatically repelling scale-forming ions and charged organic foulants in real time. The modules ship in the standard 8-inch by 40-inch spiral-wound format so they retrofit into existing pressure vessels, and are aimed at seawater and brackish desalination, produced-water and industrial reuse. The company reports field results including roughly 48% less irreversible fouling in produced-water reuse, up to 70% longer cleaning cycles in brackish water, and a Ventura County study citing about 57% lower cost and 64% less footprint. It has raised roughly $3.24M in seed funding from Natural Ventures, Echo River Capital and Pacifica Water Solutions, won the 2023 Global Water Summit Water Technology Idol award, and was selected as a Qualified Team in the XPRIZE Water Scarcity competition. Active Membranes sells capital equipment, not software: it operates no developer program, publishes no OpenAPI, GraphQL or SDK, and lists no pricing. It does, however, serve two machine-readable surfaces from its own hostname — a substantial hand-written /llms.txt, and a live, unauthenticated Model Context Protocol endpoint at /_api/mcp exposing nine tools over the public site content. Both are Wix platform features the company chose to enable and advertise rather than first-party engineering.

providers.name: Agragene
providers.description: Agragene is an agricultural biotechnology company using CRISPR-based genome engineering to build Precision-Guided Sterile Insect Technology (pgSIT), a modern evolution of the sterile insect technique that breeds insect lines producing only sterile males. Released into a field, those males mate with wild female crop pests and produce no viable offspring, giving growers season-long local pest suppression without chemical pesticides or irradiation. Founded in San Diego in 2017 and now headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri, the company's first product, KNOCKOUT-SWD, targets Spotted Wing Drosophila — a pest behind more than $500M in annual US berry losses — with a limited launch stated for 2027. Agragene has no developer program and publishes no API product; its only machine-readable surface is an anonymous Wix site MCP endpoint plus a company-authored llms.txt.

providers.name: AMP Robotics
providers.description: AMP Robotics (operating as AMP Sortation) is an artificial-intelligence company for the waste and recycling industry that designs, builds, and operates advanced, cost-competitive facilities to process single-stream recycling and municipal solid waste. Its Smart Sortation technology suite combines computer vision (real-time material characterization), high-speed air-jet sortation (Jet and MicroJet), and robotic-arm sortation (Delta) to raise material-recovery rates, cut contamination, and extend landfill life. The flagship AMP ONE platform delivers fully automated, facility-scale sortation processing from 10K to 1M+ tons annually for waste haulers, material-recovery facilities, and municipalities. AMP Robotics is a Google Ventures (GV) portfolio company. No public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal is published; this profile is maintained for network discovery and identity.

providers.name: Avina Clean Hydrogen
providers.description: Avina Clean Hydrogen, part of Avina Inc., develops and delivers cutting‑edge clean energy solutions, focusing on low‑carbon ammonia, synthetic aviation fuel, and especially clean hydrogen produced via renewable electrolysis. The company aims to accelerate the global transition to clean fuels for heavy transport, shipping, steel and chemicals, with commercial plants slated for operation from 2025. Avina’s mission is to provide affordable, reliable clean energy, scaling next‑generation fuels worldwide.

providers.name: Beewise
providers.description: Beewise is an agricultural technology company building the BeeHome, an AI- and robotics-enabled beehive that autonomously monitors, cares for, and protects honeybee colonies to reduce colony loss and deliver reliable pollination. Founded to address bee colony collapse, Beewise combines computer vision, robotics, and cloud software to detect pests and disease, regulate hive climate, and dispatch precision pollination for growers. The company serves growers with guaranteed pollination services, beekeepers with technology-enhanced hive management, and property owners through its Bees for Buildings program. Beewise is a venture-backed company (Insight Partners portfolio) surfaced into the API Evangelist network; it operates a customer grower portal but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: getecoback-com
providers.description: EcoBack provides a comprehensive climate and energy advice platform for households, offering free calculators and honest recommendations for cooling, heating, indoor air quality, and energy savings. The site helps users compare portable air conditioners, dehumidifiers, and heating solutions, and includes tools for heatwave alerts, frost warnings, and energy cost calculations.

providers.name: Greyparrot
providers.description: Greyparrot is a London-based AI waste analytics company that turns materials recovery facilities (MRFs) into data-driven operations. Its Greyparrot Analyzer uses computer-vision cameras mounted over waste conveyor belts to identify, count, and measure the composition of waste streams in real time, giving recyclers continuous visibility into what flows through their plant. The Greyparrot Sync product routes that analytics stream into existing operational control systems, ERP platforms, Power BI dashboards, and OEM sortation hardware (robotic arms, air-jet systems, balers, belt control), while Deepnest turns real-world recovery data into design feedback for packaging brands. Backed by Speedinvest, Greyparrot serves recyclers, equipment manufacturers, and consumer-goods companies working to raise recycling rates and automate compliance reporting. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition; this profile captures its public web, product, and content surface.

providers.name: Highstock
providers.description: Highstock is a private, AI-native wholesale marketplace that connects consumer brands holding excess or unsold inventory with a vetted network of global business buyers. Focused initially on beauty and personal care, the platform lets brands convert surplus stock into cash while protecting brand value and channel privacy, and gives buyers access to authentic inventory directly from brands at exclusive pricing, with centralized order management and flexible payment terms. The company reports 50+ beauty and personal care brands, 100+ wholesale buyers, $100M+ in listed inventory, and more than 1M pounds of product diverted from landfill, with offices in New York (US) and Gurgaon (India). Highstock does not currently publish a public API or developer program; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead for enrichment.

providers.name: ReelData AI
providers.description: ReelData AI builds artificial intelligence software for land-based aquaculture, helping recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) fish farms maximize growth, minimize costs, and reduce risk across smolt, post-smolt, and on-growing production. Its integrated AI suite includes AI Smart Feeding (ReelAppetite), which monitors real-time population appetite to optimize feed and cut waste; AI Biomass Monitoring (ReelWeight), a non-intrusive biomass estimation tool returning results within hours; and AI Cameras (ReelVision), dual-function cameras for fish-behavior monitoring, feed counting, and standard IP camera use. Additional tools cover stress monitoring (ReelStress) and early disease detection (ReelHealth). ReelData is a Techstars portfolio company serving major operators including Samherji, Atlantic Sapphire, Kingfish Company, and Salmon Evolution. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface; its products are delivered as on-site AI hardware and software rather than a self-serve API.

providers.name: Vistra
providers.description: Vistra Corp (NYSE: VST) is an Irving, Texas integrated retail electricity and power generation company and the largest competitive power generator in the United States, operating roughly 41,000-44,000 MW of natural gas, nuclear, coal, solar and battery storage capacity alongside a retail business serving nearly 5 million residential, commercial and industrial customers across 16 states and the District of Columbia through TXU Energy, Dynegy, Ambit Energy, Energy Harbor, Homefield Energy and U.S. Gas & Electric. Its home market is the United States, where it sits on both sides of the competitive value chain, a merchant generator selling into ERCOT, PJM, ISO-NE, NYISO, MISO and CAISO, and a retail electricity provider (REP) reselling that power to end customers. Its API posture is honestly none. No developer portal, no API subdomain and no machine-readable contract of any kind was found: developer., developers., docs., api. and data. on vistracorp.com do not resolve; /developers, /api, /docs, /data, /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /.well-known/openid-configuration all return 404; and TXU Energy's 758-URL sitemap contains no developer or API page. The United States has no consumer energy data mandate. Green Button is an NAESB/NIST ESPI standard adopted voluntarily, and TXU Energy appears on the US Department of Energy's list of "Utilities Committed to Implementing Green Button", a 2012-era commitment list and not evidence of a live endpoint. The only customer-data surface found is Download-My-Data-style export behind the TXU Energy MyAccount login, whose interval readings are themselves sourced from Smart Meter Texas, the shared ERCOT meter-data platform operated by the transmission and distribution utilities (Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, TNMP) rather than by Vistra. Because Vistra is a retailer and generator and not a wires company, the third-party interval-data API in its home Texas market belongs to Smart Meter Texas and not to Vistra. Vistra likewise publishes no open market or grid data of its own; ERCOT, the other ISOs/RTOs and the EIA publish the market data about Vistra's fleet. Both sides are therefore closed at the company boundary. Not to be confused with Vistra Limited (vistra.com), the unrelated corporate-services and fund-administration firm that does run a real API developer portal at devportal.vistra.com.

providers.name: Carbo Culture
providers.description: Carbo Culture is a climate‑tech project developer building patented Carbolysis™ reactors that convert waste biomass into stable biochar, locking carbon away for centuries while generating renewable energy. The company aims to remove 1 billion tonnes of CO₂, offering biochar, carbon credits, and clean energy solutions. Founded in 2018, backed by True‑Ventures, it operates from Helsinki, Finland, and collaborates with industry partners to scale its carbon removal platform.

providers.name: CPower, Inc.
providers.description: CPower Energy is a national leader in unlocking the full value of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs). It provides a virtual power plant platform that enables energy users across the United States to save on energy costs, balance the grid, and achieve clean energy goals. The company offers advanced DER aggregation, real‑time optimization, and analytics to help utilities and large energy consumers manage demand response, peak shaving, and renewable integration. CPower’s solutions are deployed nationwide, supporting a transition to a more resilient and sustainable energy system.

providers.name: Dandelion Energy
providers.description: Dandelion Energy is a residential geothermal heating and cooling company that designs, engineers, and installs ground-source heat pump systems for homeowners and new-home builders. Its systems tap the earth's stable subsurface temperature to heat and cool homes year-round, cutting utility bills and carbon emissions versus conventional fossil-fuel HVAC. Dandelion delivers end-to-end service from ground-loop drilling through turnkey installation, and offers a leasing program that removes the upfront cost for buyers. The company reports thousands of installations across the United States. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), it operates in the frontier-tech and climate sector; it currently exposes no public developer API.

providers.name: Grover
providers.description: Grover is a Berlin-based consumer technology rental and subscription company that lets people rent smartphones, laptops, gaming consoles, cameras, smart home devices, and audio gear on flexible monthly plans ranging from one to twenty-four-plus months. With more than 500,000 active renters across the United States, Germany, Austria, Spain, and the Netherlands, Grover positions flexible tech access as a circular, subscription-based alternative to ownership, refurbishing and recirculating returned devices for resale. Grover is a consumer-facing service and does not currently publish a public developer portal or API; this profile captures its public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Overstory
providers.description: Overstory provides AI-powered vegetation intelligence for electric utilities and grid operators. The platform fuses high-resolution satellite and aerial imagery with machine learning to detect vegetation encroachment, hazard trees, and wildfire risk along power line corridors, helping utilities prioritize trimming, optimize vegetation management spend, and improve grid reliability (SAIDI). Overstory was founded as 20tree.ai and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company. As of this profile the company delivers its intelligence through a customer platform and services rather than a public developer API; no public API documentation, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Sirius
providers.description: beSirius is an Amsterdam-based AI platform for the critical minerals and metals value chain. It builds a continuously verified digital Twin of every supplier, mapping each company's data to the frameworks, questionnaires, and regulations its buyers, auditors, and regulators require - including CSDDD, CMRT/EMRT/AMRT conflict-minerals reporting, EcoVadis, CDP, S&P CSA, UN Global Compact, LME Passport, and the Consolidated Mining Standard Initiative (CMSI). The platform automates supplier due diligence, sustainability and ESG data collection and verification, certification readiness, customer KYC, and ratings improvement across mining, processing, and trading supply chains, reducing manual audit and disclosure effort. beSirius is backed by Techstars and other investors.

providers.name: Alcoa
providers.description: Alcoa Corporation is a global industry leader in bauxite, alumina, and aluminum production. Founded in 1888, Alcoa operates mines, refineries, and smelters across Australia, Brazil, Canada, Iceland, Norway, Saudi Arabia, and the United States. The company is a Fortune 500 member and one of the world's largest aluminum producers, supplying lightweight, high-strength materials to automotive, aerospace, packaging, construction, and industrial markets. Alcoa is committed to sustainability through low-carbon aluminum production, responsible bauxite mining, and advancing aluminum recycling.

providers.name: Cactos
providers.description: Cactos is a Finnish clean-energy company that designs, manufactures, and operates smart battery energy storage systems (BESS) for commercial, industrial, and grid-scale use. Its hardware line (Cactos Mylo commercial storage and Cactos Cardo backup power, built in part from second-life Tesla EV batteries) is paired with Cactos Spine, a cloud software platform that optimizes each unit for load shifting, peak shaving, demand-charge reduction, solar self-consumption, backup power during outages, and participation in electricity and grid-balancing markets. Cactos serves logistics, manufacturing, EV charging, agriculture, real estate, and commercial-property operators. It is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. As of this profile, Cactos publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation; the Cactos Spine app at app.cactos.com is a customer-facing management console rather than a documented developer API.

providers.name: Cibotechnologies
providers.description: Cibotechnologies provides a comprehensive platform for agricultural sustainability programs, offering data, modeling, reporting, and API integration to help agribusinesses, biofuel producers, governments, and nonprofits manage and scale their environmental initiatives. Their solutions include program management, impact modeling, data APIs, trusted advisor networks, and incentive stacking, enabling real‑time visibility and compliance across millions of acres.

providers.name: Hithium
providers.description: HiTHIUM (Xiamen Hithium Energy Storage Technology Co., Ltd.) is a Chinese energy storage company founded in 2019 that designs and manufactures lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, modules and complete battery energy storage systems (BESS) for utility-scale, commercial and industrial, and residential applications. The product line runs from large-format prismatic ESS cells through liquid-cooled multi-megawatt-hour container systems to the HeroEE residential and portable range marketed at hero-ee.com. Company material reports roughly 8,000 staff, more than 1,100 R&D engineers and over 3,900 patents. Product pages publish named certifications including UL 1973, UL 9540, UL 9540A, NFPA 855, IEC 62619, IEC 62477, IEC 63056, IEC 61000 and UN 38.3. HiTHIUM operates a Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) running an IEC 62443-aligned vulnerability management process, and publishes numbered cybersecurity bulletins with CVE references and remediation guidance at hithium.com/support/security.html. HiTHIUM publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL or Postman contract, no SDKs, no CLI, no webhook catalog and no MCP or A2A agent surface; third-party integration happens over Modbus/CAN interfaces described in datasheets and manuals that sit behind the download-center account gate, and the HeroEE consumer app's backend is undocumented.

providers.name: Last Energy
providers.description: Last Energy is an American developer and operator of micro-modular nuclear power plants, founded in 2019 in Washington, D.C. by Bret Kugelmass as a commercial spinout of the Energy Impact Center. Its flagship PWR-20 is a 20 MWe pressurized water reactor assembled from a few dozen factory-made, steel-encased modules that ship to site and are installed rather than constructed in place. Last Energy sells power rather than reactors: it designs, finances, owns and operates plants under long-term power purchase agreements for energy-intensive customers including data centers, metals, chemicals, cement, pulp and paper, and food and beverage. The company has announced projects in Texas, South Wales, Poland and Romania, entered nuclear site licensing in the United Kingdom, partnered with Texas A&M and DP World, and raised roughly $164M across a $40M Series B and a $100M Series C. Last Energy publishes a marketing site and a gated customer/whitepaper portal, but no public developer program, API, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Matsmart
providers.description: Matsmart (operating internationally as Motatos) is a Swedish e-commerce company that fights food waste by selling surplus, short-dated, and overstocked groceries and household goods at a discount, with average savings of up to 50%. Its catalog spans pantry staples, beverages, snacks, candy, baby food, health and beauty, cleaning supplies, pet food, and non-food surplus, sourced from manufacturers and retailers and shipped across Sweden and other European markets via partners including Bring, Airmee, and PostNord. The company runs a consumer web storefront and iOS/Android apps. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API or documentation, so this profile captures its public web, security, and identity surface.

providers.name: Mill
providers.description: Mill is a consumer sustainability company that makes a smart kitchen bin which dries and grinds household food scraps overnight into dry, nutrient-rich "Food Grounds," keeping food waste out of landfills and cutting the methane it would otherwise produce. Sold as a membership starting around $799 or roughly $66/month, the bin is odorless, reduces food-waste volume by about 80%, and the resulting grounds are reused in gardens, as chicken feed, or through farm partnerships. Mill also runs a commercial line for grocery, offices, food service, and municipalities. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), Mill is a consumer hardware and subscription business with a companion mobile app; it exposes no public developer API — its /api/ path is an internal app backend disallowed in robots.txt.

providers.name: Presso
providers.description: Presso is a garment-care automation company (operated by parent LaundrySucks.io Inc.) that builds robotic, AI-driven systems for dry cleaning and laundry businesses. Its flagship AirTouch product is a compact, plug-and-play unit that runs on a standard 110V outlet and combines automatic fabric recognition, built-in non-toxic cleaning formulas, and smart temperature control to deliver same-day wash, fold, and dry cleaning under one roof. Presso positions itself around faster, greener, and gentler garment care without compressors, boilers, or skilled labor. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass Presso publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API surface — it is a hardware/robotics and equipment business, not an API provider.

providers.name: Bevi
providers.description: Bevi is a smart beverage-dispenser company that manufactures connected, filtered-water machines for offices and commercial spaces. Its IoT-enabled Standup and Countertop dispensers deliver still and sparkling water plus dozens of fruit flavors and functional enhancements (vitamins, electrolytes, energy, focus), connect directly to a building's water supply, and track plastic bottles saved in real time. Bevi is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Techstars, and Trinity Ventures. No public developer API surface (OpenAPI, docs, or developer portal) was found during enrichment; this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Cheaf
providers.description: Cheaf is a mobile food-rescue marketplace that connects supermarkets, restaurants, bakeries, and food retailers holding surplus inventory with consumers who buy it as discounted "surprise packages" at pickup, cutting food waste while helping merchants recover value on stock that would otherwise be thrown away. Founded in Mexico in 2020, the consumer app operates across Mexico, Chile, and Argentina, has more than 3.5 million users, and reports millions of kilograms of food rescued and greenhouse-gas emissions avoided. Businesses list surplus through a merchant onboarding portal and pay a commission on sales; consumers browse and reserve packages through the mobile app. This API Evangelist profile tracks Cheaf's public web and developer surface; Cheaf is a consumer/merchant mobile platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation.

providers.name: Cleancult
providers.description: Cleancult provides eco‑friendly cleaning products delivered in refillable containers, aiming to reduce single‑use plastic waste. Their mission emphasizes sustainability, refill culture, and a cleaner lifestyle, offering detergents, soaps, and other household cleaners through a subscription model.

providers.name: Cleancult2
providers.description: Cleancult is a sustainable cleaning products company offering refillable, eco‑friendly cleaning solutions for home and personal care. Their mission is to reduce single‑use plastic waste by providing reusable aluminum bottles and paper‑based refills for soaps, detergents, and sprays. The brand emphasizes powerful, chemical‑free formulas, a subscription‑style refill ritual, and a commitment to environmental stewardship, aiming to make clean living both effective and environmentally responsible.

providers.name: Hemster
providers.description: Hemster is a fashion-technology company that modernizes tailoring and garment fit through a digital "Fit Profile" system. Customers create a personalized fit pattern once, then match any garment — new or from their existing closet — to that saved profile so it can be tailored to their perfect fit rather than to a standard size. The platform aims to reduce returns, extend the life of clothing people already own, and remove size-related hesitation at purchase, with a sustainability angle around keeping garments out of landfill. Hemster operates a consumer web app at my.hemster.co and a related returns/deadstock product ((re)vive / byrevive.com). It is backed by Bullpen Capital. As of this profile Hemster publishes no public developer, API, or integration surface; this record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: Junk King
providers.description: Junk King is a professional junk removal and hauling franchise operating across the United States and Canada as part of the Neighborly family of home service brands. Through locally owned and operated locations, Junk King provides full-service junk removal, self-service dumpster rental, and dumpster bag pickup for residential and commercial customers, handling appliance and furniture removal, estate and property cleanouts, construction debris, yard waste, and e-waste. The company emphasizes eco-friendly disposal, recycling, donating, and reusing as much collected material as possible. Junk King offers free estimates, same-day service in many markets, and online, phone, and text-based booking. It is a portfolio company associated with Norwest Venture Partners and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; Junk King publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Material Bank
providers.description: Material Bank is a B2B digital marketplace that lets architects, interior designers, and other design professionals search, sample, and specify building and design materials from 650+ brands across hundreds of categories through a single platform, with free overnight sample delivery. The platform provides project boards, brand collections, sustainability filters (EPDs, CDPH), and a manufacturer portal for brands. Backed by bain-capital-ventures and general-catalyst. This profile was surfaced from a VC portfolio and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; no public developer API surface was found.

providers.name: Roby
providers.description: Roby (Imageous, Inc.) is a Seattle-based building-management software company whose HVAC automation product connects room and space calendars with a building's BMS (building management system) to automatically switch HVAC to an unoccupied/energy-saving mode when spaces are not in use, delivering measured energy savings and extended equipment lifetime for K-12, higher-education, and office facilities without added staff effort. Roby is deployed through building system integrators (ATS, Climatec, Syserco, ABM Systems, Oprizon, NSF-E) and also offers Receptionist and Helpdesk workplace applications. The product uses Auth0-managed authentication with token-based, SSL-only API access, but does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sustaira
providers.description: Sustaira is a modular, AI-powered sustainability and ESG application platform built on a low-code architecture in partnership with Mendix. Customers use Sustaira to run carbon accounting (Scope 1, 2, and 3), ESG disclosure and reporting aligned to CSRD, CDP, PCAF, and SASB, sustainability project and KPI tracking, supply chain data collection, and industry-specific sustainability workflows across construction, finance, logistics, healthcare, and other sectors. Integration into customer systems is handled through web services and APIs on the underlying Mendix platform, plus a marketplace of 150+ sustainability accelerators. Sustaira does not publish a public, self-service developer API portal; integration access is delivered through customer enterprise contracts and partner programs.

providers.name: trawa
providers.description: trawa (operated by Future Energy Services GmbH) is a Berlin-based energy management company that helps mid-sized businesses procure and manage electricity. It pairs AI-optimized green-electricity sourcing on the wholesale market with cloud energy-management software that gives customers real-time visibility into consumption, costs, and CO2 emissions, alongside battery storage and smart control of energy-consuming assets such as CHP plants and charging stations. Founded in 2022, trawa is backed by Balderton Capital and Speedinvest. The platform is delivered through a customer web portal and a trust center; no public developer API was found as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: APA Group
providers.description: APA Group is an Australian Securities Exchange (ASX) listed energy infrastructure business that owns and operates a portfolio of more than $20 billion in assets. It delivers around half of Australia's domestic gas through a 15,000-kilometre network of gas pipelines, alongside gas transmission, processing, compression and storage assets, and generates electricity from gas-powered and renewable assets while owning and operating battery storage and electricity transmission infrastructure. APA does not publish a public developer portal or API documentation on apa.com.au; it was surfaced via the australia-apidays-2026 harvest.

providers.name: Bonnet
providers.description: Bonnet is a UK-based electric vehicle (EV) charging app that aggregates multiple charging networks into a single platform, letting drivers find, access, and pay for chargers across Europe through one membership. Headquartered in Bristol and acquired by OVO Energy, it gives consumers real-time charger status, route planning, membership plans with per-charge savings, and weekly charging-credit rewards, while offering charge point operator (CPO) and fleet solutions with white-label integration for businesses. Surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Bonnet publishes a consumer mobile app but no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Brighte
providers.description: Brighte provides financing solutions for Australian households and businesses to adopt solar panels, green loans, and energy-efficient home improvements. Their platform offers interest‑free payment plans, green loans, personal loans, and various government‑backed schemes to make sustainable energy affordable. By partnering with vendors and offering a portal for customers, Brighte aims to accelerate the transition to renewable energy across Australia, supporting both residential and commercial projects.

providers.name: EnerSys
providers.description: EnerSys is a global leader in stored energy solutions for industrial applications, manufacturing batteries, chargers, accessories, and outdoor equipment enclosures. EnerSys serves motive power, reserve power, aerospace and defense, and specialty markets.
