Systems ship with PLC/SCADA control and a cloud-connected Eco-Insights reporting dashboard for remote monitoring, alarms and utility savings reporting, but Epic Cleantec publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; the data surface is delivered to building owners and operators as a hosted dashboard rather than as a public API.

providers.name: Everdrop
providers.description: Everdrop is a Munich-based direct-to-consumer sustainability brand, founded in 2019, that sells more sustainable everyday household products — cleaning tabs, laundry detergent, dishwasher tablets, washing-up liquid and natural body care — designed around a refill model of concentrated tabs/powders dissolved in reusable bottles to cut single-use plastic, unnecessary chemicals and CO2. The company operates an e-commerce storefront (Shopify/Next.js/Storyblok stack) with a subscription-based refill program, and reports certifications including B Corp, EU Ecolabel and Ecocert. It has no public developer or API program; this profile was surfaced as an HV Capital portfolio company and enriched from Everdrop's public web surface.

providers.name: EVERY Company
providers.description: The EVERY Company (formerly Clara Foods; site now at every.com, redirected from theeverycompany.com) is a foodtech ingredients company that produces animal-free, antibiotic-free egg proteins using precision fermentation. Its flagship OvoPro product replicates the functional properties of conventional eggs — binding, gelling, foaming, and whipping — for food manufacturers making baked goods, frozen foods, pasta, and protein bars, offering kosher, halal, and sustainable ingredients with more consistent pricing and availability than animal-derived eggs. Backed by Prosus Ventures. As a B2B ingredient supplier it publishes no public API or developer surface; this profile captures its identity and domain security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Flashfood
providers.description: Flashfood is a Toronto-based mobile marketplace that connects shoppers with heavily discounted groceries nearing their best-by date at partner grocery stores across the United States and Canada. Through its iOS and Android apps, shoppers browse deals of up to 50% off on fresh produce, meat, dairy, and packaged goods, pay in-app, and pick the items up at a dedicated Flashfood Zone in-store. By routing surplus food away from landfills and onto dinner tables, the company reduces grocery-retail food waste while helping families save on their grocery bills. Flashfood is a consumer-facing app and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web, legal, and security surface.

providers.name: Forward Earth
providers.description: Forward Earth is a Berlin-based climate technology company building AI-automated carbon management software that helps businesses measure, track, and reduce their carbon footprint in line with environmental regulation. Its platform covers Corporate Carbon Footprint (CCF) accounting certified to the GHG Protocol, Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) calculation, and Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) compliance reporting, with an emphasis on automating data collection and emissions calculation to save time and cost. Forward Earth also offers a white-label / partner offering that embeds its carbon management capabilities into GRC, ESG, supply-chain, and consultancy software, exposing environmental and partner-specific APIs plus single sign-on through a sandbox that partners access on request. The company is backed by Speedinvest and is moving toward agent-native product carbon footprinting.

providers.name: Gourmey
providers.description: Gourmey is a Paris-based cultivated meat company producing sustainable, cell-cultured meat delights — starting with cultivated foie gras — for an uncompromising and conscious generation. Founded in France and backed by Partech and Point Nine, Gourmey grows real meat directly from animal cells without raising or slaughtering animals, aiming for a lower environmental footprint across the food and agritech sectors. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio company profile; Gourmey operates a consumer and corporate website but does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Martie
providers.description: Martie is a woman-owned, San Francisco-based online discount grocery marketplace founded in 2021 to fight food waste and make quality goods accessible and affordable. Martie works directly with brands on their overstock, surplus, seasonal, and old-packaging inventory — pantry staples, beauty, and household goods — and resells it to consumers at up to 80% off retail with no membership or subscription required. Shoppers browse daily deals through the martie.com website or the Martie iOS and Android apps. The company reports having diverted over five million pounds of food from landfill since launch. Martie is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand (a Shopify-hosted storefront) and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, or documentation surface; this profile was surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and enriched with company identity plus a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Mission Barns
providers.description: Mission Barns is a Berkeley, California cultivated-meat company founded in 2018 that grows real animal fat from cells to make animal-friendly pork products — including meatballs, bacon, pepperoni, chorizo, and sausage — built on Mission Fat, its proprietary cultivated pork fat. It is the first company to receive both FDA and USDA clearance for cultivated fat and operates a dual B2C consumer-brand and B2B ingredient / co-development model across foodservice and CPG partners. This API Evangelist profile is a portfolio-company lead (backed by Point Nine); the company runs a consumer marketing site and publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Momox
providers.description: momox SE (formerly Momox AG / Momox GmbH) is a Berlin-based re-commerce company founded by Christian Wegner in 2004 — the name stands for "Moderner Medien Online Express-Ankauf" (Modern Media Online Express Purchase). Through momox.de it buys used books, CDs, DVDs/Blu-rays and games from private sellers at fixed prices in Germany, Austria, France, Belgium and the UK, reselling them via its Medimops shop and third-party marketplaces. Its momox fashion arm (formerly ubup.com, momoxfashion.com) does the same for second-hand clothing, shoes and accessories. momox runs large logistics centres in Berlin, Leipzig and Neuenhagen bei Berlin and has handled more than 350 million articles since founding. momox is a consumer-facing re-commerce operation; it publishes no official public developer program, API portal, or SDKs. The only machine surface is an internal, undocumented mobile-app pricing endpoint (api.momox.de / api.momox.fr) that is not offered as a first-party API.

providers.name: NCX
providers.description: NCX (Natural Capital Exchange), originally founded as SilviaTerra, is a forestry technology company that maps and measures every acre of U.S. forestland using satellite imagery and machine learning. NCX built the Natural Capital Exchange, a marketplace that paid landowners to defer timber harvests and generate forest carbon credits, and it now offers LandBook, a tool that helps landowners capture the story, plans, and practical knowledge behind their property so it can be passed on to the next steward. The company is backed by Union Square Ventures and Version One Ventures.

providers.name: Nexii
providers.description: Nexii is a green construction technology company that designs and manufactures prefabricated wall and roof panel systems for commercial and industrial buildings. Its panels are made from Nexiite, a proprietary low-carbon building material the company says is up to 80% lighter than conventional concrete, and bolt together on site to cut build times by as much as five times while producing near-zero construction waste. Nexii serves retail, residential, warehouse, data center, cold storage, healthcare, office and education verticals, with projects for Starbucks, McDonald's, Pizza Hut, Popeyes, Dutch Bros, Walmart and Marriott. The original Vancouver-based Nexii Building Solutions entered creditor protection in January 2024; Dallas-based 3 Gates acquired its assets in a court-approved sale completed 28 June 2024 and relaunched the business as NEXII, Inc., headquartered in Dallas, Texas with manufacturing in Squamish, British Columbia. Nucor Corporation subsequently made a strategic equity investment. Nexii is a manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Omnitron Sensors
providers.description: Omnitron Sensors designs advanced MEMS (micro electro mechanical systems) sensors using innovative 3D manufacturing techniques, aiming to deliver high-performance, low-cost sensing with major gains in precision and reliability. Its technology targets AI data centers, autonomous systems and vehicles, environmental and climate monitoring, and extended reality (XR) devices. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network, the company is a hardware/semiconductor business with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Orchard Labs
providers.description: Orchard Labs Inc. is a Toronto-based e-commerce company, founded in 2013, that buys, refurbishes, and resells pre-owned and certified-refurbished smartphones, tablets, and accessories across North America. Through its consumer website and mobile app, Orchard lets people test, price, and sell their used iPhones and Android devices, and buy thoroughly tested refurbished devices backed by a 90-day no-questions-asked warranty and carbon-neutral shipping. It is a consumer retail brand with no public API, developer portal, or SDKs. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: PierSight Space
providers.description: PierSight Space is an India-based space technology company building a constellation of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Automatic Identification System (AIS) satellites for persistent, all-weather maritime surveillance of the world's oceans. Founded by former ISRO engineer Gaurav Seth, PierSight delivers near-real-time ocean monitoring (targeting ~30-minute data latency and 100% ocean coverage) to detect illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing, monitor oil spills, protect Exclusive Economic Zones, support maritime insurance risk assessment, and improve shipping operations. The company has raised roughly $8M from investors including Alpha Wave Ventures, Elevation Capital, and Techstars. As of this enrichment pass PierSight sells data solutions to enterprise and government clients and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Polymateria
providers.description: Polymateria Ltd is a British materials-science company, based at the Imperial College I-HUB on the White City Campus in London, that develops Biotransformation — a masterbatch additive blended into polyethylene and polypropylene at roughly 2% by weight so that plastic which escapes a waste stream weathers into a bioavailable wax and fully biodegrades in the open environment without leaving microplastics behind. The company co-authored BSI PAS 9017, the first standard for measuring the biodegradability of polyolefins, is a World Economic Forum Technology Pioneer and a Terra Carta signatory, and sells to converters, brand owners and packaging manufacturers rather than to developers. Its product is a chemical additive, not software: the public website is a WordPress marketing and media site, and the only credentialed surface it operates is a customer portal that serves third-party test datasets as documents. No developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract of any kind was found in this pass.

providers.name: Rabbit Mobility
providers.description: Rabbit Mobility (Rabbit) is a clean-tech micro-mobility sharing company operating in Cairo and Giza, Egypt. Through its iOS and Android mobile apps, Rabbit offers shared standing electric scooters and electric bikes with two service models: on-demand "Unlock & Go" rides and multi-day "Day Rentals" that include delivery. The company reports covering more than one million kilometers and saving over 50 tons of CO2 emissions. Rabbit is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As a consumer mobile-app business, Rabbit publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation at this time; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: Raus
providers.description: Raus (operated by StayRaus GmbH, Berlin) is a consumer platform for booking sustainable, design-forward tiny cabins in nature across Germany and Austria, giving city dwellers a quick escape "close to home." Guests browse and book fully-equipped smart cabins in forests, by lakes, and on farms, add culinary experiences and extras, buy gift cards, and can list their own land as a host. Raus was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a B2C hospitality/booking brand with a public consumer website but no publicly documented API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Renoster Systems
providers.description: Renoster Systems is a carbon-credit ratings agency bringing deep transparency to the nature-based voluntary carbon markets. Using remote sensing, LiDAR, satellite data, and machine learning, Renoster independently rates forestry and other nature-based carbon offset projects, quantifying how much CO2 per credit a project has actually sequestered, and publishes public tools such as its Mercury project database and Renoster/Mercury rubric for researchers, reserve managers, policymakers, and corporate buyers. Renoster is a Techstars-backed startup. As of this profile the company does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface; this record captures its company identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Senken
providers.description: Senken (Senken GmbH, Berlin) is a carbon credit procurement marketplace and advisory for European enterprises. It curates high-integrity carbon credits by scoring climate projects across 600+ data points with its Sustainability Integrity Index (SII), aligned to the Oxford Offsetting Principles and ICVCM Core Carbon Principles, rejecting roughly 95% of available credits. Products span advisory (CSRD, SBTi, CDP compliance), vetted procurement, audit-ready documentation (Champion's Kit), the SBTi 2035 Reserve carbon-removal supply, an OER portfolio, and free self-serve tools at tools.senken.io (checkout, portfolio calculator, OER calculator, EU greenwashing auditor). Clients include Vodafone, Deutsche Telekom, DZ Bank, and Union Investment. No public developer API is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: SkenarioLabs
providers.description: SkenarioLabs is a Helsinki-based real estate finance data intelligence company (founded 2015) that turns fragmented building data into auditable, asset-level intelligence for European banks and financial institutions. From a single address it reconstructs complete building profiles covering automated valuation, climate and transition risk, energy performance, technical condition, and renovation potential — aligned with CRREM, EU Taxonomy, ECB, EBA, CRR3, MEPS, and SFDR frameworks. It serves 200+ institutional clients monitoring over 60 billion euros of collateral and scores more than one million assets monthly. SkenarioLabs delivers its intelligence ad hoc into loan origination, portfolio audit, and continuous risk-monitoring workflows rather than through a public self-serve developer API.

providers.name: Spire Global
providers.description: Spire Global operates a constellation of more than 100 LEMUR nanosatellites collecting maritime AIS, aviation ADS-B, GNSS-RO weather profiles, and RF geolocation data, and offers Space Services for hosted payloads and managed satellite missions. Its data products are exposed as developer-friendly APIs: Spire Maritime 2.0 (now operated by Kpler) delivers vessel-tracking AIS through a GraphQL endpoint; Spire Aviation publishes REST APIs and real-time streams for flight metadata, live ADS-B tracking, historic positions, and event feeds; Spire Weather and Climate provides RESTful weather and ocean data APIs including 30 years of maritime weather history; and Spire Space Services exposes a developer portal for managed satellite operations. Spire's APIs are documented at product-specific subdomains and authenticated with API keys.

providers.name: Stockeld Dreamery
providers.description: Stockeld Dreamery is a Swedish food-tech company founded in Stockholm in early 2019 by Sorosh Tavakoli (previously founder of the video-advertising company Videoplaza) to reinvent animal-based staples as plant-based alternatives, starting with cheese. The company develops and manufactures fermented, legume-based cultured cheese products — including a cream cheese and a melting cheese aimed at foodservice — as a sustainable substitute for dairy. Backed by venture investors including Creandum and Northzone, Stockeld Dreamery operates as a consumer packaged-goods brand and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: StoreDot
providers.description: StoreDot is an Israeli battery technology company founded in 2012 by Doron Myersdorf, Simon Litsyn and Gil Rosenman, headquartered in Herzliya with an advanced technology campus in Irvine, California. It develops extreme fast charging (XFC) lithium-ion cells built on proprietary silicon-dominant anode chemistry and synthesized organic and inorganic compounds optimized with machine-learning models, targeting the range and charging anxiety that gate mainstream electric-vehicle adoption. Its "100inX" product roadmap sets 100 miles of range charged in 5 minutes (100in5, 2024), 3 minutes (100in3, 2028) and 2 minutes (100in2, 2032); the company has demonstrated pouch and prismatic XFC cells sustaining more than 1,000 and later 2,000 extreme fast charging cycles while retaining over 80 percent of original capacity, and designs its chemistry to drop into existing Li-ion production lines. Strategic investors and partners include Daimler/Mercedes-Benz, BP, VinFast, Volvo, Polestar, Ola Electric, Samsung Ventures, TDK and manufacturing partner EVE Energy. In 2026 a planned SPAC merger with Andretti Acquisition Corp. II was terminated and the company returned to private fundraising. StoreDot is a hardware, materials and cell-manufacturing business: it publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server or machine-readable API contract, and no /.well-known/ discovery surface, llms.txt or developer subdomain resolves on store-dot.com.

providers.name: The Modern Milkman
providers.description: The Modern Milkman is a UK doorstep delivery service that brings farm-fresh milk, groceries and household essentials to customers in returnable and reusable glass bottles or recyclable packaging, with flexible ordering and early-morning delivery. Founded to modernise the traditional milkround, the company focuses on reducing food waste and single-use plastic through a return-and-reuse model, local sourcing, and a subscription-style ordering experience delivered through its website and mobile apps. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company publishes no public developer API, but does maintain an llms.txt for AI agents, a customer help centre, and a blog. Sector: consumer / direct-to-consumer grocery delivery.

providers.name: WINT
providers.description: WINT (also styled Wint) is an AI-powered water management and leak-detection platform for commercial and industrial facilities. Its IoT flow sensors, automated shut-off valves, and 24/7 staffed monitoring center use signal processing and anomaly detection to catch leaks in real time across main feeds, domestic cold and hot water, HVAC loops, cooling towers, and irrigation systems, reporting 20-25% average water-consumption reduction and up to 90% less water damage and insurance loss. WINT is backed by Insight Partners and carries NSF International, ISO, and USGBC affiliations. During enrichment no public developer API, documentation, well-known discovery surface, OpenAPI, or SDK was found; this profile captures the company's public web properties and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: World View
providers.description: World View (World View Enterprises) is a Tucson, Arizona-based stratospheric balloon company focused on remote sensing and persistent intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR). Its uncrewed high-altitude balloons carry EO/FMV, IR, SAR, and hyperspectral sensors for defense, government, and commercial missions. Acquired by Ondas Holdings in 2026, it now operates as part of the Ondas Sentinel multi-domain intelligence platform, with partnerships including Palantir and Sierra Nevada Corporation. World View publishes no public developer program or API.

providers.name: 5B Australia
providers.description: 5B is an Australian cleantech manufacturer that builds prefabricated, pre-wired ground-mount solar technology for utility-scale, mining, industrial and remote-community power projects. Founded in Sydney in 2013 by solar engineers Chris McGrath and Eden Tehan, the company designs and manufactures the 5B Maverick, an accordion-folded east-west solar array that is assembled in a factory and unfolded on site in under an hour rather than built panel by panel, cutting on-site labour by roughly 80% and roughly doubling energy yield per hectare compared with single-axis trackers. 5B manufactures in Adelaide, South Australia, with a global assembly model, and has deployed projects across Australia, the United States, Panama, Puerto Rico, El Salvador and Chile. 5B is a hardware and deployment-services company: as of this profile it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: Aalo Atomics
providers.description: Aalo Atomics is an Austin, Texas-based advanced nuclear engineering company, founded in 2021, working to make reactor deployment fast, repeatable, and economical through factory manufacturing. It is developing the Aalo-1, a factory-fabricated sodium-cooled microreactor (~10 MWe class), and Aalo Pod power plants that combine five Aalo-1 reactors to deliver roughly 50 megawatts of electricity for data centers, industrial facilities, and communities. The company describes a new XMR ("extra modular reactor") category, has raised a $100M Series B, and is advancing through U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission pre-application activities and a U.S. Department of Energy experimental microreactor site in Idaho. This API Evangelist profile tracks Aalo Atomics as a company in the network; the company does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Advano
providers.description: Advano is a New Orleans, Louisiana battery-materials company that develops silicon-based anode materials for lithium-ion batteries. Spun out of Tulane University in 2016 and backed by 25+ patents, its flagship REALSi silicon-carbon composite is engineered as a drop-in replacement for graphite anodes, delivering up to 9x the energy density of graphite for electric vehicles, consumer electronics, defense, and grid energy storage. Advano's process avoids hazardous silane gas, uses abundant metallurgical-grade silicon, and runs on existing manufacturing equipment. The company operates a pilot plant in New Orleans East and is scaling toward 3,000 tons of REALSi in 2026 and 20,000 tons by 2030. This is a physical deep-tech manufacturer with no public API or developer platform; it is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a VC portfolio company profile.

providers.name: Aerem
providers.description: Aerem is a Mumbai-based "FinTech for CleanTech" group that finances, supplies and monitors rooftop solar in India. The group comprises Aerem Solutions Private Limited, NetZero Finance Private Limited — an RBI-licensed, solar-focused NBFC — and Sunstore Solar Private Limited. Aerem underwrites collateral-free rooftop solar loans for MSMEs and homeowners, provides supply chain finance to solar EPC installers, runs the SunStore B2B solar equipment marketplace, and operates AeROC, an inverter-agnostic remote monitoring portal for installed plants. It also ships two mobile products — the Aerem App for borrowers and the Aerem Partner App for installers — and an AAA (Aerem Asset Assurance) quality-certification programme for EPCs. Aerem publishes a machine-readable llms.txt and five first-party npm packages, but no public API, developer portal or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Aiko Solar
providers.description: Aiko Solar (Zhejiang Aiko Solar Energy Co.) is a solar photovoltaic manufacturer specializing in high-efficiency solar cells and modules, best known for its ABC (All Back Contact) module technology for residential, commercial, industrial, and utility-scale applications. A BloombergNEF Tier 1 manufacturer, the company reports 200 GW+ accumulative cell and module shipments and mass-production cell efficiency around 25%. This is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer or API surface; the profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Amogy
providers.description: Amogy is an energy-technology company decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors by converting energy-dense ammonia into dispatchable, zero-carbon electricity. Its AMMDrive power systems crack ammonia into hydrogen and nitrogen and convert the hydrogen to power for data centers, industrial facilities, microgrids, and maritime vessels, and it develops proprietary low-temperature ammonia-cracking catalysts. Backed by DCVC and other investors, Amogy has demonstrated the world's first carbon-free ammonia-powered maritime vessel and partners with firms such as Samsung Heavy Industries and Mitsubishi. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Amogy publishes no public developer API surface at this time, so this record captures its corporate identity and public web properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Black Sheep Foods
providers.description: Black Sheep Foods is a San Francisco food-technology company making plant-based meat that targets the flavors and textures of premium and heritage animal proteins — starting with its signature meat-free lamb, plus steak bites, built on a proprietary pea-protein DualTexture blend. Originally launched as a restaurant and retail brand (served at Bay Area restaurants and sold as vegan ground lamb), the company has increasingly positioned itself as a B2B ingredient supplier, licensing its DualTexture protein platform for hybrid and fully plant-based meat products. It is venture-backed (investors include Bessemer Venture Partners and AgFunder) and pitches a sustainability story of far lower land, water, and greenhouse-gas footprint than conventionally raised lamb. This is a consumer/ ingredient food-tech business with no first-party public developer API; its web presence runs on Shopify.

providers.name: Bolt.Earth
providers.description: Bolt.Earth operates what it describes as India's largest EV charging network, with more than 100,000 charging points deployed across 2,100+ cities. The company sells EV charging hardware (3.3kW smart sockets for 2/3/4-wheelers, AC chargers from 7.4kW to 22kW, and DC fast chargers from 30kW to 240kW) alongside a Charging Management System (CMS) for operators and a consumer mobile app for locating, booking, and paying for charging sessions. Services span site assessment, installation, KYC onboarding, charger activation, remote firmware updates, and 24/7 support for individuals, RWAs, enterprises, fleet operators, hospitality venues, highways, and government agencies. Bolt.Earth is backed by Version One Ventures and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as an energy-sector company profile. No public developer API portal or OpenAPI definition was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Capstone Turbine
providers.description: Capstone Turbine Corporation, now operating as Capstone Green Energy (and its operating entity Capstone Energy+), is a California-based manufacturer of low-emission microturbine energy systems founded in 1988. The company designs and builds oil-free, air-bearing microturbines ranging from 65 kW to multi-megawatt configurations for on-site and on-demand power, combined heat and power (CHP), and combined cooling, heat and power (CCHP). Its systems power data centers, microgrids, ports, EV charging, oil and gas operations, critical power, and renewable energy applications. Capstone was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. It is an industrial energy manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures company identity and public web properties only.

providers.name: CEEZER
providers.description: CEEZER (CEEZER Software GmbH) is a Berlin-based climate-tech enterprise platform for the procurement and portfolio management of carbon credits, Energy Attribute Certificates (EACs), and Sustainable Aviation Fuel Certificates (SAFc). The platform gives corporate sustainability teams access to a marketplace of more than 10,000 global carbon projects with transparent pricing and volume data, a proprietary risk-assessment engine ("Prism") that evaluates hundreds of validated data points per project, and audit-ready reporting for net-zero and decarbonization commitments. CEEZER combines expert climate advisory with enterprise-grade technology to help buyers plan, procure, and manage climate performance assets. Surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and added to the API Evangelist network; the company operates a customer-facing web application but does not publish a public developer API or documentation at this time.

providers.name: Ceibo
providers.description: Ceibo is a Chilean copper technology company accelerating access to copper supply through a proprietary leaching process that recovers copper from primary sulfide ores. Backed by Khosla Ventures and BHP Ventures, the company positions its on-site technology as faster than bioleaching, using less water than concentration and a fraction of the capital expenditure of concentrators, aiming to close the global copper supply-demand gap needed for the energy transition. Headquartered in Santiago, Chile, Ceibo was named a 2026 Fast Company World Changing Ideas winner. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Ceibo publishes no public developer/API surface at this time.

providers.name: Choose Energy
providers.description: Choose Energy is a free online energy marketplace, founded in 2008 and operated by Red Ventures, that helps consumers and businesses in deregulated U.S. energy markets compare electricity and natural gas plans, view transparent all-inclusive pricing, and switch providers online in minutes. The platform serves customers across Texas, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Illinois, New Jersey, New York, Maryland, Massachusetts, Connecticut, and other deregulated states, and also offers solar cost estimation, business energy procurement, and educational energy resources. Choose Energy is a consumer-facing web marketplace and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: E-Peas
providers.description: e-peas is a Belgian fabless semiconductor company founded in 2014 in Louvain-la-Neuve that designs power management integrated circuits (PMICs) for energy harvesting, enabling battery-free and battery-assisted IoT devices to power themselves from ambient energy. Its flagship Ambient Energy Manager (AEM) family harvests from photovoltaic (light), thermal, vibration/piezoelectric, radio-frequency, and hybrid multi-source inputs, and the company also develops ultra-low-power microcontrollers for autonomous data acquisition. e-peas positions itself as a pioneer of the "Ambient IoT" concept serving smart buildings, industrial IoT, consumer electronics, and wearables, with an ecosystem of 30+ partners including Panasonic, TDK, Vishay, and Silicon Labs. This is a hardware/silicon company that does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: ecoplanet
providers.description: ecoplanet provides cloud-based, integrated energy management software for German mid-market companies. The platform combines three core functions: real-time consumption monitoring through meter integration with AI-powered anomaly detection and automated load-shifting on price signals; strategic energy procurement using algorithmic purchasing across spot markets, tranches, and power purchase agreements (PPAs); and automated ISO 50001 compliance documentation. The company reports customers achieve up to 15% consumption savings and ~13.9% average price advantages on energy purchases. Backed by EQT Ventures and HV Capital. No public developer/API surface was found at the time of profiling.

providers.name: Enertiv
providers.description: Enertiv is a commercial real estate sustainability and decarbonization technology company serving owners and operators of large CRE portfolios. Its platform combines portfolio-scale utility data collection and ESG reporting (Report), asset-specific carbon planning that pairs AI recommendations with on-site equipment surveys (Decarbonize), and real-time monitoring with fault detection and operational optimization (Optimize). Additional workflow tools cover automated tenant utility billing and maintenance/work-order management, with integrations into property management systems such as Yardi and MRI. The company guarantees 100% utility data coverage — including tenant-controlled utilities — and has worked with 100+ large portfolios over more than fifteen years.

providers.name: Enpal
providers.description: Enpal is a Berlin-based residential clean-energy company and one of Germany's market leaders in home solar. It sells and finances complete home energy systems — rooftop solar PV, battery storage, air-to-water heat pumps, EV wallbox chargers, and a dynamic electricity tariff — orchestrated by its Enpal.One+ smart energy-management platform, with flexible purchase and zero-down financing options. Enpal serves over 130,000 German households and operates business (business.enpal.de) and installer partner (enpal.pro) channels alongside its consumer offering. Backed by HV Capital and the SoftBank Vision Fund. This API Evangelist profile was created from a VC-portfolio lead; Enpal publishes a consumer website and customer portal but no public developer API surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Enter
providers.description: Enter is a Berlin-based residential energy-efficiency company that positions itself as Germany's largest energy advisor, combining on-site building analysis with installation of heat pumps, photovoltaic (solar) systems, battery storage, EV wallboxes, and home energy-management systems. It guides homeowners through energy consulting, subsidy (Foerderung) applications, and financing, and reports 37,000+ completed projects and 150M+ EUR in secured subsidies. Enter is a B2C service provider with no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs; it was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

providers.name: Essity
providers.description: Essity is a Swedish-headquartered global hygiene and health company operating across four business areas: Health & Medical, Personal Care, Consumer Tissue, and Professional Hygiene. The company is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (ESSITY) and owns roughly 40 brands including TENA (incontinence care), Tork (professional hygiene), Libero (baby diapers), Libresse / Bodyform / Nana / Saba / Nuvenia / Libra (feminine care), Modibodi and Knix (period underwear), JOBST (compression hosiery), Leukoplast (adhesive bandages), Cutimed, Sorbact, Hydrofera and Actimove (wound care, sports medicine, orthopedic supports), Delta-Cast (casting), and consumer tissue brands Lotus, Zewa, Tempo, Cushelle, Plenty, Velvet, Regio, Sorbent and Purex. No public developer-facing APIs or developer portal have been identified for Essity; this repository tracks corporate, brand, sustainability, investor, and integration surfaces for ongoing API discovery. The company's Tork brand ships a connected washroom data platform — Tork Vision Cleaning — which is the closest thing to a public data surface in the portfolio.

providers.name: Explomar
providers.description: ExploMar (Changshu, China) designs and manufactures high-power fully-electric outboard propulsion systems for boats, ranging from 70HP to 1200HP. Its product line spans lightweight axial-flux electric outboard motors, high-density marine batteries for long-range and wide-temperature operation, the Smart Captain integrated control system with 200+ diagnostic capabilities, and 5S energy/charging stations (7kW portable through 120kW dual-gun). ExploMar markets an eco-friendly, high-performance alternative to combustion marine propulsion and exhibits at international yachting festivals (Cannes, Monaco, Interboot, Polboat). Backed by DCM Ventures; surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. Note: ExploMar is a marine hardware manufacturer and publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time — this profile carries identity and web-property signals only.

providers.name: Exporo
providers.description: Exporo is a Hamburg, Germany-based digital investment platform for real estate and renewable-energy infrastructure, operating as a regulated European Crowdfunding Service Provider (ECSP). The platform lets private investors participate in residential and commercial property development as well as clean-energy projects such as solar, with typical terms of 12-36 months. Exporo has mediated over EUR 1.17 billion of capital across more than 600 financed projects, and also offers Club Deals for larger qualified investors. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API or developer portal is currently published; this profile is maintained as a company lead and will be enriched if a developer surface appears.

providers.name: Fazla Gida
providers.description: Fazla (formerly Fazla Gida / Whole Surplus) is a Turkish technology-driven waste management and circular-economy company founded in 2017 in Istanbul. Its digital, decision-support platform helps B2B clients across the supply chain — manufacturers, retailers, e-commerce, distributors, HoReCa, food banks and municipalities — prevent waste at the source and recover value from surplus inventory through a food-recovery hierarchy of secondary-sales marketplace, donation, animal-feed conversion and recycling modules, backed by logistics support, a smart-scale IoT inventory system and an AI analysis tool that reports financial, CO2 and social impact. The company operates the Fazla Iyi surprise-box consumer app, is the first B Corp-certified waste-management organization in Turkey, and is backed by 500 Global among other investors.

providers.name: Forum Mobility
providers.description: Forum Mobility develops, owns, and operates zero-emission heavy-duty trucking infrastructure, bundling electric Class 8 truck leases with charging subscriptions for a single monthly price so freight carriers of every size can electrify without upfront capital. The company builds and runs a network of charging depots — anchored by its flagship FM Harbor site at the Port of Long Beach (44 ports, 360KW fast chargers, 9MW capacity) — with additional depots in development across California and Nevada. Forum Mobility was surfaced as a portfolio company of obvious-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a physical-infrastructure operator with no public developer/API surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: GOOD Meat
providers.description: GOOD Meat is the cultivated-meat division of Eat Just, Inc., a San Francisco food technology company. It grows real chicken from animal cells in production bioreactors rather than by raising and slaughtering birds, and it was the first company in the world cleared to sell cultivated meat to consumers — approved in Singapore in December 2020, then cleared by the U.S. FDA in March 2023 and granted USDA label approval and grant of inspection in June 2023. Its products have been served at 1880 and Huber's Butchery in Singapore and at José Andrés' China Chilcano in Washington, D.C., and in May 2024 it became the first cultivated meat sold at retail. GOOD Meat is a consumer packaged-food and foodservice brand: it sells meat, not software. It operates no developer program, publishes no API, SDK, webhook or machine-readable specification, and its parent's GitHub organization carries no public repositories.

providers.name: Green Fusion
providers.description: Green Fusion GmbH is a Berlin-based climate-energy software company that provides an intelligent 360-degree energy management platform for the residential real estate sector (Wohnungswirtschaft). Its software digitizes and optimizes building heating systems: "Der Energiespar-Pilot" delivers digital boiler-room management and optimized operation of conventional heat sources (gas, oil, district heating, CHP/BHKW), while its AI platform for sector coupling (Sektorkopplung) integrates heat pumps, PV systems, storage, and grid connectivity for intelligent monitoring and control. The platform is TUV-certified under GEG section 71a. Green Fusion is backed by HV Capital and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a climate-energy provider; it operates a customer control platform (control.green-fusion.de) but publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Iontra
providers.description: Iontra Inc. is a Denver, Colorado battery technology company that develops proprietary Charge-Control technology for rechargeable lithium batteries. Founded in 2013 and publicly launched in 2022, Iontra applies electrodynamic sensing and signal processing during charging to suppress lithium plating, dendrite growth and SEI-layer expansion, claiming up to 4x cycle life, 2x faster charging, improved cold-weather charging and better safety without changing cell chemistry. The technology is chemistry agnostic across Li-ion, Li-metal, Li-S, solid-state and Na-ion cells, and is delivered to OEMs as custom charging algorithm "recipes" flashed onto an application-specific microcontroller, or as a software-only library. Iontra closed a $45M Series C led by Volta Energy Technologies to launch an integrated RISC-V charge-control and fuel-gauge MCU. Iontra is an embedded/silicon company: it publishes no public web API, no OpenAPI, and no public SDK packages — its SDK is firmware delivered to OEM customers through a login-gated Document Portal under commercial engagement.

providers.name: Mazama Energy
providers.description: Mazama Energy is a geothermal energy company reinventing power generation with enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) that tap superhot rock to deliver universal, scalable, clean, and affordable electricity. Its Thermal Lattice sequential-stimulation technology improves connectivity between injectors and producers in super hot reservoirs (SHR). The company is developing the Newberry project in Oregon and runs the Mazama EMPOWER program, and is backed by Khosla Ventures. Headquartered in Frisco, Texas.

providers.name: Mesodyne
providers.description: Mesodyne is an MIT-founded engineering and manufacturing company (established 2018) that builds the LightCell, a patented thermophotovoltaic power generator which converts liquid and gaseous fuels — gasoline, diesel, propane, jet fuel, and hydrogen — directly into silent electricity with more than ten times the energy density of batteries. Designed for military, tactical, drone, and off-grid use, it operates day or night across extreme environments with low heat and emissions signatures and no routine maintenance. Mesodyne publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures the company identity and its domain-security posture.

providers.name: Persefoni
providers.description: Persefoni is a climate management and accounting platform (CMAP) used by enterprises and financial institutions to measure, report, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The platform serves more than 9,000 sustainability teams and covers Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions, financed emissions for financial services (PCAF), and disclosures aligned to SBTi, TCFD, CSRD, SEC, and SASB. Persefoni also ships PersefoniAI and the Persefoni Copilot for in-product carbon accounting expertise. An Integration Hub provides pre-built connectors to enterprise systems (AWS, SAP Concur, Expensify, Navan, Google Sheets, Coupa, NetSuite, Stripe, utilities). Persefoni does not publish a fully open, self-service API portal; programmatic access is delivered through customer and partner channels.

providers.name: Reach
providers.description: Reach Power (Reach Labs) is a Y Combinator-backed (S2015) wireless power company building long-range wireless energy distribution networks, aiming to "do for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented, AI-driven power-beaming systems use adaptive metamaterial antennas to steer electromagnetic waves and deliver electricity through the air to multiple devices simultaneously, scaling from microwatts to kilowatts across both mobile and stationary transmitters. Reach serves defense and intelligence, manufacturing and logistics, and public safety markets, powering autonomous vehicles, industrial robotics, sensors, and drones. Partners and customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, NASA, DARPA, the U.S. Army and Air Force, Aisin/Toyota, and Panasonic. The company is headquartered in San Francisco. As of this profile, Reach publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this is a hardware and energy-infrastructure company rather than an API platform.

providers.name: Recyda
providers.description: Recyda is a German software company offering an all-in-one platform for packaging sustainability and regulatory compliance. The platform centralizes packaging data, automates Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) fee calculation and declaration across 20+ countries, and assesses packaging recyclability against standards such as the ZSVR Minimum Standard and EN 18120. It supports EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) compliance, portfolio-wide assessments, and submission-ready reporting, turning weeks of manual compliance work into minutes. Recyda is trusted by global brands and is backed by venture firm Speedinvest.

providers.name: Redwood Materials
providers.description: Redwood Materials is a Carson City, Nevada battery materials company founded in 2017 by former Tesla CTO JB Straubel. It operates a domestic circular supply chain for lithium-ion batteries: collecting and recycling end-of-life EV, consumer, micromobility and stationary-storage batteries, refining the recovered lithium, nickel, cobalt and copper, and remanufacturing anode copper foil and cathode active material for North American cell producers. Through Redwood Energy it also deploys second-life battery energy storage systems for data centers and the grid. Redwood runs the Tahoe Campus in Northern Nevada, the Carolina Campus outside Charleston, South Carolina, and an R&D center in San Francisco, and works with Panasonic, Toyota, GM, BMW, VW/Audi, Rivian, Caterpillar, Isuzu and Lime. Redwood publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK or MCP server; its only machine-facing surface is a gated AWS Cognito partner portal used by automotive dismantlers to price and sell end-of-life battery packs.

providers.name: Sage Geosystems
providers.description: Sage Geosystems is a Houston, Texas energy company developing "Pressure Geothermal" — an evolution of traditional geothermal that applies subsurface breakthroughs from the oil and gas industry to hot dry rock. Its two-well Power Generation system circulates water through engineered "lung" fractures and extracts heat at surface through a heat exchanger driving an sCO2 turbine, while its single-well EarthStore energy storage system charges and discharges over 8-hour to multi-day timescales for long-duration storage. The company markets to utilities, data centers and government partners rather than to developers: as of this profile it operates a seven-page marketing site with no developer portal, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Sakuu
providers.description: Sakuu Corporation is a Silicon Valley advanced-manufacturing company that builds commercial-scale printing equipment for the battery and supercapacitor industries. Founded in 2016 as KeraCel and renamed Sakuu in 2021, it develops the Kavian platform — a dry-process electrode printing system that produces cathodes and anodes without solvents or drying ovens, covering NCA, NCM, LFP, LTO, graphite and silicon-graphite chemistries as well as sodium-ion, aluminum-ion and solid-state formulations. Kavian was named a TIME Best Invention of 2024 and a Fast Company World Changing Idea of 2025, and the Kavian 2000 platform is sold to battery makers serving AI data centers, energy storage, two- and three-wheel mobility, aerospace and industrial electrification. Sakuu sells capital equipment and process technology; it does not operate a software product, a developer program, or any public API.

providers.name: Solaren
providers.description: Solaren is a combination energy and aerospace company headquartered in Manhattan Beach, California, founded in 2001 by a team of satellite engineers and space scientists. Solaren designs, develops, integrates, deploys and operates space solar power (SSP) plants: solar arrays on a patented lightweight solar power satellite in geosynchronous orbit convert sunlight to electricity, convert that electricity to radio-frequency power, and beam it to an earth receiving station that returns it to the grid as baseload power. The company's business model is to own and operate its SSP plants and sell continuous, zero-emission electricity to utility and government customers; it signed the world's first power purchase agreement for space solar electricity, with Pacific Gas & Electric. Solaren is a hardware and energy-generation company and publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: SOLS Energy
providers.description: SOLS Energy is Malaysia's leading residential and commercial solar energy company, on a mission to make green energy a basic human right. It has completed more than 8,900 solar installations across Malaysia spanning residential (Green Homes), commercial (Green Business), and off-grid indigenous community projects (Green Impact), and also offers EV charging (ChargeSingh) and a Solar Academy apprenticeship program. The company is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass SOLS Energy publishes a consumer marketing website (blog, FAQ, contact, privacy and terms pages) but no public developer platform, API, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Swell Energy
providers.description: Swell Energy is a residential clean-energy company that designs, finances, installs, and operates home solar, battery storage, and virtual power plant (VPP) systems for homeowners, businesses, and utilities. Its Swell Compass platform connects to home energy devices to monitor, report, and optimize energy use, and coordinates aggregated distributed batteries into grid services (GridRevenue programs) in partnership with utilities. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, the company operates a consumer web and mobile experience (Compass) rather than a public developer API; no developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documented public API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Swift Charge
providers.description: Swift Charge is an electric vehicle charging company that provides turn-key, fully managed EV charging infrastructure to property owners across the hospitality, education, and multi-family residential sectors, pairing installed charging hardware with a payment application that lets EV drivers locate and pay for charging sessions. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Swift Charge publishes a public marketing and charger-map website but exposes no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal, so this profile is limited to company identity plus a domain-security probe of its website host.

providers.name: Tiger New Energy
providers.description: Tiger New Energy is a Bangladesh-based clean-energy company building a battery-swapping network for electric vehicles, primarily electric rickshaws and motorcycles. Drivers swap depleted lithium batteries for fully charged ones at Tiger swapping stations in seconds instead of waiting to recharge, and a "battery passport" tracks each pack's health and lifecycle. The company operates consumer and partner mobile apps (Tiger Driver, Tiger Partner, Tiger Dealer) on iOS and Android. Tiger New Energy is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; its mobile apps are backed by private, undocumented services.

providers.name: Twelve
providers.description: Twelve is a carbon transformation company that converts CO2, water, and renewable electricity into fuels and chemicals that serve as drop-in replacements for petroleum-based products. Its proprietary eManufacturing technology powers AirPlant One in Moses Lake, Washington, which produces E-Jet sustainable aviation fuel and E-Naphtha, while its eMade program partners with consumer brands on CO2-made materials. Investors include TPG, DCVC, Microsoft, Carbon Direct, Breakout Ventures, and the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. Twelve publishes no public developer API, but its Wix-hosted site exposes an llms.txt and a live site MCP endpoint for agentic access.

providers.name: ZeroAvia
providers.description: ZeroAvia is a UK/US hydrogen-electric aviation company founded in 2017 by Valery Miftakhov, developing hydrogen fuel cell and electric propulsion systems for commercial aircraft. Its powertrain line runs from the ZA600 (600kW, 10-20 seat regional turboprops) through the ZA2000 (2-5MW, 40-80 seat turboprops) to the ZA2000 RJ (5MW+, up to 90 seat regional jets), alongside a component business selling electric propulsion systems, inverters, electric motors and HTPEM/SuperStack fuel cell stacks to other clean-aviation manufacturers, plus a hydrogen airport refuelling ecosystem of electrolyzers, mobile refuelers and LH2 development. It operates from Cotswold Airport in Kemble, UK and from Everett, Washington, and holds FAA and CAA experimental certificates for its flight-test aircraft. ZeroAvia sells certified aerospace hardware to airframers, airlines, lessors and defense customers; it publishes no public developer API, SDK or developer portal.

providers.name: Astroscale
providers.description: Astroscale provides on‑orbit servicing and space sustainability solutions, offering end‑to‑end services such as mission licensing, spectrum acquisition, insurance, and operations for debris removal and satellite life‑extension. The company aims to accelerate space development while ensuring long‑term orbital sustainability for future generations.

providers.name: Avathon
providers.description: Avathon — formerly SparkCognition, rebranded in November 2024 — is an industrial AI company whose Industrial AI Platform combines a data platform, industrial digital twin, AI modeling and application development layers to bring predictive maintenance, asset performance management, visual intelligence and autonomy to physical operations. Its solutions span renewables, oil and gas, power and utilities, manufacturing, mining, aerospace and defense, maritime, rail, aviation, logistics, warehousing and retail, with named offerings including Asset Performance Management, Visual AI / Visual Intelligence, Autonomy for Health, Safety and Environment, the Digital Maintenance Advisor and the Multidomain Awareness Advisor. The platform is sold and delivered as an enterprise engagement — marketing material references an application development SDK and APIs, but no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification is published; the only documentation surface, support.avathon.com/help, redirects to a HubSpot member login. Avathon is backed by investors including Temasek, Verizon Ventures and Boeing, and is headquartered in Silicon Valley after relocating from Austin, Texas.

providers.name: Blau
providers.description: Blau (Blau Corp) is a waste-management operating system for haulers (gestores), final-destination facilities, and government regulators across Mexico, Colombia, and Spain. The SaaS platform delivers AI-assisted route optimization, route-level profitability analysis, automated RP and RPBI hazardous- and biological-infectious-waste manifests, online collection booking, and end-to-end traceability, plus the Blau Driver mobile app for field crews. Founded in Guadalajara, Mexico in 2021 and backed by 500 Global (LatAm B17 batch), Blau integrates with SAT/CFDI, SEMARNAT, SAP/ERP, QuickBooks, WhatsApp, fleet GPS, and Power BI. Blau does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: IGO Limited
providers.description: IGO Limited is an ASX 100 listed Western Australian mining company focused on discovering, developing and delivering the critical minerals needed for clean energy and electrification. It owns and operates the Nova nickel-copper-cobalt operation in the Fraser Range and holds a lithium joint venture with Tianqi Lithium Corporation comprising a 51% stake in the Greenbushes Lithium Mine and the Kwinana lithium hydroxide refinery. No public developer API, documentation or developer portal was found on igo.com.au (surfaced via the australia-apidays-2026 harvest).

providers.name: LiquidStack
providers.description: LiquidStack is a data center liquid cooling company that designs, manufactures and services direct-to-chip and immersion cooling systems for AI, hyperscale, high performance computing, edge/5G and cryptocurrency workloads. Its product line spans direct-to-chip coolant distribution units — the CDU-1MW at up to 1,350kW of cooling at N+1 and the modular GigaModular CDU-10MW platform — alongside single-phase and two-phase immersion DataTank systems rated to 252kW, plus full lifecycle services covering consulting, installation, training and maintenance. The company spun out of Bitfury in 2021, raised $20 million from Tiger Global, is headquartered in Carrollton, Texas with engineering, R&D and manufacturing operations in Texas and Hong Kong, and was acquired by Trane Technologies in a deal completed in March 2026. LiquidStack sells capital equipment and services rather than software: it operates no developer program and publishes no public API, specification, SDK or developer portal. The only machine interface it documents is embedded in the hardware — its CDUs ship with native MODBUS TCP/IP or a RESTful API, plus BACnet/IP and SNMP, for remote management from a customer's own building or data center management system.

providers.name: One Five
providers.description: One Five (styled one.five) is a sustainable packaging technology company based in Holm, Germany that pairs an AI-driven decision platform, Quartermaster, with ready-to-use recyclable and compostable packaging products. The Quartermaster platform embeds product-market-fit and material analysis into packaging development to accelerate material scouting and packing trials, helping consumer brands cut R&D spend, improve customer acquisition efficiency, and meet emerging packaging regulations while reducing environmental impact. One Five ships flexible sustainable packaging for categories such as dishwasher tablets and gummies through partners including Bluemorph and Glassleaf, and is backed by Speedinvest. The company offers no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Recycleye
providers.description: Recycleye is a London-based company building AI-powered sorting equipment and analytics for waste management and material recovery businesses worldwide. Its products include Recycleye QualiBot robotic sorting cells, Recycleye QuantiSort optical sorting technology, and Recycleye Insights, a data analytics platform that uses computer vision (WasteNet) to identify and categorize waste streams. The company sells hardware and software into recycling operations to improve purity, recovery rates, and profitability. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC. As of this enrichment pass Recycleye publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures its identity and public web properties only.

providers.name: Sandfire Resources
providers.description: Sandfire Resources (Sandfire) is a global copper producer that describes its mission as mining copper sustainably to energise the future. Its website lists operations and projects including MATSA (Spain), Motheo (Botswana), Kalkaroo and DeGrussa (Australia) and Black Butte (United States), plus exploration, and it publishes ASX announcements, financial, quarterly and sustainability reports for investors. Sandfire is headquartered on Whadjuk Noongar land in Western Australia. No public developer API, documentation or developer portal was found on its site; this profile records its corporate web presence.

providers.name: Sims Limited
providers.description: Sims Limited is an ASX-listed global recycling company whose story began in 1917 with a single scrap metal yard in Sydney, Australia. The parent company took the name Sims Limited in 2020 to reflect the breadth of its businesses, including Sims Metal and Sims Lifecycle Services, which extend the life of discarded goods through advanced recycling and repurposing. Its stated purpose is to 'create a world without waste to preserve our planet'. Surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (australia-apidays-2026); its corporate site publishes no developer portal, API documentation or public API.

providers.name: The Atlas Marketplace
providers.description: The Atlas Marketplace (branded "The Atlas") is a free online community and knowledge marketplace for local government leaders. Officials and staff use it to learn from their peers about the smart, safe, and sustainable solutions working in their communities, browsing a searchable library of case studies, vendors, and civic-technology projects. The platform connects public-sector practitioners with the companies and partners behind proven municipal solutions across mobility, infrastructure, sustainability, and public safety. Backed by 500 Global, it operates as a content and community website rather than a developer/API product; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched from its public web presence.

providers.name: Thea Energy
providers.description: Thea Energy, Inc. is a fusion energy company headquartered in Kearny, New Jersey, founded in 2022 on stellarator physics and engineering developed at Princeton University and the Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory. Thea is reinventing the stellarator by replacing complex, hand-wound 3D modular coils with a phased array of simple planar electromagnetic coils, moving the complexity of shaping the magnetic field out of the hardware and into a software control stack that can be tuned over an asset's lifetime. Its first integrated machine, Eos, is a steady-state, neutron-producing stellarator; the follow-on Helios is intended to be an electricity-producing plant. The company raised a $100M Series B in May 2026 led by Thomas Tull's US Innovative Technology Fund, and the U.S. Department of Energy has certified its power plant preconceptual design milestone. Thea publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable contract; its only public software surface is a small set of open-source nuclear-engineering and simulation libraries on GitHub.

providers.name: Zeitview
providers.description: Zeitview (formerly DroneBase) is an AI-powered aerial inspection and asset intelligence platform. It combines a managed network of drone and aircraft pilots with computer-vision analytics and lifecycle asset-management software to deliver inspection imagery, condition assessments, and actionable intelligence for wind energy, solar, utilities, oil & gas, construction, commercial real estate, and property management. As of this profile the company operates a customer web platform, support center, and blog but does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDK; data access is arranged through direct customer engagement.

providers.name: Allonnia
providers.description: Allonnia is a biotechnology and critical materials technology company focused on accelerating the deployment of innovative solutions for the life sciences and sustainable mining sectors. It provides data-driven platforms, advanced materials, and consulting services to help organizations navigate complex regulatory landscapes, improve operational efficiency, and drive sustainable growth. Founded to bridge the gap between scientific research and commercial application, Allonnia leverages AI-driven analytics and a global network of partners to deliver impactful results across the biotech and mining industries.

providers.name: David Energy
providers.description: David Energy is a clean-energy technology company and licensed electricity retailer that installs free plug-in smart batteries for homes and businesses. Its software charges batteries when grid power is cheap and discharges them during peak-price periods to lower customers' monthly utility bills, alongside bill-monitoring and thermostat-management advisory tools. Backed by Union Square Ventures, David Energy operates in the New York City market with a stated mission of powering the grid on 100% clean energy and shifting the balance of energy control from institutions toward consumers.

providers.name: Iceotope
providers.description: Iceotope Technologies is a Sheffield, UK precision liquid cooling company founded in 2005 as a research-driven "green computing" venture, now supplying chassis-level liquid cooling for AI, HPC, data center and edge infrastructure. Its "direct to everything" single-phase immersion approach removes heat from every component rather than the processor alone, and ships as two product lines: KUL BOX for near-edge AI and HPC deployments, and KUL AI liquid-cooled server chassis for high-density rack environments. The company licenses its thermal IP (228 patents granted, allowed and pending) and works through OEM/ODM partnerships with vendors including HPE, Intel and nVent. Iceotope is a hardware and thermal-engineering business: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: Manus Bio
providers.description: Manus Bio Inc. (trading as "Manus", the BioAlternatives Company) is a Cambridge, Massachusetts industrial biotechnology company founded in 2011 out of MIT by Dr. Aji Parayil and Dr. Greg Stephanopoulos. Manus engineers microbial cell factories and precision-fermentation processes so that complex molecules normally obtained through petrochemical synthesis, agricultural extraction, or animal husbandry can be produced by fermentation instead - what the company calls bioalternatives. Its commercialized products include the first U.S. commercial-scale monk fruit sweetener (produced at its Augusta, Georgia BioFacility), the Yume M stevia Reb M sweetener co-developed with Tate & Lyle, citrus-derived aroma ingredients (Nootkatone 70, Valencene 80, BioNootkatone) for Givaudan, and an artemisinin antimalarial program funded by HHS/ASPR. It sells scale-up services through its BioAccelerator and BioManufacturing programs (protein engineering, strain development, bioprocess development from 250 ml to 3,000 L, pilot-scale and biomanufacturing). In April 2025 Manus merged with genome-engineering company Inscripta, adding whole-genome editing technology and the MAD7 CRISPR nuclease licensing program; inscripta.com is now a redirect notice. Manus is a manufacturer of physical ingredients and a contract development and manufacturing organization - it sells molecules and services, not software. It publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, webhook surface, or machine-readable specification of any kind, and its computational and AI-driven enzyme-engineering tools are internal capabilities that support its services rather than a customer-facing platform.

providers.name: Sealed
providers.description: Sealed is a New York-based climate technology company, founded in 2012, whose Sealed Pro platform helps home-improvement contractors sell and finance home weatherization and electrification projects — insulation, air sealing, heat pumps, smart thermostats and heat-pump water heaters. Sealed pairs energy data and analytics with a rebate and incentive engine that qualifies a project at the point of sale, guarantees a minimum rebate amount, files the utility and Inflation Reduction Act (HOMES / HEAR) paperwork on the contractor's behalf, and pays the contractor after installation while Sealed carries the incentive-collection risk. The company began as a direct-to-consumer home energy retrofit provider with the first residential energy-savings guarantee, and relaunched as Sealed Pro, a contractor-facing software platform, working with utilities and state energy offices on measured- and modeled-savings programs.

providers.name: Sourgum
providers.description: Sourgum provides technology-driven waste and recycling solutions, unifying thousands of local haulers to deliver scalable, transparent, and reliable services across the United States. The platform offers modern waste management with real‑time tracking, transparent pricing, and robust customer support, aiming to improve sustainability and operational efficiency for businesses and municipalities.

providers.name: Sunrun
providers.description: Sunrun is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Sunrun API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Syzygy Plasmonics
providers.description: Syzygy Plasmonics is a Houston, Texas deep-decarbonization company commercializing photocatalytic chemical manufacturing. Its Rigel reactor cell uses photonic energy from renewable electricity in place of combustion heat to drive reforming reactions, and its NovaSAF / GHG e-Reforming pathway converts waste biogas into low-carbon sustainable aviation fuel, independently assessed as eligible for both ISCC EU RFNBO and Advanced BioSAF certification. Adjacent targets include hydrogen from ammonia e-cracking, syngas, methanol, butadiene and other commodity chemicals, sold as reactor hardware plus a licensing and front-end engineering support package. Syzygy is a hardware and process-licensing business, not a software vendor: as of 2026-08-29 it publishes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Unspun
providers.description: Unspun is a fashion-technology company building Vega, the world's first 3D weaving machines, which transform yarn directly into finished woven garments in about twenty minutes for automated, localized, on-demand apparel manufacturing. Founded by Beth Esponnette, Walden Lam, and Kevin Martin and operating from Oakland, California and Hong Kong, the company pairs its weaving hardware with software for custom-fit patternmaking and design automation, working with manufacturers and brands to eliminate overproduction, with a mission of reducing global human carbon emissions by one percent. Unspun is backed by DCVC and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Booosttechnologies
providers.description: Booost Technologies is a Japanese sustainability‑focused enterprise software company offering the Booost Sustainability ERP platform. The platform helps organizations integrate environmental, social and governance (ESG) data into their operations, driving scalable growth and net‑zero initiatives across more than 95 countries. With multilingual support and a global client base, Booost delivers a comprehensive suite for sustainability reporting, risk management, and value creation.

providers.name: ConnectDER
providers.description: ConnectDER is a Philadelphia-based clean energy hardware company and the leading US manufacturer of meter socket adapters (MSAs, also called meter collars) for the residential market. Founded in 2011 as Infinite Invention LLC after a DOE SunShot Incubator grant, it builds plug-and-play devices that install at the utility meter socket to interconnect distributed energy resources — rooftop solar, battery storage and EV charging — without panel upgrades, line-side taps or circuit relocations. Its product line is the IslandDER MSA (a microgrid interconnect device for solar-plus-battery and whole-home backup, integrated by SolarEdge, FranklinWH, Lunar Energy, EcoFlow and Fox ESS), the Solar MSA and the EV MSA. ConnectDER helped author UL 414 Supplements A, B and C, the standards governing meter socket adapters, and has surpassed 40,000 devices installed across US utility territories including PG&E, SCE and SDG&E. ConnectDER publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract; its devices communicate with partner battery systems over discrete hardwired sensing, control and status signals rather than a network interface. It does publish an llms.txt at its web root.

providers.name: Jetti Resources
providers.description: Jetti Resources is a Boulder, Colorado based metallurgical technology company whose catalytic leaching process unlocks copper from low-grade primary sulfide ores such as chalcopyrite — roughly 70% of the world's copper resources — that conventional pyrometallurgy cannot treat economically and that bioleaching cannot treat at all because of the passivation layer that halts extraction. Jetti's catalyst prevents that layer from forming, allowing uninterrupted heap and stockpile leaching through existing bioleach and SX-EW circuits using modular, standardized micro plants that require no additional permits. The technology has been deployed commercially since 2019, including at Capstone's Pinto Valley mine in Arizona and Freeport-McMoRan's El Abra operation in Chile, and the company is backed by BHP, Freeport-McMoRan, Mitsubishi Corporation, BMW Group, BlackRock, T. Rowe Price, Orion Resource Partners, DNS Capital and Zoma Capital. Jetti sells a chemical and process technology licence to mine operators rather than software: it runs no developer program, publishes no public API, SDK or machine-readable specification, and its only authenticated surface is an Intralinks-hosted customer portal for existing licensees.

providers.name: La Solive
providers.description: La Solive is a French vocational training organization (organisme de formation) preparing career-changers and apprentices for the trades behind building energy renovation and the climate transition. It runs state-recognized, practice-based programs — chef de projet en rénovation énergétique, conducteur de travaux, plombier chauffagiste pompe à chaleur et gaz, technicien de maintenance CVC, installateur de panneaux photovoltaïques, QualiPAC and agent de maintenance du bâtiment — delivered across campuses in Paris, Lyon, Nantes, Marseille, Toulouse and Lille plus a distance-learning track, with Qualiopi certification and France Travail / Mon Compte Formation / Transitions Pro financing. La Solive reports 1,500+ students trained and 500+ recruiting partner companies. It is a Partech portfolio company in the Climate sector. As of this enrichment pass La Solive publishes no public API, developer portal, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; it does publish an /llms.txt agent-readable site index, captured in this repo.

providers.name: Brookfield Asset Management
providers.description: Brookfield Asset Management (NYSE: BAM, TSX: BAM) is a leading global alternative asset manager with over $1 trillion in assets under management and approximately $614 billion in fee-bearing capital. BAM describes itself as "a pure-play, asset-light investment manager with earnings derived from stable, predictable fee-related revenue." The publicly listed manager was formed in December 2022 when it was spun out of Brookfield Corporation (NYSE: BN), which remains the majority shareholder. BAM operates across five investment verticals — Renewable Power & Transition, Infrastructure, Real Estate, Private Equity, and Credit — and adjacent Insurance Solutions capability is delivered through Brookfield Wealth Solutions, a sister business within the broader Brookfield ecosystem. BAM does not publish a public developer API program. Institutional Limited Partners, financial intermediaries, distribution platforms, and portfolio companies interact with the firm through private, authentication-gated investor portals, PDF reporting (10-K, supplemental, letters to shareholders), data feeds from fund administrators, and the investor-relations website at bam.brookfield.com.

providers.name: Burnbot
providers.description: Burnbot is a wildfire mitigation and fuels management company that builds autonomous, remotely-operated machines and delivers field services to reduce hazardous vegetation and conduct controlled, precision fuel-reduction burns. Its equipment operates in steep, remote, and hazardous terrain around the clock in most weather conditions, cutting fuel loads without disturbing healthy vegetation or compacting soil, and is used across fire hazard mitigation, systematic fuels management, and timber operations. Burnbot works with utilities, transportation agencies, land managers, and tribal governments including PG&E, Caltrans, the U.S. Forest Service, and CAL FIRE. Burnbot was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a hardware and field-services company with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: CarbonQuest
providers.description: CarbonQuest provides distributed carbon capture solutions that turn industrial CO₂ emissions into revenue-generating resources. Their modular DCCS™ system captures CO₂ at source across biogas, low‑carbon power, and food & beverage sectors, offering financing with no upfront capital and enabling carbon credit generation, tax credits, and sustainable CO₂ supply.

providers.name: Collectiv Food
providers.description: Collectiv Food is a next-generation B2B food wholesaler serving professional kitchens across the UK and France.
