Launched in London in 2022, it combines collective buying power, consolidated deliveries, and direct sourcing through a shortened, patented supply-chain model to supply restaurants, hotels, and caterers with meat, fish, plant-based proteins, dairy, produce, dry and frozen goods, and prepared items. The company emphasizes traceability, responsible sourcing, and sustainability, and is B-Corp certified with an EcoVadis Gold rating. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; no public API or developer portal is currently published.

providers.name: EnerGaia
providers.description: EnerGaia is a spirulina producer, incorporated in Thailand in April 2009 and now headquartered in Singapore, that grows nutrient-dense microalgae in proprietary closed bioreactors rather than open ponds to deliver clean, consistent spirulina for food and beverage manufacturers. The company originated from research into using microalgae to capture industrial CO2 from power-plant flue gas and has since focused on making spirulina a mainstream, sustainable food ingredient. Its product line includes Fresh Spirulina Paste, Fresh-Frozen Spirulina, and Freeze-Dried Spirulina Powder, used in beverages, egg substitutes, noodles, meat replacements, pastas, and snacks. EnerGaia is a portfolio company of 500 Global. It publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: HumanCo
providers.description: HumanCo is a mission-driven consumer packaged goods and wellness holding company that builds and acquires better-for-you food, beverage, and lifestyle brands made with real, clean ingredients and free of seed oils and highly processed inputs. Its portfolio spans brands and concepts such as Against the Grain (gluten-free foods), True Food Kitchen (health-focused restaurants), and Grove Collaborative (sustainable home and personal care). Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. HumanCo operates a marketing and e-commerce web presence but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or technical developer platform at this time.

providers.name: Juno
providers.description: Juno (juno.co), operated by Juno Technology, Inc., is a San Francisco-based owner's representation, development-consulting and construction-management firm for prefabricated, modular and mass-timber multifamily development, working with developers from site feasibility and entitlement through delivery across North America. Juno owns the rights to the Juno Mass Timber System, a field-tested kit-of-parts building system of roughly 33 components configurable into 25+ unit types, proven on the 24-unit Juno East Austin project at 400 Comal St, Austin TX. The current company is the 2024 relaunch ("Juno 2.0") of the venture-funded Juno / Juno Residential founded in 2019 by Jonathan Scherr, BJ Siegel and Chester Chipperfield, which raised roughly $32M from Comcast Ventures, Khosla Ventures and RET Ventures before running out of money; the relaunched firm is led by co-founders Emily Mills Marineau and Jen Canchola. Juno sells professional services and a physical building system, not software: as of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing site, a mass-timber system page, a contact form, a newsletter signup, terms of service and a privacy policy, and no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Koobz
providers.description: Koobz is a Ventura, California additive-manufacturing company rebuilding the footwear supply chain around on-demand 3D printing. Its "gigafactory" prints circular-ready, mono-material foamed-TPU shoes to order, so brands carry zero inventory and face no minimum order quantities: a consumer buys on the brand's own storefront, the order and personalization specs sync to the Koobz factory, the shoe is printed in Ventura and dropshipped direct to the customer in days. The company markets 10x faster concept-to-market cycles (4-6 weeks, no tooling), custom cushioning and foot-scanning personalization, and a KoobzWeave toolpath-as-textile upper pattern engine. Its mono-material architecture is positioned for Extended Producer Responsibility regimes such as California SB 707, since a single-polymer shoe yields premium TPU on take-back rather than mixed waste. Koobz has raised $7.2M and is backed by Uncork Capital. It describes its factory as API-driven and its order intake as an API sync from brand storefronts, but as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definition; integration appears to run through its partner ("Partner With Us") channel.

providers.name: Public Goods
providers.description: Public Goods is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce retailer selling household essentials, personal care, and home products under its own private label, with an emphasis on natural formulations, simplified ingredient lists, minimalist packaging, and sustainable sourcing. The company operates a membership model (an annual fee unlocking member pricing, free shipping, and store credit) and a wholesale channel. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer retail brand it publishes no developer API, SDK, or technical documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Terra CO2
providers.description: Terra CO2 Technology is a Golden, Colorado climate-technology and building-materials manufacturer that produces low-carbon replacements for Portland cement. Its commercial product, OPUS SCM, is a supplementary cementitious material that replaces up to 50% of the Portland cement in a concrete mix as a drop-in substitute for legacy SCMs such as fly ash, cutting CO2 by roughly 70% and NOx by roughly 90% per ton replaced, and it is produced from abundant silicate feedstocks rather than coal-plant by-products. A second product, OPUS ZERO, targets a full zero-carbon cement replacement and is in concrete trials. The company runs a pilot and materials R&D facility in Golden and is building a 240,000-ton-per-year commercial plant in Cleburne, Texas, backed by more than $250M raised from climate and construction investors including Cemex Ventures. Terra CO2 sells physical material into the construction supply chain; it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Volter
providers.description: Volter (Get Volter Ltd) is a London-based energy platform that connects UK businesses with renewable generators to procure cheaper, greener electricity, and helps commercial real estate owners and generators deploy, optimize, and monetize rooftop solar and other onsite renewable assets. The platform spans renewable energy matching, solar optimization, and a forthcoming energy management suite with analytics, anomaly detection, flexible asset control, and battery storage. Backed by Transition and Seedcamp with a $3.2M pre-seed round in 2024. Volter does not currently publish a public API or developer documentation.

providers.name: Axalta Coating Systems
providers.description: Axalta Coating Systems is a global supplier of liquid and powder coatings for transportation and industrial end-markets, operating through Performance Coatings (refinish and industrial) and Mobility Coatings (light vehicle and commercial vehicle) segments. Brands include Cromax, Spies Hecker, Standox, Imron, and Voltatex. In July 2024 Axalta acquired The CoverFlexx Group from Transtar Holding for $285 million to expand its economy-tier aftermarket coverage in North America. In November 2025 Axalta announced a $17 billion all-stock merger of equals with AkzoNobel that is expected to close in late 2026 or early 2027, forming a coatings company with dual headquarters in Amsterdam and Philadelphia.

providers.name: Cowboy Space Corporation (formerly Aetherflux)
providers.description: Cowboy Space Corporation is an American orbital-infrastructure company founded in 2024 by Baiju Bhatt, co-founder and former co-CEO of Robinhood, headquartered in San Carlos, California with a second site in Seattle, Washington. It operated as Aetherflux Inc. from founding until May 2026, when it renamed to Cowboy Space Corporation and broadened its mission from space-based solar power alone to vertically integrated orbital infrastructure for the AI era, spanning launch vehicles, space-based power generation and in-orbit compute. Its flagship program is Stampede, a Low Earth Orbit constellation of satellites that harvest solar power to run on-orbit GPU data centers, with the first Galactic Brain data-center node targeted for early 2027 using NVIDIA Space-1 Vera Rubin modules and a small infrared power-beaming demonstrator satellite planned for 2026. The company concluded that launch supply was the binding constraint on orbital compute and is therefore also developing its own rocket, sized between Falcon 9 and Starship at roughly 20,000-25,000 kg of payload, whose upper stage is itself the payload - each one intended to become a one-megawatt orbital data center - with a first launch targeted for the end of 2028. It has raised roughly USD 365 million to date, including a USD 50 million Series A in April 2025 and a USD 275 million Series B in May 2026 at a USD 2 billion valuation, led by Index Ventures with IVP, Blossom Capital, SAIC, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Construct Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, NEA and Interlagos participating. Cowboy Space is a space hardware and energy infrastructure company, not a software vendor: as of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK, no public GitHub organization and no machine-readable API contract of any kind. Its entire public web presence is a four-page Framer-hosted marketing site (home, terms, privacy, media terms of use) plus an Ashby-hosted careers board.

providers.name: Crown Holdings
providers.description: Crown Holdings, Inc. is a global leader in the design, manufacture, and sale of rigid packaging products for consumer goods, including metal beverage cans and ends, food cans, aerosol cans, specialty closures and promotional tins, as well as transit and protective packaging products for industrial markets. The company operates in more than 40 countries and supports customers with design, decoration, reprographics, compound development, pilot facilities, and seaming training services. Crown Holdings does not publish a public developer API program; technical collaboration with customers happens through B2B and EDI channels.

providers.name: Gravity
providers.description: Gravity (Gravity Technologies) builds and deploys ultra-fast DC electric-vehicle charging infrastructure for dense urban environments. Its Distributed Energy Access Points (DEAPs) deliver up to five-minute charges from compact, modular hardware that requires minimal real estate and no dedicated utility upgrade, letting operators place high-power charging in garages, curbside, and fleet depots. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and Redpoint Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it publishes no public developer portal, API, or SDKs at this time, so this profile captures company identity and the domain security surface rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Blattnertech
providers.description: Blattnertech, operating under the Blattner Company brand, provides engineering and technology solutions across renewable energy, storage, and safety sectors. With over a century of innovation heritage, the firm delivers solar, wind, and storage projects, emphasizing sustainability, community impact, and advanced technical expertise. The company’s portfolio includes large‑scale renewable installations and comprehensive project development services.

providers.name: Anthro Energy
providers.description: Anthro Energy is a battery materials company based in Alameda, California, developing next-generation electrolyte technology for lithium-ion and next-gen battery cells. Its flagship Proteus platform is a drop-in electrolyte that increases energy density, improves safety, and adds mechanical integrity without requiring changes to existing gigafactory manufacturing infrastructure, and is compatible with a wide range of anodes, separators, and cathodes. Spun out of research at Stanford, Anthro Energy is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures and Ultratech Capital. It is a physical-materials company with no public API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company and market discovery.

providers.name: Chiquita Brands International
providers.description: Chiquita Brands International is a leading global producer, marketer, and distributor of bananas and other fresh produce, recognized worldwide by the iconic Blue Sticker on its bananas. Founded in 1899 as the United Fruit Company and rebranded as Chiquita in 1990, the company is headquartered in Etoy, Switzerland (with significant operations in Fort Lauderdale, Florida) and sources fruit from plantations across Latin America (Honduras, Guatemala, Costa Rica, Panama, Colombia, and Ecuador) for distribution in the United States, Europe, and other markets. Beyond core Cavendish bananas, Chiquita markets specialty banana varieties (organic, Reds, Manzanos, Minis), plantains, pineapples (including the Sunburst Gold variety), and partners with retailers worldwide. Chiquita does not currently publish a consumer-facing developer API; supplier, retailer, and grower integrations are managed through internal portals and bilateral EDI systems, and consumer-facing digital experiences focus on recipes, sticker collection campaigns, and retail merchandising.

providers.name: EY
providers.description: One of the Big Four professional services firms providing audit, tax, consulting, and advisory services. Operates in over 150 countries helping businesses navigate regulatory and strategic challenges, and runs proprietary technology platforms such as EY Helix (analytics), EY Atlas (research), and EY Canvas (audit) for internal and engagement use.

providers.name: Scythe Robotics
providers.description: Scythe Robotics builds autonomous lawn mowers to transform commercial landscaping. Their flagship M.52 robot delivers up to 1.5 acres per hour, reducing crew size and emissions. The company emphasizes sustainable technology, mission-driven teamwork, and community impact, aiming to make outdoor maintenance more efficient and eco‑friendly.

providers.name: SolarCycle
providers.description: SolarCycle is a technology-driven solar recycling company founded in 2022 that provides certified end-of-life management for solar energy systems. It recovers up to 97% of panel materials (silver, copper, gold, aluminum, glass), recycles power electronics such as inverters and transformers, and handles logistics and field operations for large-scale solar projects, achieving 100% landfill diversion. SolarCycle operates seven facilities across Georgia, Illinois, Texas, Nevada, and Arizona and is building a domestic recycled-solar-glass manufacturing plant, serving major solar companies including Q Cells, AES, Orsted, and Sunrun. It is a portfolio company of Fifth Wall. This is a physical circular-economy operations business with no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: UBQ Materials
providers.description: UBQ Materials is a climate-tech company founded in 2012 that converts unsorted mixed household waste, including organics and hard-to-recycle plastics, into UBQ, a climate-positive thermoplastic material that substitutes for oil-based plastics in manufacturing. A Certified B Corporation backed by Battery Ventures, the company operates a full-scale production facility in Bergen op Zoom, Netherlands (opened 2024) with 80,000 tons of annual capacity, plus an R&D center in Tze'elim, Israel. UBQ Materials publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Watershed
providers.description: Watershed is an enterprise sustainability platform used by large companies to measure their carbon footprint, report against regulatory and voluntary frameworks, and act on decarbonization opportunities. The platform combines a library of 500,000+ emissions factors, pre-verified methodologies, and AI agents for data cleaning, analysis, and report drafting. Watershed exposes an API for automated data ingestion and reporting, alongside guided uploads, and publishes integrations for common enterprise data sources. API keys are provisioned to customers via the Watershed dashboard at dashboard.watershedclimate.com. Public developer documentation is limited; most API access is delivered through customer onboarding and partner enablement.

providers.name: zincfive
providers.description: ZincFive is a power solutions company that manufactures nickel-zinc (NiZn) battery technology for mission-critical and backup power applications, including data center UPS systems, AI dynamic power, and grid storage. Its product line covers BC Series UPS battery cabinets, NiZn retrofit kits, monobloc batteries, and cylindrical cells, positioned as non-flammable, high-power-density, and highly recyclable alternatives to lead-acid batteries. ZincFive publishes technical documents, papers, and industry insights reports, but does not expose a public developer API or SDK surface.

providers.name: 24M
providers.description: 24M Technologies is a battery technology company founded in 2010 out of MIT laboratories and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Rather than manufacturing cells at scale itself, 24M licenses its battery materials, cell architecture and SemiSolid manufacturing platform to energy-storage system integrators, EV battery manufacturers and OEMs worldwide. Its product portfolio spans the Eternalyte electrolyte (ultra-fast charging and low-temperature performance), the Impervio separator (thermal-runaway prevention), the LiForever electrode, the 24M ETOP electrode-to-pack architecture, and 24M production equipment. Partners and corporate investors have included Volkswagen Group, Kyocera, Itochu and FREYR Battery. 24M is a hardware, materials and manufacturing company; it publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Antora Energy
providers.description: Antora Energy is a San Jose, California clean-energy hardware company founded by Justin Briggs, Andrew Ponec and David Bierman that designs, manufactures and deploys factory-built thermal batteries for heavy industry, data centers and the grid. Antora's system resistively heats blocks of solid carbon to temperatures up to 2,400C when electricity is cheapest, stores that energy for multiple days in a compact modular unit, and discharges it around the clock as radiant heat delivered directly to industrial processes or paired with off-the-shelf steam turbine equipment for firm power; the company also develops thermophotovoltaic (TPV) heat-to-power cells at what it describes as the world's largest TPV manufacturing line. Its HeatCore product delivers heat up to 375C at 300 kW-thermal per module, and its power block is rated at 50 MW-electric. Antora's first giga-scale deployment, Project Big Stone, is a 5 GWh system of more than 200 thermal batteries at POET's bioprocessing plant in Big Stone City, South Dakota, built from empty lot to energy delivery in under twelve months. The company closed a $550 million Series C in 2026. Antora sells energy hardware and long-term energy offtake rather than software: it publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract, and its only public software surface is Insight, an authenticated steam and power optimization dashboard for named project stakeholders.

providers.name: Cylib
providers.description: Cylib is a German battery recycling company founded in 2022 as a spinoff from RWTH Aachen University, headquartered in Aachen, Germany. It transforms end-of-life lithium-ion batteries, production scrap, and black mass back into critical raw materials, recovering lithium, graphite, nickel, cobalt, and manganese through a proprietary, largely water-based hydrometallurgical process that the company reports achieves over 90% recycling efficiency with an ~80% reduced carbon footprint versus primary extraction, powered by 100% renewable electricity. The company is backed by Speedinvest and other investors. Cylib operates as an industrial cleantech / circular-economy materials business and does not currently publish a developer program, public API, developer portal, SDKs, or other software integration surface; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and carries only identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Fibmold
providers.description: Fibmold is an eco-friendly molded-fiber packaging manufacturer building sustainable, plastic-free alternatives to rigid single-use plastic packaging. Its products are thermoformed from natural fibres such as bagasse, bamboo, and hard/soft wood pulp collected from farms, forests, and agro-processing units, then upcycled into compostable and recyclable packaging. Applications span food-service packaging, customised industrial solutions, fibre-based dosing scoops, aviation casseroles, cosmetic inserts, pharma injectable trays, chocolate trays, and noodle cups. Fibmold also runs the Primo by Fibmold retail storefront and builds manufacturing eco-systems and material-science innovation to scale sustainable packaging on the supply side. Backed by Accel.

providers.name: Mast Reforestation
providers.description: Mast Reforestation (formerly DroneSeed) is North America's leading post-fire reforestation and carbon-removal company, restoring wildfire-damaged forests across the American West. It operates two nurseries, Cal Forest Nurseries and Silvaseed, manages the largest seed bank in the western United States, grows more than 30 million seedlings annually, and develops carbon-removal credits by burying post-wildfire biomass to finance reforestation for landowners and consulting foresters. Mast publishes no public developer program or API surface.

providers.name: Niron Magnetics
providers.description: Niron Magnetics is a U.S. advanced-manufacturing company commercializing high-performance permanent magnets made from Iron Nitride rather than rare-earth elements. Spun out of University of Minnesota and U.S. Department of Energy ARPA-E research and founded in 2013, the company holds 150+ patents around its Clean Earth Magnet technology and is building the first full-scale Iron Nitride magnet plant in Sartell, Minnesota, alongside its Minneapolis headquarters and a Washington, D.C. policy office. Its magnets target electric-motor, automotive, consumer-audio, industrial and defense applications, with announced collaborations including Stellantis, Moog, Aspina, FaitalPRO, MATTER and Bimotal. Niron Magnetics is a materials and hardware manufacturer: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Northvolt
providers.description: Northvolt AB is a Swedish lithium-ion battery developer and manufacturer, founded in Stockholm in 2016, that built and operated the Northvolt Ett gigafactory in Skelleftea and the Northvolt Labs R&D and qualification campus in Vasteras, with further sites in Heide (Germany), Gdansk (Poland) and Montreal (Canada). Its product line covered lithium-ion, sodium-ion and lithium-metal cells, the Voltpack Core and Voltpack Mobile System battery energy storage systems, the Revolt battery recycling operation, and a Connected Battery telemetry and fleet-management service. Northvolt AB filed for bankruptcy in Sweden on 12 March 2025; through 2025 its remaining assets in Sweden, Germany and Poland were acquired by Lyten. The company never published a public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract; its only named developer-facing surface, api.northvolt.com, no longer has a reachable origin.

providers.name: VITO (Flemish Institute for Technological Research)
providers.description: VITO (Flemish Institute for Technological Research) is a leading Flemish research institute focusing on sustainable energy, climate, water management, and digital transformation. It provides scientific expertise, data‑driven solutions, and innovative technologies to governments, businesses, and society to accelerate the transition to a low‑carbon, resilient future. VITO collaborates with international partners, runs large‑scale test facilities, and offers open data platforms and APIs for environmental and energy data.

providers.name: Volteum
providers.description: Volteum provides fleet electrification and EV fleet management software that helps companies plan, execute, and operate the transition of their vehicle fleets to electric. The platform covers electrification planning, charging optimisation, and live fleet management, connecting directly to vehicles through OEM APIs across 30+ brands with no hardware installation to track mileage, fault codes, charging sessions, maintenance intervals, and costs across electric, diesel, petrol, and hybrid fleets. Volteum is a Techstars portfolio company and publishes no public developer portal; its telematics and fleet-system API integrations are offered to customers directly.

providers.name: 247Solar
providers.description: 247Solar, Inc. is a zero-carbon energy technology company with MIT origins that designs and builds modular third-generation concentrated solar power (CSP) systems delivering round-the-clock clean electricity and industrial-grade heat. Its 247Solar Plant couples a high-temperature solar receiver (~970C) with the Heat2Power turbine and HeatStore thermal storage, holding energy in ceramic pellets or ordinary sand for 20+ hours without batteries or molten salts. The company targets mining, microgrids, off-grid and rural electrification, industrial heat, economic development zones, grid support, data centers and green hydrogen, and sells through power purchase agreements as well as equipment. Headquartered in Great Falls, Virginia, 247Solar is a hardware and project-development business; it publishes no public API, developer program or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Albemarle
providers.description: Albemarle Corporation is a global specialty chemicals company and leading provider of lithium, bromine, and other essential elements. Operating from its global headquarters in Charlotte, NC, Albemarle serves customers in approximately 70 countries with world-class hard-rock and brine lithium resources, state-of-the-art lithium conversion facilities, advanced lithium material and process development, bromine production facilities, and the US's only producing lithium resource in Silver Peak, NV. The company serves critical markets including electric vehicle batteries, energy storage, flame retardants, pharmaceutical ingredients, catalysts, and specialty chemicals, employing approximately 7,800 people and holding over 1,500 active patents worldwide.

providers.name: Better Origin
providers.description: Better Origin is a UK-based agritech company decarbonizing the food chain by converting food waste into sustainable, locally produced animal feed. Its core technology is a fully automated, AI-controlled containerized insect farm that breeds black soldier fly larvae to consume food waste and produce nutrient-rich insect-based ingredients for pet food, poultry feed, and aquaculture. The systems are remotely monitored and controlled by software and require no specialist knowledge from operators. Better Origin is a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Beyond Meat
providers.description: Beyond Meat, Inc. is a Los Angeles-based producer of plant-based meat substitutes founded in 2009 and publicly traded on Nasdaq (BYND). The company makes plant-protein versions of beef, pork, and poultry products, including the Beyond Burger, Beyond Sausage, Beyond Beef, and Beyond Chicken, distributed across grocery retail and foodservice channels worldwide. Beyond Meat operates as a consumer packaged-goods brand rather than a technology or developer-platform company; it publishes a marketing and e-commerce website, product and recipe catalogs, a newsroom, and an investor-relations presence, but does not offer a public developer API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Kleiner Perkins and Obvious Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Circulate
providers.description: Circulate is a sustainable packaging data platform founded in Sweden. It aggregates, structures, and enriches packaging supplier information, turning PDFs, spreadsheets, and certificates into a searchable database. The platform enables businesses to source compliant packaging quickly, reduces greenwashing, and supports sustainability reporting with AI‑driven insights.

providers.name: EcoPlant
providers.description: EcoPlant provides an intelligent air compressor control and monitoring platform for industrial facilities. The Ecoplant 360 solution uses IoT sensors, AI-powered dynamic controls, and predictive analytics to optimize compressed-air systems in real time, preventing downtime, improving reliability, and reducing compressed-air energy costs by up to 50 percent. It installs in under a week with no installation fees and is compatible with most compressor brands and existing plant technology.

providers.name: Electric Hydrogen
providers.description: Electric Hydrogen (EH2) is a Massachusetts-based clean-energy company that designs, manufactures, and commissions the world's most powerful PEM electrolyzers, packaged into a fully-integrated 100MW HYPRPlant that turns water and renewable electricity into the lowest-cost green hydrogen. The complete plant solution bundles power conversion, gas processing, water treatment, and thermal management so heavy industry can decarbonize ammonia, e-fuels, steel, and refining at gigawatt scale. Founded in 2020 and led by CEO Raffi Garabedian, EH2 operates a 1.2GW gigafactory in Devens, Massachusetts, became green hydrogen's first unicorn with a $380M Series C, and is backed by Fifth Wall, Fortescue, Energy Impact Partners, bp Ventures, Temasek, and Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund. This profile enriches the API Evangelist network stub with the company's real public web surface.

providers.name: Ethic
providers.description: Ethic is an SEC-registered technology-driven asset manager that helps financial advisors and institutions build and manage highly customized, values-aligned, and tax-smart investment portfolios at scale. Its platform centralizes client portfolio management across direct indexing, model portfolios, and unified managed accounts (UMAs), letting advisors personalize holdings to individual values and tax situations. Ethic is a private, advisor- and institution-facing platform and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or webhooks as of this profiling.

providers.name: Exowatt
providers.description: Exowatt is a clean-energy technology company redefining power generation for the AI era. Its flagship Exowatt P3 is a modular, dispatchable solar-thermal energy platform that captures solar energy with proprietary Fresnel lenses and heat exchangers, stores it in a high-efficiency heat battery, and dispatches electricity on demand via a proprietary heat engine, delivering up to 24 hours of dispatchable baseload power. The systems are factory-built in the USA from abundant, low-cost materials without rare-earth minerals, and are aimed at energy-intensive customers such as AI data centers and utilities. Backed by a16z and Felicis, Exowatt is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it currently publishes no public developer API or documentation surface.

providers.name: Forge Nano
providers.description: Forge Nano is a materials-technology manufacturer headquartered in Thornton, Colorado that commercializes particle and wafer Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) under its Atomic Armor platform and patented ALDx architecture. The company applies atomic-scale nanocoatings to powders, electrodes and semiconductor wafers to improve energy density, cycle life, thermal stability and yield, and sells three lines of business: US-sourced lithium-ion cells from its Morrisville, North Carolina gigafactory, commercial semiconductor wafer-fabrication equipment including the TEPHRA cluster tool for 200mm wafers, and Powder ALD coating systems for batteries, catalysts and composites. Its markets are semiconductors, energy storage, defense and aerospace, AI hardware and quantum devices. Forge Nano is a hardware and advanced-materials company: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: General Matter
providers.description: General Matter is a domestic nuclear-fuel company founded in 2024 and based in California, building United States uranium enrichment capacity to produce low-enriched uranium (LEU) and high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) for advanced commercial and government nuclear reactors. Co-founded by Scott Nolan and Lee Robinson and backed by Founders Fund, the company was awarded a $900M Department of Energy IDIQ contract and plans a $1.5B commercial enrichment facility at the former Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant in Kentucky, plus a lease on the Hanford Fuels and Materials Examination Facility in Washington. Its mission is to reduce American reliance on foreign nuclear fuel and strengthen energy independence. General Matter is an industrial energy manufacturer with no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, website properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Heron Power
providers.description: Heron Power is an industrial power-electronics company modernizing the electrical grid with solid-state transformers and integrated power conversion systems. Founded by former Tesla executive Drew Baglino, the company builds Heron Link products that combine a solid-state transformer with a power supply or inverter for two markets: data centers (AI and hyperscale power delivery, including 800 VDC datacenter architectures) and solar-and-storage renewable energy systems. Heron Power targets the grid infrastructure bottlenecks of the clean-energy transition, replacing century-old passive transformer technology with dense, controllable, software-defined power hardware. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Breakthrough Energy. Heron Power is a hardware and infrastructure company and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company intelligence.

providers.name: HyperStrong
providers.description: HyperStrong (Beijing HyperStrong Technology Co., Ltd. / 北京海博思创科技股份有限公司, SSE: 688411) is a leading Chinese provider of battery energy storage systems (BESS) and integrated energy solutions. Founded in 2011 and headquartered in Beijing, the company designs and manufactures modular liquid-cooled storage systems (HyperBlock and HyperCube series), integrated solar-plus-storage and charging-storage units, and the core control stack of battery management systems (BMS), energy management systems (EMS), and power conversion systems (PCS), alongside its HyperCloud AI cloud platform for fleet monitoring and optimization. HyperStrong serves generation-side, grid-side, and user-side (commercial, industrial, and residential) storage markets, ranking among the top domestic and global players by cumulative installed capacity with 60+ GWh deployed across 400+ projects. It is backed by IDG Capital and Qiming Venture Partners. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; HyperStrong is a hardware and energy-platform company and does not publish a public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Indian Energy Exchange
providers.description: Indian Energy Exchange (IEX) is India's largest electricity trading platform, operating a nationwide automated exchange for the physical delivery of electricity, renewable energy, and certificates. IEX runs Day-Ahead, Real-Time, Term-Ahead, Renewable Energy Certificate and Energy Saving Certificate market segments, matching buy and sell bids across a member network of distribution utilities, industrial and commercial consumers, and power generators. For members with sophisticated trading needs IEX offers a members-only trading API (currently for the iDAM and RTM segments) supporting order placement, trade-data retrieval and real-time monitoring for automated and high-frequency trading; access is provisioned to registered members rather than published as a public developer portal. Surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Inertia
providers.description: Inertia is a commercial fusion energy company pursuing laser-driven inertial confinement fusion to deliver safe, affordable, grid-scale clean power. Building on the December 2022 ignition milestone at the National Ignition Facility (NIF) in Livermore, Inertia is developing a modular laser system composed of roughly a thousand smaller, more efficient lasers, mass-manufacturing 4.5mm fusion fuel targets for under a dollar each, and firing them ten times per second to power a 1.5 gigawatt baseload, dispatchable power plant. The company is a deep-tech venture tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; it operates a corporate/marketing web presence and publishes no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Kula Bio
providers.description: Kula Bio is an agricultural biotechnology company headquartered in Natick, Massachusetts that manufactures Kula-N, a nitrogen-fixing microbial biofertilizer built on the bacterium Xanthobacter autotrophicus. The company's process, originating in Dr. Dan Nocera's research, "supercharges" the microbe with renewable energy so it fixes atmospheric nitrogen at the root zone, letting growers replace a portion of synthetic nitrogen while cutting the greenhouse-gas footprint of the applied product. Kula Bio sells a liquid formulation and, since February 2026, a Soluble Powder (SP) line, serving produce and row-crop growers through agronomic distribution rather than through software. It raised a $50M Series A led by Lowercarbon Capital and was named to TIME's list of America's Top GreenTech Companies of 2026. Kula Bio publishes no developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind; this profile records that measured absence alongside its verified public corporate surface.

providers.name: LF Energy
providers.description: LF Energy is a Linux Foundation project building open source technology solutions for the power grid and energy sector. Launched in 2018, it accelerates the energy transition through open source collaboration and hosts projects for grid modernization, flexibility, and decarbonization.

providers.name: Marvel Fusion
providers.description: Marvel Fusion is a Munich-based deep-tech company founded in 2019 that is developing laser-based inertial confinement fusion energy. It combines a proprietary fast-ignition approach with innovations across lasers, fuel targets, and power-plant design to make commercial fusion power viable, building on the National Ignition Facility 2022 ignition breakthrough. The company operates in Germany and the United States, with a demonstration facility in Fort Collins, Colorado, and has raised over $400M from venture capital, industrial partners, and public funding. As a physics and energy-infrastructure company it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or MCP surface; this profile captures its corporate identity and web/domain security posture.

providers.name: Pelikan Mobility
providers.description: Pelikan Mobility is a Paris-based smart-leasing and fleet-management company for electric commercial vehicles, founded in late 2022 by David Salfati and Vincent Schachter. It operates two products: Pelikan Lease, a very-long-term leasing offer (up to 10 years / 300,000 km) for electric utility vans that targets a 20% lower total cost of ownership, and Pelikan FleetPilot, a SaaS platform using digital twins, optimization algorithms and generative AI to plan fleet renewal, electrification and vehicle redeployment across large B2B fleets in utilities, maintenance, construction and logistics. The company is backed by Seedcamp, Frst and PaleBlueDot Ventures. It publishes a marketing and resources website but exposes no public API or developer surface at this time; this profile records its identity and web-domain security posture.

providers.name: Plantible Foods
providers.description: Plantible Foods is a business-to-business food-ingredient company founded in 2018 by Dutch entrepreneurs Tony and Maurits, with its first commercial production facility in Schleicher County, Texas. The company cultivates lemna (duckweed) in controlled, automated aquafarms and uses a proprietary water-based extraction process to isolate RuBisCO, sold as Rubi Protein — roughly 85% protein by weight with a PDCAAS of 1.0 — alongside Lemna Leaf Greens and application-specific systems such as RubiWhisk and RubiPrime. It sells to food manufacturers and ingredient companies rather than consumers, and in February 2026 became the first company to receive an FDA "no questions" GRAS letter for isolated RuBisCO protein in food. Investors include RA Capital, Nourish Ventures, Chipotle, Kellogg's and CJ Group. Plantible is an agricultural manufacturing business: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind, and plantiblefoods.com is a Webflow marketing site with no developer surface.

providers.name: Proxima Fusion
providers.description: Proxima Fusion is a Munich-based fusion energy company building the first generation of commercial fusion power plants using quasi-isodynamic (QI) stellarators. Spun out of the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics, the company is developing Stellaris, a stellarator power plant concept, with milestones that include a Stellarator Model Coil and an Alpha demonstration stellarator on the path to grid-scale fusion energy. Proxima Fusion is a privately held deep-tech startup and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures its identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: rabot.energy
providers.description: rabot.energy (RABOT Energy DE GmbH) is a Hamburg-based German electricity supplier offering dynamic and fixed-rate power tariffs where consumers pay hourly rates that track the wholesale electricity market. The company provides 100% renewable energy certified by TÜV NORD, smart meter installation and management, EV charging optimization (Autostrom), and home battery storage (Rabot Flow), all managed through a consumer mobile app for consumption monitoring. It is a consumer-facing energy retailer; no public developer portal or API is currently published. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of HV Capital.

providers.name: Sunfire
providers.description: Sunfire SE is a German hydrogen technology manufacturer headquartered in Dresden, Saxony, with additional sites in Berlin and Solingen. Founded in 2010 by Carl Berninghausen, Christian von Olshausen and Nils Aldag, and converted to a European stock corporation (SE) in 2025, the company builds industrial-scale electrolyzers and power-to-X plants that convert renewable electricity into green hydrogen and synthetic fuels. Its Sunfire-HyLink portfolio spans pressurized alkaline electrolysis (HyLink Alkaline 22 at 10 MW and HyLink Alkaline 23 at 50 MW per module, operating at 30 bar(g)) and high-temperature solid oxide electrolysis (HyLink SOEC, 10 MW modules, a claimed world-record 37.5 kWh/kg H2 efficiency), alongside FEED engineering, project delivery, maintenance and remote data-driven monitoring services. Customers and projects include RWE, Salzgitter, Neste, TotalEnergies, BASF, P2X Solutions, Nordic Ren-Gas and the Bad Lauchstaedt Energy Park. Sunfire is an industrial equipment manufacturer: it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Suplari
providers.description: Suplari is an enterprise procurement intelligence platform that goes beyond spend analytics, using AI to clean, classify, and unify fragmented spend data across ERP, P2P, and spreadsheet sources. It delivers spend analytics, value orchestration, savings tracking, contract intelligence, and ESG intelligence, alongside procurement-specific AI agents (Suplari Worker, Assistant, and AI Studio) that integrate with SAP, Oracle, Workday, Coupa, Databricks, Snowflake, and Microsoft. Suplari was acquired by Microsoft in 2021. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Vartega
providers.description: Vartega is a Denver, Colorado-based advanced materials company that produces recycled carbon fiber (rCF) from post-industrial scrap as a sustainable, lower-cost drop-in alternative to virgin carbon fiber. Its product line includes EasyFeed Bundles for thermoplastic compounding, chopped carbon fiber in multiple lengths and sizings, and carbon fiber reinforced polypropylene and nylon pellets. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; enrichment probing found no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface.

providers.name: Vattenfall
providers.description: Vattenfall is a leading European energy company focused on delivering sustainable, carbon‑free electricity and heat. Operating in multiple countries, it invests in renewable generation, energy storage, and digital solutions to accelerate the transition to fossil‑free energy. The company emphasizes innovation, customer‑centric services, and a commitment to climate goals, positioning itself as a major player in the European utilities sector.

providers.name: Whisper Aero
providers.description: Whisper Aero is a Crossville, Tennessee based aerospace company developing ultra-quiet electric ducted-fan propulsion that converts electricity into thrust with roughly 20 percent more efficiency and 20 dB less noise than conventional systems, scaling from 5 to 500 pounds of thrust and 40 to 400 knots for aviation, defense, and commercial applications. Backed by Kindred Ventures, Lux Capital, and Menlo Ventures. The company is a hardware manufacturer and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Wunder
providers.description: Wunder (formerly Wunder Capital, wewunder.com, now wunderpower.com) is a commercial clean-energy company that deploys solar, battery storage, and EV charging infrastructure across real estate portfolios with no-CapEx energy solutions, managing projects from design through operations in 40+ US states. Backed by Techstars and a $650M partnership with Blackstone, Wunder runs its project development on Astra, a proprietary internal platform for energy data analysis, forecasting, and automation. Wunder publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: BlueLayer
providers.description: BlueLayer is an operating-system platform for carbon-project developers, providing infrastructure to collect project data, run automated digital measurement, reporting and verification (dMRV), manage the carbon-credit lifecycle from estimation through retirement, and generate revenue by distributing and selling credits while reducing compliance burden. The product spans project operations, a revenue engine, credit management, a stakeholder DataHub, customizable dashboards, and integrations with registries, CRMs, accounting software, and ERPs. Backed by Point Nine, BlueLayer was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; as of this enrichment pass no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface was found — the platform is accessed via its hosted web application.

providers.name: Cfgi
providers.description: CFGI (Corporate Finance Group International) is a global advisory firm providing finance, accounting, tax, risk, and technology services to corporations, private equity firms, and investors. With over 25 years of experience, CFGI offers private capital solutions, technical accounting, cybersecurity, ESG advisory, and strategic transaction support across multiple industries worldwide.

providers.name: Niv-AI
providers.description: Niv-AI provides AI‑driven energy management solutions that monitor and orchestrate data‑center power usage in real time. By analyzing the electrical fingerprint of GPU workloads, Niv‑AI maximizes existing capacity, reduces over‑provisioning, and turns stranded power into tradable tokens. The platform combines high‑resolution sensor data with advanced software orchestration to deliver visibility, efficiency, and cost savings for modern AI compute facilities.

providers.name: SATIM
providers.description: SATIM provides AI-powered analysis of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) operations. Its OREC analytics engine performs automated object detection and classification on satellite and airborne SAR data (accuracy up to 95%), deployable in cloud, edge, or air-gapped environments and integrable into C2 and C4ISR workflows. OREC-Intelligence adds persistent monitoring with real-time area-of-interest change alerts and activity pattern analysis. Headquartered in Krakow, Poland, with offices in Dover, Delaware and London. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company; no public API surface, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation are published at this time.

providers.name: Zanskar
providers.description: Zanskar (Zanskar Geothermal & Minerals, Inc.) is a Salt Lake City-based geothermal energy company founded in 2021 by Carl Hoiland and Joel Edwards. It uses custom artificial intelligence, machine learning, and subsurface geoscience to discover and develop conventional geothermal resources, with a mission to make geothermal the most affordable form of widely-deployable, 24/7 carbon-free power. The company raised a $115M Series C and is backed by Obvious Ventures and Union Square Ventures. Zanskar publishes public geothermal datasets on the Snowflake Marketplace; it does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Atmo AI
providers.description: Atmo AI provides ultra‑precise AI‑driven weather forecasting for micro‑climates, leveraging real‑time satellite, radar, buoy and ground‑station data. Its deep‑learning models deliver forecasts up to 40,000× faster than traditional methods, achieving up to 50% higher accuracy across nowcasting to 14‑day horizons. Trusted by governments, militaries and industries worldwide, Atmo AI serves sectors such as aerospace, defense, agriculture and disaster response.

providers.name: CohnReznick
providers.description: CohnReznick is a top-25 US accounting, tax, and advisory firm formed in 2012 by the merger of J.H. Cohn LLP and Reznick Group, P.C. The firm serves clients across more than 30 industries from offices throughout the United States and four offshore subsidiaries, with its global reach extended through membership in the Nexia International network (operating in more than 128 countries). In May 2024 CohnReznick became the first US accounting firm of its scale to receive a strategic growth investment from a private equity sponsor when funds advised by Apax Partners acquired a majority stake. As part of that transaction the firm operates under an alternative-practice structure: audit and attest services are delivered by CohnReznick LLP (a licensed CPA firm) while tax and advisory services are delivered through CohnReznick Advisory LLC. Largest practice areas include Real Estate, Renewable Energy, Government Contracting, Asset Management (private equity, hedge funds, private credit, REITs), Financial Services, Healthcare, Life Sciences, Consumer & Industrial, Technology & Media, Public Sector, and Private Clients (family offices, high net worth individuals, professional sports). CohnReznick does not publish a public software developer API; this repository documents the firm's organizational profile, practice taxonomy, and linked-data context for API catalog purposes.

providers.name: Nanotech Energy
providers.description: Nanotech Energy is an advanced materials manufacturer that develops and produces graphene-based super materials and the energy-storage products built from them. Its catalog spans graphene powders, graphene oxide pastes, dispersions, conductive inks and conductive adhesives, silver nanowires, and non-flammable lithium-ion battery cells and packs aimed at home and grid energy storage, marine, household and electric-vehicle applications. The company also offers customer-facing testing, analysis and product development services to help customers scale a graphene formulation from concept to full production. It is a physical-goods manufacturer: it publishes a marketing and product website but no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: 45-8 ENERGY
providers.description: 45-8 ENERGY is a French exploration and production company, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Metz with offices in Lyon, dedicated to helium and natural (native) hydrogen in Europe. It is the first company in France and Western Europe specialised in the exploration and production of these two low-carbon subsurface gases, covering the full value chain from geoscientific exploration through production, distribution and recycling. In 2024 it delivered the first helium produced on Western European soil, and it operates RECYCL'He, Europe's first mobile helium recovery and recycling unit. Its exploration and production portfolio spans France (Fonts-Bouillants, Avant-Monts, Marensin, Beauvoir), Germany (Guhlen, Brimir), the Balkans and the United States (Humboldt, Fayette). In April 2026 Ad Terra took a majority stake in the company. 45-8 ENERGY is a physical-resources operator and publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable data surface.

providers.name: BlueNalu
providers.description: BlueNalu, Inc. is a San Diego, California cellular aquaculture company founded in 2017 by Lou Cooperhouse, Chris Somogyi and Chris Dammann that produces cell-cultivated seafood — real seafood grown directly from fish cells rather than harvested from the ocean. Its lead product is cell-cultivated bluefin tuna toro, marketed as "Seafood Without Compromise", targeted first at premium foodservice operators in the United States and then internationally. The company has raised approximately $84 million to date, including a Series B and a December 2025 insider-led convertible note and preferred stock financing led by Agronomics, Siddhi Capital and Lewis & Clark AgriFood, and was the first cell-cultivated seafood company admitted to the National Fisheries Institute. BlueNalu is a food and biotechnology producer; it publishes a marketing website and no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Brambles
providers.description: Brambles Limited (ABN 89 118 896 021, ASX-listed) is a pooling solutions company specialising in the provision of reusable pallets, crates and containers and associated logistics services through its CHEP and IFCO brands, with a digital supply-chain arm (BXB Digital). Its corporate site at brambles.com publishes investor, sustainability, governance and news content; no public developer portal, API documentation or API reference was found on the Brambles site or the BXB Digital page it links to (checked 2026-10-21).

providers.name: Carbon Capture
providers.description: Carbon Capture Inc. provides direct air capture (DAC) technology to remove CO₂ from the atmosphere and store it underground. Founded in 2022, the company offers modular, scalable DAC systems, sells carbon removal credits, and operates large‑scale projects such as the multi‑megaton Project Bison in Wyoming. It aims to accelerate the transition to net‑zero by delivering cost‑effective carbon removal solutions for industrial and corporate customers.

providers.name: CF Industries Holdings
providers.description: CF Industries Holdings is a Fortune 500 American manufacturer and distributor of nitrogen-based fertilizers (ammonia, urea, ammonium nitrate, UAN) and clean-energy products serving agricultural and industrial customers worldwide. CF operates one of the largest global ammonia production networks and is scaling clean (blue and green) ammonia for low-carbon energy. CF does not publish a public developer API program; programmatic data access is limited to investor-relations SEC filings feeds, press/news RSS, and partner EDI/B2B integrations with agricultural distributors, rail, terminal, and industrial customers.

providers.name: Chestnutcarbon
providers.description: Chestnutcarbon is a U.S.-based nature‑based carbon removal company that develops, finances, and operates forest‑based carbon offset projects. It focuses on afforestation, improved forest management, and nature‑works initiatives, delivering high‑quality carbon credits to corporate clients and investors. The firm emphasizes transparency, community benefits, and biodiversity, managing over 90,000 acres of land and supporting sustainable land restoration across the United States.

providers.name: Clariter
providers.description: Clariter is a global cleantech company producing sustainable petrochemicals upcycled from plastic waste. It offers high‑quality alternatives to fossil‑based products for thousands of industrial and consumer applications, helping create circularity and reduce carbon waste. The company’s proprietary technology turns plastic waste into profitable, sustainable solutions, addressing the global plastic waste epidemic.

providers.name: Clariterrecyclingandrefiningcenter
providers.description: Clariter is a global cleantech company producing sustainable petrochemicals upcycled from plastic waste. It pioneers chemical recycling technology, offering high‑quality, food‑grade and industrial‑grade products, and operates worldwide with plants and partnerships to create circular economies.

providers.name: DePoly
providers.description: DePoly’s novel and patented technology breaks down PET back to monomers, enabling the production of recycled PET and fostering a sustainable circular economy for plastics. Over 90% of plastics worldwide are not recycled; DePoly aims to change this by providing a clean, scalable solution that transforms waste into valuable raw material, supporting industries in adopting circular practices and reducing reliance on virgin fossil resources.

providers.name: Electra
providers.description: Electra (legal name Electrasteel, Inc.) is a Boulder, Colorado clean-industrial company founded in 2020 that is reinventing ironmaking. Instead of smelting iron ore with fossil fuels in a blast furnace, Electra uses an electrochemical process — an acidic leach plus electrowinning driven by renewable electricity — to dissolve a broad range of iron ores, including low-grade and previously uncommercialized ores, and plate out 99% pure iron at roughly 60°C while recovering high-value co-minerals and emitting oxygen. The modular design lets units be added as building blocks for rapid scaling and lets the process follow intermittent renewable power. Electra has raised over $200M from Rio Tinto, BHP Ventures, POSCO, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund, Capricorn and Lowercarbon Capital, runs a pilot plant in Boulder, and is building a demonstration plant in Colorado. It is an industrial manufacturer with no public developer program: as of this profile it publishes no API, developer portal, documentation, machine-readable specification, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Inertia
providers.description: Inertia is a commercial fusion energy company focused on delivering limitless, clean power through advanced laser-driven fusion technology. The company builds modular laser systems and mass‑produces fusion fuel targets to operate gigawatt‑scale power plants, aiming to provide safe, affordable energy for millions of homes worldwide. Inertia’s leadership includes seasoned entrepreneurs and scientists driving the transition from experimental ignition to commercial energy generation.

providers.name: LanzaJet
providers.description: LanzaJet is a sustainable fuels technology company, headquartered at 520 Lake Cook Road, Deerfield, Illinois, that produces and licenses sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and renewable diesel. Founded in 2020 as a spin-out of LanzaTech with Suncor and Mitsui, and later backed by Shell, British Airways, Southwest Airlines, Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund, Breakthrough Energy, Groupe ADP, MUFG and All Nippon Airways, the company commercializes a patented Alcohol-to-Jet (ATJ) process that converts ethanol into synthetic paraffinic kerosene through a continuous catalytic reaction, reaching roughly 90% hydrocarbon selectivity to jet fuel and converting about 98% of the ethanol carbon into salable product. The ATJ pathway was approved by ASTM International in 2018. LanzaJet Freedom Pines Fuels in Soperton, Georgia — opened in 2024 — is the world's first commercial ethanol-to-jet SAF plant, producing roughly 10 million gallons of SAF and renewable diesel a year, and the company is developing Project Speedbird in the UK alongside a CirculAir joint solution with LanzaTech that widens the feedstock base to municipal solid waste, agricultural residues and industrial off-gases via gas fermentation. LanzaJet sells technology licenses, project development and engineering services and fuel offtake rather than software: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, no API reference, no SDKs, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind, and every /.well-known/ discovery probe against its web host returned 404.

providers.name: Liontown Ltd
providers.description: Liontown Ltd (formerly Liontown Resources Limited, ASX: LTR, ABN 39 118 153 825) is a Perth, Western Australia based, ASX-listed battery minerals company. It operates the Kathleen Valley lithium project, Australia's first underground lithium mine, and holds the Buldania and Centenario projects plus downstream expansion plans. Its corporate website publishes investor, ASX release, sustainability/ESG and careers information; no public developer API, documentation or developer portal was found on its own sites.

providers.name: Orora
providers.description: Orora (Orora Group Limited, ASX: ORA) is an Australian-listed packaging company that describes itself as the global leader in sustainable glass and aluminium packaging, partnering with major drinks brands. Its roughly 4,500-person team runs 17 sites across Australia, North America, Europe and the UAE, covering design, manufacturing and decoration of glass bottles and aluminium beverage cans. Orora does not publish a public developer portal or API; this profile was surfaced from the australia-apidays-2026 harvest.

providers.name: Schnitzer Steel Industries
providers.description: Schnitzer Steel Industries, now rebranded as Radius Recycling (acquired by Toyota Tsusho in 2025), is one of the largest manufacturers and exporters of recycled metal products in North America. The company processes scrap metal from automotive and industrial sources for use in steelmaking, operating 103 recycling facilities including the Pick-n-Pull auto parts chain and Cascade Steel Rolling Mills in McMinnville, Oregon. Schnitzer/Radius Recycling does not expose a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Assembly OSM
providers.description: Assembly OSM is a New York City off-site manufacturing company founded in 2019 by SHoP Architects co-founders Bill and Chris Sharples to industrialise the construction of high-rise urban housing. The company calls its method "post-modular": rather than trucking finished volumetric boxes from a single factory, Assembly designs a kit-of-parts chassis and distributes fabrication across a network of specialist suppliers — an aerospace and automotive supply-chain model applied to buildings — then stacks the resulting units on site, claiming delivery of market-competitive high-rise residential architecture in roughly 60% of conventional schedule. Its buildings are all-electric and passive-design led, targeting 55-70% energy-efficiency improvement and 35% less embodied carbon today, net-zero operational carbon by 2027 and climate-positive buildings by 2040. Completed and in-progress work includes Prototype Alpha, 147 St. Felix Street and 247 East 117th Street in New York, plus an AOSM Canada operation. The company has raised more than $60 million, including a $38 million Series A in 2022, and draws engineering staff from SpaceX, Tesla and Boeing. Assembly runs a digital-twin engineering platform — a heavily scripted CATIA environment carrying each module from design through fabrication to installation — but that platform is an internal manufacturing tool, not a product: Assembly OSM sells buildings, and publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Endless West
providers.description: Endless West is a Detroit-based molecular spirits manufacturer that applies food and molecular science to create alcoholic beverages without traditional distilling or aging. The company operates a TTB-approved production facility offering bulk base spirits and ready-to-bottle liquids, turnkey and private-label packaged brands, pre-made concentrates, and contract co-packing and bottling services for other brands and entrepreneurs. Its proprietary Glyph Molecular Spirit showcases a sustainability approach that reduces water usage and CO2 footprint versus conventional distillation. Endless West is a consumer-products and manufacturing company with no public developer API surface; this profile was surfaced as a Partech portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Simplifyber
providers.description: Simplifyber is a sustainable footwear and materials technology company that manufactures shoe uppers and other components using a proprietary fiber-molding process. By casting products directly from a liquid, cellulose-based material it eliminates the spinning, weaving, and knitting steps and much of the cutting and sewing of traditional shoemaking, which it says lowers the CO2 emissions of a shoe upper by roughly 33x versus conventional methods. Its flagship Moon Shoe was developed with the fashion brand Ganni. Simplifyber is a Techstars-backed startup. It operates as a consumer and industrial manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Terrascope
providers.description: Terrascope is a Singapore-headquartered climate-tech and sustainability software company building an enterprise carbon measurement, management, and decarbonization platform. Launched in 2022 after being incubated and spun out of Olam Group (a Temasek-linked Singapore agribusiness), and led by former Google and AWS executive Felipe Daguila, Terrascope serves large food, agriculture, retail, and manufacturing enterprises that need to quantify Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions across their operations, products, and supply chains. The platform centers on four core modules: Corporate Carbon Footprint (CCF) for organization-level inventories, Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) for product-level lifecycle emissions, Supplier Engagement for Scope 3 primary-data collection, and Climate Reporting for audit-ready disclosure. Terrascope's differentiator is its AI-assisted data ingestion layer (built on Amazon Bedrock) that reduces measurement cycles by roughly 80% versus manual baselines, intelligent emissions factor matching with FLAG (Forestry, Land, and Agriculture) breakdowns, data gap-filling claiming 92% accuracy versus supplier data, and a curated library of over 20,000 decarbonization best practices used to power what-if scenario modeling and ROI-ranked recommendations. The platform supports the GHG Protocol (including Land Sector and Removals guidance), SBTi FLAG, CDP (Terrascope is a CDP Gold Accredited software provider), TCFD, California SB253, and Australia's S2 climate disclosure regimes. Notable customers include Kellanova, Princes Group, iNova Pharmaceuticals, Mandai Wildlife Group, Olam Food Ingredients, Tetra Pak, Mitsubishi, Japan Tobacco, and Kagome. Investors include Olam Group and Plug and Play Tech Center. Terrascope is delivered as a closed enterprise SaaS — there is no publicly documented developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, or open-source release. The github.com/terrascope organization exists but has no public repositories, and docs.terrascope.com is not publicly resolvable. Integration with customer ERP, procurement, and energy systems is handled through bespoke implementation engagements rather than self-serve developer onboarding.

providers.name: AMP Robotics
providers.description: AMP Robotics designs, builds, and operates advanced facilities that process single‑stream recycling and municipal solid waste using artificial intelligence. It provides waste companies and municipalities with AI‑powered sortation services and automation at scale, offering cost‑competitive processing and increased diversion rates. The company’s AMP ONE facilities deploy Smart Sortation™ technology for capacities ranging from 10 K to over 1 M tons per year.

providers.name: Brilliant Light Power
providers.description: Brilliant Light Power is a privately held energy technology company founded by Dr. Randell L. Mills. It claims to develop a novel method of extracting usable energy from hydrogen atoms, termed the SunCell® technology, which it says can produce clean, non‑polluting power. The company provides detailed information about its theory, validation reports, and commercial applications on its website, including business, technology, and research sections. It positions itself as a potential source of primary energy beyond conventional fossil fuels.

providers.name: Chooose
providers.description: Chooose provides a purpose‑built software platform for scaling Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) programs. Their end‑to‑end solution helps aviation and freight companies plan, procure, report, and manage SAF initiatives, integrating tools for carbon accounting, supplier engagement, and regulatory compliance. The platform is used by industry leaders to accelerate SAF adoption and meet climate targets.

providers.name: Clrfacilityservicespvtltd
providers.description: CLR Facility Services Private Limited provides integrated facility management solutions across multiple industries including healthcare, aviation, manufacturing, and retail. Their services span IFM, technical services, business support, aviation services, production support, and sustainable impact initiatives such as circular economy and renewable energy. The company emphasizes ESG pledges, corporate governance, and smart building technologies, offering comprehensive facility management and consulting.

providers.name: Cmbluenergyag
providers.description: Cmblu Energy AG (CMBLU) is a global deep‑tech company developing SolidFlow batteries – a non‑lithium, water‑based, long‑duration energy storage solution. Their modular, scalable systems target utilities, grid operators, data centers and industrial customers, enabling reliable, cost‑effective power storage for renewable integration and backup. The company is headquartered in Germany and focuses on sustainable, safe battery technology for a decarbonized energy future.

providers.name: Corvusenergy
providers.description: Corvus Energy, founded in 2009, provides zero‑emission energy storage solutions for the maritime industry. The company designs, manufactures and deploys battery systems that power hybrid and fully electric vessels, aiming to reduce diesel consumption and CO₂ emissions worldwide. With over 1,300 installations and more than 50% market share in maritime zero‑emission solutions, Corvus Energy serves a global customer base across shipping, offshore, and ferry sectors, delivering innovative, reliable and sustainable power.

providers.name: De-Ice
providers.description: De-Ice Technologies is a Somerville, Massachusetts deep-tech aviation startup building a chemical-free aircraft de-icing system that replaces conventional glycol spray with electrically heated strips applied to aircraft surfaces, removing snow and ice prior to takeoff. The technology eliminates weather-related departure delays, cuts glycol spraying costs, and reduces CO₂ emissions from idling fuel burn and chemical production. Named to Time's Best Inventions of 2024, De-Ice counts Air Canada as its launch customer and is backed by Techstars. This is a physical-hardware aviation company and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Geoscience Australia
providers.description: Geoscience Australia is the national agency delivering geoscientific knowledge and data to support decision‑making, research, and public understanding. It provides authoritative information on Australia’s geology, natural resources, hazards, and environmental processes, offering open data, maps, and tools for scientists, industry, and the community.

providers.name: Ilmateenistus
providers.description: Keskkonnaagentuur tagab ilmainfo ja turvatunde ning on teie jaoks olemas. Meilt saad ilmaprognoosi, vaatlusandmed 108-st seirejaamast üle Eesti. Meie ilmaradarid aitavad jälgida sajupilvede liikumist.

providers.name: InRisk
providers.description: InRisk provides parametric insurance solutions leveraging advanced data and technology to help governments, development agencies, insurers, and intermediaries manage climate and disaster risk. Their platform offers tailored products for crops, livestock, energy, infrastructure and more, delivering rapid, transparent payouts based on objective weather data. InRisk aims to redefine risk financing through proactive, data‑driven methodologies, supporting a wide range of stakeholders in building resilient economies.

providers.name: Optivolt Labs
providers.description: Optivolt Labs builds advanced battery management and IoT solutions for renewable energy storage, offering a cloud‑based platform that monitors, controls, and optimizes battery performance for commercial and industrial applications. Backed by Techstars, the company focuses on sustainability, reliability, and real‑time analytics to help clients maximize energy efficiency and extend battery life.

providers.name: Wunder
providers.description: Wunder is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: vc-portfolio; backed by techstars) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Apheabio
providers.description: Apheabio (Aphea.Bio) develops innovative biocontrol and biostimulant products for sustainable agriculture. Leveraging its APEXbio™ R&D platform, the company creates microbial‑based solutions that integrate with conventional and organic crop protection, aiming to improve yields, resilience, and environmental outcomes across the agricultural sector.

providers.name: Boston Metal
providers.description: Boston Metal is an industrial metals and materials company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Woburn, Massachusetts, with a wholly owned subsidiary and commercial plant in Brazil. The company commercializes Molten Oxide Electrolysis (MOE), a one-step electrochemical process that uses clean electricity rather than fossil fuels to reduce iron ore into liquid metal, producing steel with no direct CO2 emissions, and to recover high-value critical metals such as niobium and tantalum from low-grade ore and mining waste. Boston Metal commissioned a multi-inert-anode industrial MOE cell at its Woburn facility and has raised over $500 million from investors including Tata Steel. Boston Metal is a physical process-technology and manufacturing company; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI definition, developer portal, or machine-readable contract of any kind. This profile captures its public web, corporate, and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Earth AI
providers.description: Earth AI is a vertically integrated, AI-powered mineral exploration company that discovers, develops, and owns critical mineral mines for the emerging hardware economy — data centers, humanoid robots, eVTOL aircraft, fusion energy, space, and defense. Its proprietary predictive model, MTP, is trained on roughly 400 million geological sites to identify the source rocks of new mineral deposits and dramatically compress traditional exploration timelines. The company vertically integrates the search for critical minerals: it predicts targets with AI, acquires mineral rights, and drills to prove and own the resource. Earth AI is backed by DCVC and has been profiled by TechCrunch, Business Insider, and The Generalist's Future 50. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Earth AI does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Sylvera
providers.description: Sylvera is a London-headquartered carbon data and climate intelligence platform — often described as the "Moody's for the voluntary carbon market" — providing independent ratings, market data, and geospatial analytics that help corporate buyers, investors, project developers, governments, and standards bodies make informed decisions across carbon and commodities markets. Founded in 2020 by Allister Furey and Samuel Gill, Sylvera combines remote sensing, machine learning over satellite imagery and LiDAR-derived biomass data, and on-the-ground project assessment to produce letter-graded ratings (e.g., AA, A, B) for carbon credit projects across nature-based (REDD+, ARR, IFM), engineered removals, renewable energy, and cookstove methodologies. The platform's product surface spans Ratings, Market Intelligence (supply, demand, and pricing signals), an Article 6 & CORSIA Hub for compliance risk, a Market Gateway to roughly 400 million tonnes of project inventory, Earth Analytics and a Biomass Atlas for geospatial MRV, and Commodity Insights covering CORSIA, LCFS, CFR, and FuelEU Maritime mechanism eligibility and carbon intensity assessments. Sylvera distributes its data through a web platform, downloadable reports, and a gated Carbon Credit Analytics API (base URL https://api.sylvera.com/v1, JSON API style, API-key auth) used to syndicate ratings and pricing into ESG and sustainability reporting tools such as Workiva, Persefoni, and Watershed. Commercial packaging runs Freemium, Essentials, and Enterprise tiers, with Accelerated Ratings, Market Forecasts, and Geospatial add-ons all sold via contact-sales; there is no public OpenAPI specification, no published SDK, and no Sylvera GitHub organization — the API and full ratings catalog are available only to authenticated enterprise customers.

providers.name: Aerospacelab
